source: Written 2026-10-17 by Claude Sonnet and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin. Hand-written fixture questions are "approved".

notes.NC26.3.ANR.7: Area models and number lines are always described in words, never pictured. Denominators are only 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8. A few difficulty-3 questions use equivalent fractions between related denominators (2, 4, 8 and 3, 6) to compare or order, e.g. 3/8 against 1/2; no unlike-denominator comparison beyond those. Some numeric fraction answers have an equivalent form (4/8 = 1/2), which the checker accepts.
notes.NC26.3.SGMR.1: Text only: shapes, lines and angles are described by their features (sides, parallel and perpendicular sides, square corners) and by familiar objects. No degrees or protractors (grade 4), no rays. Where a shape name could also fit a square (square is a rectangle, a rhombus), the other options are chosen so that only one answer is defensible; a trapezoid is always described as having exactly one pair of parallel sides.
notes.NC26.3.SGMR.2: Text only: rulers and clocks are described in words (where the ends or the hands are), never pictured. Time questions stay within one hour of elapsed time (a few two-part ones total at most 60 minutes) and answers that are clock times are choice questions; numeric ones ask for the minutes. Customary units used are inches, feet, yards, miles, cups, gallons, ounces and pounds; no conversions between units (a grade 4 skill). A few questions use half inches (mixed-number answers) and rounding to the nearest 10 for estimates.
notes.NC26.3.SGMR.3: Whole-number side lengths only. Shapes that are not rectangles are described by their measurements in words (an L-shaped hall, a flag with a stripe), never by a picture. Subtracting a cut-out corner is avoided; composite areas are found by adding parts or by subtracting a stripe from a rectangle.
notes.NC26.3.RD.1: Every graph and table is written out in words (the scale, the bar ends, the key), never shown as a picture. Tally marks are described as full groups of five plus single marks. Predictions are limited to simple, steady patterns and to which category will probably stay popular.
notes.NC26.3.ANR.1: Words, numbers and contexts stay within 10,000. Mentally adding multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000 covers addition only, as the summary says.
notes.NC26.3.ANR.2: All numbers and answers stay within 1,000 (one use of 1,000 as the top of a count). Problems are one-step, as the summary says; a few add three numbers.
notes.NC26.3.ANR.3: 90 questions spread over 7 skills. Products of two single-digit factors stay within 90; multiples-of-10 products reach 720 (e.g. 9 x 80). Division appears only as 'find the missing factor' in equal-groups stories.
notes.NC26.3.ANR.4: Dividends stay within 100, with divisors and quotients up to 10. Every question is text only. Contexts are equal groups, sharing, arrays, equations with an unknown and strategies; no remainders are used.
notes.NC26.3.ANR.5: 90 questions spread over 7 skills. The facts stay within 10 x 10 and the matching divisions; bare-fact questions avoid 7 x 8 and 8 x 7 (already in the bank). Some d3 questions combine two facts or compare expressions.
notes.NC26.3.ANR.6: Only addition, subtraction and multiplication (products within about 100, sums and differences within 1000), as the summary names. Every estimation question names the place to round to, so each has one key. The choice-the-equation questions use a letter for the unknown or an expression, which the key matches by text (no compute).

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: What is the value of the digit 7 in $4{,}732$?
questions.solution: In $4{,}732$ the 7 is in the hundreds place, so it means 7 hundreds. 7 hundreds is 700.

solve.work: 4,732: 4 thousands, 7 hundreds, 3 tens, 2 ones. The 7 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 700.

questions.skill: Build a number from its places
questions.stem: A number has 6 thousands, 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 9 ones. Write the number.
questions.solution: 6 thousands is 6,000. 3 hundreds is 300. 4 tens is 40. 9 ones is 9. Put them together: $6{,}000 + 300 + 40 + 9 = 6{,}349$.

questions.skill: Compare four numbers
questions.stem: Which number is the greatest?
questions.solution: All four numbers have 3 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 9, 9, 8 and 0. The two with 9 hundreds are 3,908 and 3,980. Compare their tens: 0 tens is less than 8 tens. So 3,980 is the greatest.

solve.work: All have 3 thousands. Compare hundreds: 8, 9, 9, 0. 3,980 vs 3,908: tens 8 > 0, so 3,980 is greatest.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: A number is $2{,}916$. What is the value of the 9?
questions.solution: The 9 is in the hundreds place, so it means 9 hundreds. 9 hundreds is 900.

solve.work: 2,916: thousands 2, hundreds 9, tens 1, ones 6. The 9 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 9 x 100 = 900.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: Maya writes the number $6{,}340$. Which choice tells the value of the digit 6?
questions.solution: The 6 is in the thousands place, so it means 6 thousands, which is 6,000. The choice 600 would be the hundreds place and 60 the tens place.

solve.work: 6,340: the 6 is in the thousands place, so its value is 6 x 1,000 = 6,000.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: In $9{,}125$, the 2 is in the tens place. What is the value of the 2?
questions.solution: The 2 is in the tens place, so it means 2 tens. 2 tens is 20.

solve.work: 9,125: thousands 9, hundreds 1, tens 2, ones 5. The stem correctly says the 2 is in the tens place; value 2 x 10 = 20.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: In $3{,}052$, the digit 5 stands for which value?
questions.solution: Read the places from the right: ones 2, tens 5, hundreds 0, thousands 3. The 5 is in the tens place, so it stands for 5 tens, or 50.

solve.work: 3,052: thousands 3, hundreds 0, tens 5, ones 2. The 5 is in the tens place: 50.

questions.skill: Write a number from its places
questions.stem: Write the number with 2 thousands, 8 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones.
questions.solution: 2 thousands is 2,000, 8 hundreds is 800, 0 tens is 0 and 6 ones is 6. Together: 2,806.

questions.skill: Write a number from its places
questions.stem: Sofia has 5 bundles of $1{,}000$ sticks, 3 bundles of 100 sticks and 4 single sticks. How many sticks does she have?
questions.solution: 5 bundles of 1,000 is 5,000. 3 bundles of 100 is 300. Then 4 single sticks. There are no tens. $5{,}000 + 300 + 4 = 5{,}304$.

questions.skill: Write a number from its places
questions.stem: A number is made of 4 thousands and 7 ones, with no hundreds and no tens. What is the number?
questions.solution: 4 thousands is 4,000 and 7 ones is 7. The hundreds and tens places hold zeros, so the number is 4,007.

questions.skill: Write a number from its places
questions.stem: Which number has 9 in the thousands place, 1 in the hundreds place, 6 in the tens place and 0 in the ones place?
questions.solution: Write the digits in order from the thousands place to the ones place: 9, 1, 6, 0. The number is 9,160.

questions.skill: Expanded form
questions.stem: Which choice is $3{,}425$ in expanded form?
questions.solution: 3,425 has 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 2 tens and 5 ones. In expanded form that is $3{,}000 + 400 + 20 + 5$.

questions.skill: Expanded form
questions.stem: $4{,}567 = 4{,}000 + ? + 60 + 7$. What number does the ? stand for?
questions.solution: The 5 in 4,567 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 500. The missing part is 500.

questions.skill: Expanded form
questions.stem: Which number is the same as $5{,}000 + 90 + 1$?
questions.solution: 5,000 is 5 thousands, 90 is 9 tens and 1 is 1 one. There are no hundreds. The number is 5,091.

questions.skill: Expanded form
questions.stem: Leo writes a number in expanded form as $7{,}000 + 200 + 40 + 3$. What number is it?
questions.solution: 7 thousands, 2 hundreds, 4 tens and 3 ones make 7,243.

questions.skill: Number words and standard form
questions.stem: Write "two thousand, five hundred sixty-three" as a number.
questions.solution: Two thousand is 2,000. Five hundred is 500. Sixty-three is 63. Together: 2,563.

solve.work: two thousand = 2,000; five hundred = 500; sixty-three = 63. Total 2,563.

questions.skill: Number words and standard form
questions.stem: Which choice is $3{,}800$ written in words?
questions.solution: 3,800 is 3 thousands and 8 hundreds, so it is "three thousand, eight hundred". "Three thousand, eighty" is 3,080, "thirty-eight" is 38 and "three hundred eight" is 308.

solve.work: 3,800 = 3 thousands and 8 hundreds: 'three thousand, eight hundred'. Others are 3,080, 308, 38.

questions.skill: Number words and standard form
questions.stem: A sign says that a stadium has "six thousand, four hundred" seats. How many seats is that? Write the number.
questions.solution: Six thousand is 6,000 and four hundred is 400. The stadium has 6,400 seats.

questions.skill: Number words and standard form
questions.stem: Which number is "nine thousand, one hundred twenty"?
questions.solution: Nine thousand is 9,000. One hundred twenty is 120. Together: 9,120.

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup place values
questions.stem: $1{,}000$ is the same as how many hundreds?
questions.solution: Ten hundreds make one thousand: $10 \times 100 = 1{,}000$. So 1,000 is 10 hundreds.

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup place values
questions.stem: 5 hundreds is the same as how many tens?
questions.solution: 1 hundred is 10 tens. So 5 hundreds is $5 \times 10 = 50$ tens.

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup place values
questions.stem: Which is the same as 3 thousands?
questions.solution: 1 thousand is 10 hundreds, so 3 thousands is 30 hundreds. Both 30 tens and 300 ones are only 300.

solve.work: 3 thousands = 3,000. 300 ones = 300; 3 hundreds = 300; 30 hundreds = 3,000; 30 tens = 300. Answer 30 hundreds.

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup place values
questions.stem: 2 thousands and 3 hundreds is the same as how many hundreds?
questions.solution: 2 thousands is 20 hundreds. Add the 3 hundreds: $20 + 3 = 23$ hundreds.

questions.skill: Mentally add multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.solution: 5 thousands plus 2 thousands is 7 thousands: 7,000.

questions.skill: Mentally add multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: Pedro has 340 stamps. He gets 20 more. How many stamps does he have now?
questions.solution: 20 is 2 tens. Add 2 tens to the 4 tens in 340: 6 tens. The answer is 360.

questions.skill: Mentally add multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: A box holds $1{,}200$ beads. Anna adds 300 more beads. How many beads are in the box now?
questions.solution: 300 is 3 hundreds. 12 hundreds plus 3 hundreds is 15 hundreds: 1,500.

questions.skill: Mentally add multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.solution: 600 is 6 hundreds, so it goes in the hundreds place: 7 thousands and 6 hundreds is 7,600.

questions.skill: Compare two numbers
questions.stem: Which comparison of $5{,}019$ and $5{,}190$ is true?
questions.solution: Both numbers have 5 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 0 hundreds is less than 1 hundred. So 5,019 is less than 5,190.

solve.work: Same thousands (5). Hundreds: 0 in 5,019 vs 1 in 5,190, so 5,019 < 5,190.

questions.skill: Compare two numbers
questions.stem: Which is greater, $4{,}205$ or $4{,}052$? Write the greater number.
questions.solution: Both have 4 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 2 hundreds is more than 0 hundreds. So 4,205 is greater.

solve.work: Thousands equal (4). Hundreds: 2 vs 0, so 4,205 is greater.

questions.skill: Compare two numbers
questions.stem: A zoo counted its visitors: Monday $3{,}640$, Tuesday $3{,}604$, Wednesday $3{,}046$ and Thursday $3{,}460$. Which day had the most visitors?
questions.solution: All four numbers have 3 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 6, 6, 0 and 4. So Monday or Tuesday is greatest. Compare their tens: 4 tens is more than 0 tens. Monday (3,640) had the most visitors.

solve.work: All have 3 thousands. Hundreds: Mon 6, Tue 6, Wed 0, Thu 4. Mon vs Tue tens: 4 vs 0, so Monday 3,640 is the most.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Which list shows $2{,}340$, $4{,}120$ and $3{,}560$ from least to greatest?
questions.solution: Compare the thousands digits: 2, 4 and 3. From least to greatest: 2,340, then 3,560, then 4,120.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Which is the least of these numbers: $8{,}140$, $4{,}810$ and $1{,}480$? Write the least number.
questions.solution: The thousands digits are 8, 4 and 1. The least thousands digit is 1, so 1,480 is the least.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Which list shows $3{,}270$, $3{,}720$ and $3{,}072$ from greatest to least?
questions.solution: All have 3 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 2, 7 and 0. From greatest to least: 3,720, then 3,270, then 3,072.

questions.skill: Write a number in words
questions.stem: Which choice is the number $4{,}206$ written in words?
questions.solution: $4{,}206$ is 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones. That is "four thousand, two hundred six".

solve.work: 4,206 = 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, 0 tens, 6 ones = four thousand, two hundred six.

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup hundreds into thousands
questions.stem: A number is made of 3 thousands and 14 hundreds. What is the number?
questions.solution: 3 thousands is 3,000. 14 hundreds is 1,400. Together: $3{,}000 + 1{,}400 = 4{,}400$.

questions.skill: Mentally add a multiple of 100
questions.solution: 400 is 4 hundreds. Add 4 to the hundreds digit: 2 hundreds + 4 hundreds = 6 hundreds. The thousands, tens and ones stay the same, so the answer is 3,650.

solve.work: 3,250 + 400: add 4 hundreds to 2 hundreds = 6 hundreds, giving 3,650.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: A stadium has $6{,}418$ seats. What is the value of the digit 4 in the number of seats?
questions.solution: In 6,418 the 4 is in the hundreds place (6 thousands, 4 hundreds, 1 ten, 8 ones). Its value is 4 hundreds, or 400.

solve.work: 6,418: thousands 6, hundreds 4, tens 1, ones 8. The 4 is in the hundreds place: 400.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: In which number does the digit 5 have a value of 500?
questions.solution: A 5 worth 500 must be in the hundreds place. In 3,509 the hundreds digit is 5. In 5,039 the 5 is worth 5,000, in 2,350 it is worth 50, and in 4,005 it is worth 5.

solve.work: A 5 worth 500 must be in the hundreds place. 4,005: 5 ones. 3,509: 5 hundreds = 500. 5,039: 5 thousands. 2,350: 5 tens. Only 3,509.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: In $7{,}072$ the digit 7 appears twice. What is the value of the 7 on the left?
questions.solution: The left 7 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 7 thousands, or 7,000. (The other 7 is in the tens place and is worth 70.)

solve.work: 7,072: the left 7 is in the thousands place (the other is in the tens). Value 7,000.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: Which statement about the number $4{,}368$ is true?
questions.solution: In 4,368 the digits are 4 thousands, 3 hundreds, 6 tens and 8 ones. So the 3 is worth 300, the 6 is worth 60, the 4 is worth 4,000 and the 8 is worth 8. Only "The digit 3 is worth 300" is true.

solve.work: 4,368: 4 is worth 4,000; 3 is worth 300; 6 is worth 60; 8 is worth 8. Only 'The digit 3 is worth 300.' is true.

questions.skill: Write a number from its places
questions.stem: A toy store packs $1{,}000$ blocks in a crate, 100 blocks in a box and 10 blocks in a bag. A shipment has 6 crates, 0 boxes, 8 bags and 5 loose blocks. How many blocks is that in all?
questions.solution: 6 crates is 6,000 blocks. 0 boxes is 0 blocks. 8 bags is 80 blocks. Then 5 loose blocks. $6{,}000 + 0 + 80 + 5 = 6{,}085$.

questions.skill: Write a number from its places
questions.stem: Ana makes a number with digit cards. She puts the 6 in the tens place, the 2 in the thousands place, the 9 in the ones place and the 4 in the hundreds place. What number does she make?
questions.solution: Thousands 2, hundreds 4, tens 6, ones 9. Reading from the thousands place to the ones place gives 2,469.

questions.skill: Write a number from its places
questions.stem: Which number has 3 hundreds, 5 ones, 2 thousands and no tens?
questions.solution: Put each digit in its place: thousands 2, hundreds 3, tens 0, ones 5. The number is 2,305.

questions.skill: Expanded form
questions.stem: Which choice shows $9{,}070$ in expanded form?
questions.solution: 9,070 has 9 thousands, 0 hundreds, 7 tens and 0 ones. So it is $9{,}000 + 70$. A part that is zero is left out.

questions.skill: Expanded form
questions.stem: Mia wrote $50 + 8{,}000 + 6 + 700$. What number did she write?
questions.solution: Put each part in its place: 8,000 is 8 thousands, 700 is 7 hundreds, 50 is 5 tens and 6 is 6 ones. The number is 8,756.

questions.skill: Expanded form
questions.stem: Which choice does NOT equal $6{,}205$?

questions.skill: Expanded form
questions.stem: What number is $3 \times 1{,}000 + 5 \times 100 + 2 \times 10 + 8 \times 1$?

questions.skill: Number words and standard form
questions.stem: Which choice shows $5{,}047$ in words?
questions.solution: 5,047 is 5 thousands, 0 hundreds, 4 tens and 7 ones. In words: "five thousand, forty-seven".

questions.skill: Number words and standard form
questions.stem: A museum sign says, "Four thousand, three hundred eighteen people visited this year." How many people visited? Write the number.
questions.solution: Four thousand is 4,000, three hundred is 300 and eighteen is 18. The number is 4,318.

questions.skill: Number words and standard form
questions.stem: Which number is written in words as "eight thousand, six"?
questions.solution: "Eight thousand" is 8,000 and "six" is 6. There are no hundreds and no tens, so the number is 8,006.

questions.skill: Number words and standard form
questions.stem: In which choice do the words and the standard form name the same number?
questions.solution: "Four thousand, three hundred" is 4,300, so that pair matches. "Four thousand, thirty" is 4,030, "four hundred three" is 403, and "four thousand, three" is 4,003.

solve.work: four thousand, three = 4,003 (not 4,300). four hundred three = 403 (not 4,030). four thousand, thirty = 4,030 (not 4,300). four thousand, three hundred = 4,300: match.

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup place values
questions.stem: A number is made of 5 thousands and 12 tens. What is the number?
questions.solution: 5 thousands is 5,000. 12 tens is 120. Together: $5{,}000 + 120 = 5{,}120$.

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup place values
questions.stem: Which choice equals $4{,}500$?
questions.solution: 450 tens is $450 \times 10 = 4{,}500$. 45 tens is 450, "4 thousands and 5 tens" is 4,050, and "4 hundreds and 5 thousands" is 5,400.

solve.work: 45 tens = 450. 4 hundreds + 5 thousands = 5,400. 450 tens = 4,500. 4 thousands + 5 tens = 4,050. Only 450 tens.

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup place values
questions.stem: A warehouse stores $2{,}800$ pencils in bundles of 100 pencils. How many bundles is that?
questions.solution: Each bundle holds 100 pencils. $2{,}800 \div 100 = 28$, so there are 28 bundles. (28 hundreds make 2,800.)

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup place values
questions.stem: A number is made of 80 tens and 6 ones. What is the number?
questions.solution: 80 tens is $80 \times 10 = 800$. Add the 6 ones: $800 + 6 = 806$.

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup place values
questions.stem: Which choice is another way to write $6{,}430$?
questions.solution: 64 hundreds is 6,400, and 3 tens is 30, so together they are 6,430. The other choices are 6,700, 6,403 and 1,030.

questions.skill: Mentally add multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: A town has $4{,}560$ people. Then 200 more people move in. How many people live in the town now?
questions.solution: 200 is 2 hundreds. Add 2 to the 5 hundreds: 7 hundreds. The number is 4,760.

questions.skill: Mentally add multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.solution: Add the thousands: 2 thousands plus 5 thousands is 7 thousands. The rest of the number stays the same: 7,350.

questions.skill: Mentally add multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.solution: 50 is 5 tens. 4 tens plus 5 tens is 9 tens. The answer is 3,690.

questions.skill: Mentally add multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: Which number is $1{,}000$ more than $4{,}785$?
questions.solution: 1,000 more means one more thousand. The thousands digit goes from 4 to 5, and the other digits stay the same: 5,785.

questions.skill: Mentally add multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: A van carries 800 boxes and a truck carries $2{,}600$ boxes. How many boxes do the two carry in all?
questions.solution: 8 hundreds plus 26 hundreds is 34 hundreds, which is 3,400.

questions.skill: Compare two numbers
questions.stem: Which number is less than $7{,}205$?
questions.solution: All four numbers have 7 thousands. 7,205 has 2 hundreds. Only 7,025 has fewer hundreds (0), so it is less than 7,205.

solve.work: 7,205: hundreds 2. 7,502 and 7,520 have hundreds 5 (greater). 7,250: hundreds 2, tens 5 > 0 (greater). 7,025: hundreds 0 (less).

questions.skill: Compare two numbers
questions.stem: Which is less, $6{,}099$ or $6{,}100$? Write the lesser number.
questions.solution: Both have 6 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 0 hundreds is less than 1 hundred. So 6,099 is less than 6,100.

solve.work: 6,099 has hundreds 0; 6,100 has hundreds 1. 6,099 is less.

questions.skill: Compare two numbers
questions.stem: Each choice shows two numbers. In which choice is the first number greater than the second number?
questions.solution: Compare the digits from the left. 4,520 and 4,502 have the same thousands and hundreds; 2 tens is more than 0 tens, so 4,520 is greater. In each of the other pairs, the first number is the smaller one.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Four towns have these numbers of people: Ridge $5{,}480$, Dale $5{,}408$, Moss $5{,}840$ and Pine $5{,}048$. How many people live in the town with the second greatest number of people?
questions.solution: All have 5 thousands. Compare the hundreds: Ridge 4, Dale 4, Moss 8, Pine 0. Moss is greatest. Ridge and Dale both have 4 hundreds; Ridge has 8 tens and Dale has 0 tens, so Ridge is next. From greatest to least: 5,840; 5,480; 5,408; 5,048. The second greatest is 5,480.

solve.work: Order greatest to least: Moss 5,840; Ridge 5,480; Dale 5,408; Pine 5,048. Second greatest: 5,480.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Maya puts $7{,}014$, $7{,}401$, $7{,}140$ and $7{,}104$ in order from least to greatest. Which list is hers?
questions.solution: All have 7 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 0, 4, 1 and 1. So 7,014 is least and 7,401 is greatest. For 7,104 and 7,140, compare the tens: 0 tens is less than 4 tens. Order: 7,014; 7,104; 7,140; 7,401.

questions.skill: Order four numbers
questions.stem: Which list shows $6{,}058$, $6{,}508$, $6{,}085$ and $5{,}860$ in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: 5,860 has only 5 thousands, so it is the least. The other three have 6 thousands. Compare their hundreds: 0, 5 and 0. So 6,508 is the greatest. For 6,058 and 6,085, both have 0 hundreds; compare tens: 5 tens is less than 8 tens. Order: 5,860; 6,058; 6,085; 6,508.

questions.skill: Add thousands, hundreds and tens in steps
questions.stem: Start at $2{,}450$. Add 3 thousands, then add 5 hundreds, then add 4 tens. What number do you reach?

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: groups of ten in a number
questions.stem: How many groups of 10 are in $3{,}460$?
questions.solution: Every 10 ones make one ten. $3{,}460$ ones is the same as 346 tens, because $346 \times 10 = 3{,}460$.

solve.work: 3,460 = 346 tens (3,460 / 10 = 346). So there are 346 groups of 10.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: In $5{,}555$, the value of the 5 in the thousands place is how many times the value of the 5 in the hundreds place?
questions.solution: The 5 in the thousands place is worth 5,000. The 5 in the hundreds place is worth 500. Since $5{,}000 \div 500 = 10$, it is worth 10 times as much.

solve.issues: Minor: the 'ten times' relationship between places is usually a Grade 4 emphasis; acceptable as a place-value stretch item.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: Which number has a digit 4 whose value is ten times the value of the digit 4 in $1{,}043$?
questions.solution: In 1,043 the 4 is in the tens place and is worth 40. Ten times 40 is 400, so we need a 4 in the hundreds place. That is 2,401. In 4,012 the 4 is worth 4,000, in 1,340 it is worth 40, and in 1,204 it is worth 4.

solve.issues: Minor: 'ten times' relationship is more typically Grade 4; fine as a harder Grade 3 item.
solve.work: In 1,043 the 4 is in the tens place: 40. Ten times 40 = 400, so need 4 in the hundreds place. 4,012: 4,000. 2,401: 400. 1,204: 4. 1,340: 40. Answer 2,401.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: What is the sum of the values of the digits 2 and 8 in $2{,}480$?
questions.solution: The 2 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 2,000. The 8 is in the tens place, so it is worth 80. $2{,}000 + 80 = 2{,}080$.

solve.work: 2,480: the 2 is worth 2,000; the 8 is in the tens place, worth 80. 2,000 + 80 = 2,080.

questions.skill: Write a number from its places
questions.stem: A four-digit number has a ones digit of 5. Its tens digit is 3 more than its ones digit. Its hundreds digit is 0. Its thousands digit is 4 less than its ones digit. What is the number?
questions.solution: Ones digit: 5. Tens digit: $5 + 3 = 8$. Hundreds digit: 0. Thousands digit: $5 - 4 = 1$. The number is 1,085.

questions.skill: Write a number from its places
questions.stem: A four-digit number has 8 in the thousands place. Its hundreds digit is 5 less than its thousands digit. Its tens digit is double its hundreds digit. Its ones digit is 0. Which number is it?
questions.solution: Thousands digit: 8. Hundreds digit: $8 - 5 = 3$. Tens digit: $2 \times 3 = 6$. Ones digit: 0. The number is 8,360.

solve.work: Thousands 8. Hundreds 8 - 5 = 3. Tens 2 x 3 = 6. Ones 0. Number 8,360.

questions.skill: Write a number from its places
questions.stem: What is the smallest four-digit number you can make using each of the digits 4, 0, 9 and 2 exactly once?
questions.solution: To make the number small, put the smallest digits in the biggest places. But a four-digit number cannot start with 0, so the smallest digit that can go first is 2. Then use 0, 4 and 9 in order: 2,049.

solve.work: Digits 0, 2, 4, 9. The thousands digit cannot be 0 (it would not be four-digit), so use the smallest nonzero, 2, then the rest in increasing order: 0, 4, 9. Number 2,049.

questions.skill: Expanded form
questions.stem: Which choice shows $4{,}608$ in expanded form using multiplication?
questions.solution: 4,608 has 4 thousands, 6 hundreds, 0 tens and 8 ones. So it is $4 \times 1{,}000 + 6 \times 100 + 0 \times 10 + 8 \times 1$. The other choices put a digit in the wrong place.

questions.skill: Expanded form
questions.stem: Kim writes $3{,}000 + 14 \times 100 + 8$. What number is that?

questions.skill: Expanded form
questions.stem: A number is $6{,}000 + 300 + 20 + 8$. If the digit in the hundreds place and the digit in the tens place swap places, what is the new number?
questions.solution: The number is 6,328. Swap the 3 in the hundreds place with the 2 in the tens place: 6 thousands, 2 hundreds, 3 tens, 8 ones. The new number is 6,238.

solve.work: 6,000 + 300 + 20 + 8 = 6,328. Hundreds digit 3, tens digit 2; swap: hundreds 2, tens 3 -> 6,238.

questions.skill: Number words and standard form
questions.stem: In words, a number is "nine thousand, nine hundred ninety-nine". What number is one more than it?
questions.solution: "Nine thousand, nine hundred ninety-nine" is 9,999. One more than 9,999 is 10,000.

solve.work: nine thousand, nine hundred ninety-nine = 9,999. One more: 10,000.

questions.skill: Number words and standard form
questions.stem: Which choice does NOT name $4{,}120$?
questions.solution: 4,120 is "four thousand, one hundred twenty". Also 41 hundreds and 20 ones is $4{,}100 + 20 = 4{,}120$, and 412 tens is $412 \times 10 = 4{,}120$. But "four thousand, twelve" is 4,012.

solve.work: 412 tens = 4,120 (yes). Words 'four thousand, one hundred twenty' = 4,120 (yes). 41 hundreds + 20 ones = 4,100 + 20 = 4,120 (yes). 'four thousand, twelve' = 4,012 (no).

questions.skill: Number words and standard form
questions.stem: Write "six thousand, seventy-one" as a number.
questions.solution: Six thousand is 6,000 and seventy-one is 71. There are no hundreds, so the hundreds place holds a 0: 6,071.

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup place values
questions.stem: A store has $6{,}050$ stickers. They are wrapped in packs of 10 stickers. How many packs can be made?
questions.solution: Each pack holds 10 stickers. $6{,}050 \div 10 = 605$, so 605 packs can be made. (605 tens make 6,050.)

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup place values
questions.stem: Maria says that $3{,}400$ is the same as 34 hundreds. Tom says that it is the same as 340 tens. Who is right?
questions.solution: 34 hundreds is $34 \times 100 = 3{,}400$. 340 tens is $340 \times 10 = 3{,}400$. Both are right.

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup place values
questions.stem: Jon thinks of $5{,}306$ as 5 thousands, 3 hundreds and 6 ones. He trades 2 of the thousands for hundreds. Now the same number is 3 thousands, some hundreds and 6 ones. How many hundreds is that?
questions.solution: Each thousand is worth 10 hundreds, so 2 thousands is 20 hundreds. Add the 3 hundreds he already had: $20 + 3 = 23$ hundreds. (Now the number is 3 thousands, 23 hundreds and 6 ones, still 5,306.)

solve.work: Trading 2 thousands gives 20 hundreds; 3 + 20 = 23 hundreds. Check: 3,000 + 2,300 + 6 = 5,306.

questions.skill: Mentally add multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.solution: $6{,}950 + 50 = 7{,}000$, because 95 tens plus 5 tens is 100 tens. The other 20 is still to add: $7{,}000 + 20 = 7{,}020$.

questions.skill: Mentally add multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: Which sum equals $5{,}000$?
questions.solution: 46 hundreds plus 4 hundreds is 50 hundreds, which is 5,000. The other sums are 4,640, 4,460 and 4,900.

questions.skill: Mentally add multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: What number makes $3{,}200 + ? = 4{,}500$ true?
questions.solution: 3,200 is 32 hundreds and 4,500 is 45 hundreds. $45 - 32 = 13$, so the missing number is 13 hundreds, or 1,300. Check: $3{,}200 + 1{,}300 = 4{,}500$.

questions.skill: Compare two numbers
questions.stem: What is the greatest digit that can replace the ? so that $3{,}8?5 < 3{,}865$ is true?
questions.solution: The number 3,8?5 must be less than 3,865. The thousands and hundreds match, so the tens digit ? must be less than 6. The greatest digit less than 6 is 5. Check: 3,855 is less than 3,865.

solve.work: 3,8?5 vs 3,865: thousands and hundreds equal; the tens digit ? must be less than 6 (if ? = 6 the numbers are equal, not less). Greatest is 5: 3,855 < 3,865.

questions.skill: Compare two numbers
questions.stem: Which number is greater than $4{,}689$ and less than $4{,}701$?
questions.solution: The number must be between 4,689 and 4,701. 4,699 is greater than 4,689 and less than 4,701. 4,609 and 4,680 are less than 4,689, and 4,710 is more than 4,701.

solve.work: Need 4,689 < n < 4,701. 4,609 too small; 4,699 works; 4,710 too big; 4,680 too small.

questions.skill: Compare two numbers
questions.stem: Which comparison of numbers in expanded form is true?
questions.solution: $4{,}000 + 300 + 5 = 4{,}305$ and $4{,}000 + 30 + 50 = 4{,}080$, and 4,305 is greater. In the others, 6,020 is not less than 800, 2,090 is not greater than 2,900, and 8,008 is not less than 880.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Put these five numbers in order from least to greatest: $4{,}920$, $4{,}092$, $4{,}209$, $4{,}902$ and $4{,}029$. Which number is in the middle? Write it.
questions.solution: All have 4 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 9, 0, 2, 9 and 0. The two with 0 hundreds are 4,092 and 4,029 (4,029 is less). Then 4,209. Then the two with 9 hundreds: 4,902 and 4,920. Order: 4,029; 4,092; 4,209; 4,902; 4,920. The middle number is 4,209.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Which list shows the numbers 9,010; 9,001; 9,100 and 9,011 in order from greatest to least?
questions.solution: All have 9 thousands. 9,100 has 1 hundred, so it is greatest. The others have 0 hundreds; compare the tens: 9,011 and 9,010 have 1 ten and 9,001 has 0 tens. Of 9,011 and 9,010, compare the ones: 1 is more than 0. Order: 9,100; 9,011; 9,010; 9,001.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: How many of the numbers $3{,}205$, $3{,}502$, $3{,}250$ and $3{,}520$ are greater than $3{,}300$?
questions.solution: All four numbers have 3 thousands, and 3,300 has 3 hundreds. 3,205 and 3,250 have only 2 hundreds, so they are less than 3,300. 3,502 and 3,520 have 5 hundreds, so they are greater than 3,300. That is 2 numbers.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Book A is number $3{,}408$, Book B is number $3{,}480$, Book C is number $3{,}048$ and Book D is number $3{,}804$. A librarian lines the books up from the least number to the greatest number. Which book is third in the line?
questions.solution: All have 3 thousands. Compare the hundreds: A 4, B 4, C 0, D 8. C is first and D is last. A and B both have 4 hundreds; A has 0 tens and B has 8 tens, so A comes before B. The line is C (3,048), A (3,408), B (3,480), D (3,804). The third book is Book B.

solve.work: Least to greatest: C 3,048; A 3,408; B 3,480; D 3,804. Third is Book B.

questions.skill: Order numbers
questions.stem: Each choice shows a number in a different way. Which choice is the greatest number?
questions.solution: Change each choice to a number. 3 thousands and 5 hundreds is 3,500. 34 hundreds is 3,400. 340 tens is 3,400. 3 thousands and 49 tens is 3,490. The greatest is 3,500.

solve.work: 34 hundreds = 3,400. 340 tens = 3,400. 3 thousands + 49 tens = 3,000 + 490 = 3,490. 3 thousands + 5 hundreds = 3,500. Greatest: 3,500.

questions.skill: Subtract in a story with regrouping
questions.stem: Lena had 86 stickers. She gave 39 of them to a friend. How many stickers does Lena have now?
questions.solution: Subtract: 86 − 39. You cannot take 9 ones from 6 ones, so trade one ten for 10 ones: 16 − 9 = 7 ones. Now there are 7 tens left: 7 − 3 = 4 tens. The answer is 47. Check: 47 + 39 = 86.

questions.skill: Add in a story
questions.stem: A bakery sold 128 muffins in the morning and 145 muffins in the afternoon. How many muffins did it sell in all?
questions.solution: Add: 128 + 145. Ones: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and carry 1 ten. Tens: 2 + 4 + 1 = 7. Hundreds: 1 + 1 = 2. The total is 273.

questions.skill: Add in a story
questions.stem: A farm stand sold 213 apples on Friday and 142 apples on Saturday. How many apples did it sell on the two days?
questions.solution: Add: ones $3 + 2 = 5$, tens $1 + 4 = 5$, hundreds $2 + 1 = 3$. The farm stand sold 355 apples.

questions.skill: Add in a story
questions.stem: Nora read 120 pages last week and 60 pages this week. How many pages did she read in all?
questions.solution: "In all" means add: $120 + 60 = 180$. (12 tens plus 6 tens is 18 tens.)

questions.solution: Add: $305 + 210$. Ones: $5 + 0 = 5$. Tens: $0 + 1 = 1$. Hundreds: $3 + 2 = 5$. The library has 515 books.

questions.skill: Add in a story

questions.solution: Add: ones $2 + 7 = 9$, tens $5 + 3 = 8$, hundreds $2 + 1 = 3$. There are 389 passengers.

questions.solution: "How many are still on" means take away: $450 - 200 = 250$. (45 tens minus 20 tens is 25 tens.)

questions.skill: Subtract in a story (take away or compare)
questions.stem: Kai has 64 marbles and Ana has 38 marbles. How many more marbles does Kai have than Ana?
questions.solution: "How many more" means find the difference: $64 - 38$. You cannot take 8 ones from 4 ones, so trade 1 ten: $14 - 8 = 6$ ones. Now 5 tens are left: $5 - 3 = 2$ tens. The answer is 26. Check: $26 + 38 = 64$.

questions.skill: Subtract in a story (take away or compare)
questions.stem: Mia's rope is 560 centimeters long. Sam's rope is 230 centimeters long. How many centimeters longer is Mia's rope than Sam's rope?
questions.solution: Find the difference: $560 - 230$. Ones: $0 - 0 = 0$. Tens: $6 - 3 = 3$. Hundreds: $5 - 2 = 3$. The answer is 330. Check: $230 + 330 = 560$.

questions.skill: Subtract in a story (take away or compare)

questions.skill: Find the unknown in a story
questions.stem: Ravi had 40 trading cards. A friend gave him some more, and now he has 70 cards. How many cards did his friend give him?
questions.solution: The friend gave him the extra cards. Think $40 + ? = 70$, so $? = 70 - 40 = 30$. Check: $40 + 30 = 70$.

questions.skill: Find the unknown in a story
questions.stem: Mrs. Lee needs 250 chairs for an event. She has 100 chairs. How many more chairs does she need?
questions.solution: She needs the difference: $250 - 100 = 150$. Check: $100 + 150 = 250$.

questions.solution: The birds at first plus 20 is 85, so the birds at first is $85 - 20 = 65$. Check: $65 + 20 = 85$.

questions.solution: You can add two numbers in either order and get the same sum, so $146 + 53 = 53 + 146$. The other choices use different numbers.

questions.skill: Strategies and properties of addition and subtraction
questions.stem: Use the fact $5 + 8 = 13$ to help you. What is $50 + 80$?
questions.solution: $50 + 80$ is 5 tens plus 8 tens, which is 13 tens. 13 tens is 130.

questions.skill: Strategies and properties of addition and subtraction
questions.stem: Hugo says $483 - 215 = 268$. Which choice can he use to check his answer?
choices: Add $483 + 215$ and see if the sum is 268
Add $268 + 483$ and see if the sum is 215
Add $268 + 215$ and see if the sum is 483
Subtract $215 - 268$ and see if the difference is 483
questions.answer: Add $268 + 215$ and see if the sum is 483
questions.solution: Addition undoes subtraction. If $483 - 215 = 268$, then the answer added to the number taken away must give back the start: $268 + 215 = 483$.

solve.answer: Add $268 + 215$ and see if the sum is 483
solve.work: Subtraction is checked by adding the difference to the part taken away: 268 + 215 = 483, which matches. Option A.

questions.solution: Addition and subtraction are opposites. From $350 + 120 = 470$, taking one part away from the whole leaves the other part: $470 - 120 = 350$.

questions.solution: Ones: $5 + 9 = 14$, write 4 and carry 1 ten. Tens: $7 + 8 + 1 = 16$, write 6 and carry 1 hundred. Hundreds: $2 + 1 + 1 = 4$. The hiker climbed 464 meters.

questions.solution: Find the difference: $842 - 566$. Ones: trade a ten, $12 - 6 = 6$. Tens: now 3 tens, so trade a hundred, $13 - 6 = 7$. Hundreds: now 7 hundreds, $7 - 5 = 2$. The answer is 276. Check: $566 + 276 = 842$.

questions.skill: Subtract in a story (take away or compare)
questions.stem: A water tank holds 920 liters. After 465 liters are used, how many liters are left?
questions.solution: Subtract: $920 - 465$. Ones: $0 - 5$, so trade: tens go from 2 to 1 and ones become 10, so $10 - 5 = 5$. Tens: $1 - 6$, so trade a hundred: $11 - 6 = 5$. Hundreds: $8 - 4 = 4$. The answer is 455. Check: $455 + 465 = 920$.

questions.solution: Subtract: $713 - 289$. Ones: trade a ten, $13 - 9 = 4$. Tens: now 0 tens, so trade a hundred, $10 - 8 = 2$. Hundreds: now 6 hundreds, $6 - 2 = 4$. The answer is 424. Check: $424 + 289 = 713$.

questions.skill: Add in a story
questions.stem: Three classes collected 189, 215 and 276 stamps. How many stamps did they collect in all?
questions.solution: Add the first two: $189 + 215 = 404$. Then add the third: $404 + 276 = 680$. They collected 680 stamps.

questions.skill: Add in a story
questions.stem: A park had 548 visitors in the morning and 375 visitors in the afternoon. How many visitors came in all?
questions.solution: Ones: $8 + 5 = 13$, write 3 and carry 1 ten. Tens: $4 + 7 + 1 = 12$, write 2 and carry 1 hundred. Hundreds: $5 + 3 + 1 = 9$. The total is 923 visitors.

questions.skill: Add in a story
questions.stem: Zoe has 478 red beads and 495 blue beads. How many beads does she have in all?
questions.solution: Ones: $8 + 5 = 13$, write 3 and carry 1. Tens: $7 + 9 + 1 = 17$, write 7 and carry 1. Hundreds: $4 + 4 + 1 = 9$. Zoe has 973 beads.

questions.skill: Subtract in a story (take away or compare)
questions.stem: A concert hall has 905 seats. There are 487 people in the hall, and every person is sitting in a seat. How many seats are empty?
questions.solution: Subtract: $905 - 487$. Trade so that 9 hundreds, 0 tens, 5 ones becomes 8 hundreds, 9 tens, 15 ones. Ones: $15 - 7 = 8$. Tens: $9 - 8 = 1$. Hundreds: $8 - 4 = 4$. The answer is 418. Check: $418 + 487 = 905$.

questions.skill: Subtract in a story (take away or compare)
questions.stem: A game's top score is $1{,}000$ points. Kim has 376 points. How many more points does she need to reach the top score?

questions.skill: Subtract in a story (take away or compare)
questions.stem: A parking lot has 800 spaces. On Friday, 588 spaces were used. How many spaces were not used?
questions.solution: Subtract: $800 - 588$. Count up from 588 to 600 is 12, and from 600 to 800 is 200 more. $12 + 200 = 212$. Check: $588 + 212 = 800$.

questions.skill: Subtract in a story (take away or compare)
questions.stem: Dan scored 645 points in game one and 387 points in game two. How many more points did he score in game one than in game two?
questions.solution: Find the difference: $645 - 387$. Ones: trade a ten, $15 - 7 = 8$. Tens: now 3 tens, so trade a hundred, $13 - 8 = 5$. Hundreds: now 5 hundreds, $5 - 3 = 2$. The answer is 258. Check: $387 + 258 = 645$.

questions.skill: Find the unknown in a story
questions.stem: Chen put 186 coins into a jar. The jar now has 431 coins. How many coins were in the jar before Chen put his coins in?
questions.solution: Coins before + 186 = 431, so coins before = $431 - 186$. Ones: trade, $11 - 6 = 5$. Tens: now 2 tens, $12 - 8 = 4$ (trade a hundred). Hundreds: now 3 hundreds, $3 - 1 = 2$. The answer is 245. Check: $245 + 186 = 431$.

questions.skill: Find the unknown in a story
questions.stem: A baker needs 900 eggs this week. He has 478 eggs. How many more eggs does he need?

questions.skill: Find the unknown in a story
questions.stem: Marcus read 168 pages on Monday. On Tuesday he read some more pages. By the end of Tuesday he had read 391 pages in all. How many pages did he read on Tuesday?
questions.solution: Pages on Tuesday = all the pages minus Monday's pages = $391 - 168$. Ones: $11 - 8 = 3$ (trade). Tens: $8 - 6 = 2$. Hundreds: $3 - 1 = 2$. The answer is 223. Check: $168 + 223 = 391$.

questions.skill: Find the unknown in a story
questions.stem: Anna and Ben have 703 shells together. Anna has 358 of the shells. How many shells does Ben have?
questions.solution: Ben has the rest: $703 - 358$. Trade so that 7 hundreds, 0 tens, 3 ones becomes 6 hundreds, 9 tens, 13 ones. Ones: $13 - 8 = 5$. Tens: $9 - 5 = 4$. Hundreds: $6 - 3 = 3$. The answer is 345. Check: $358 + 345 = 703$.

questions.skill: Add or subtract by place value
questions.stem: Mina finds $538 - 276$ by splitting 276 into $200 + 70 + 6$ and subtracting 200 first, then 70, then 6. Which choice shows her three steps correctly?
questions.solution: $538 - 200 = 338$. Then $338 - 70 = 268$, because 33 tens minus 7 tens is 26 tens, so 268. Then $268 - 6 = 262$. The other choices each have one wrong step. Check: $262 + 276 = 538$.

questions.skill: Add or subtract by place value
questions.stem: Zara adds $467 + 235$ by place value. She adds the hundreds, the tens and the ones separately and gets $600 + 90 + 12$. What is the sum of those three parts?

questions.skill: Add or subtract by place value
questions.stem: Dev wants $705 - 328$. He subtracts $705 - 300 = 405$, and then subtracts the rest, 28, from 405. What is the answer?
questions.solution: After taking away 300, 28 is left to take away: $405 - 28$. Take away 20 to get 385, then 8 more to get 377. The answer is 377. Check: $377 + 328 = 705$.

questions.skill: Strategies and properties of addition and subtraction
questions.stem: Which way of changing $710 - 396$ keeps the answer the same?
questions.solution: Changing both numbers by the same amount keeps the difference the same. Adding 4 to both gives $714 - 400$. Check: $710 - 396 = 314$ and $714 - 400 = 314$.

questions.skill: Strategies and properties of addition and subtraction
questions.stem: Jana counts up to find $1{,}000 - 647$. She goes from 647 to 650, then to 700, then to $1{,}000$. How many does she count up in all?

questions.skill: Strategies and properties of addition and subtraction
questions.stem: Which choice does NOT equal $374 + 258$?

questions.skill: Strategies and properties of addition and subtraction
questions.stem: Omar finds $832 - 399$ by subtracting 400 and then adding 1 back. What is the answer?
questions.solution: $832 - 400 = 432$. Taking away 400 took away 1 too many, so add 1 back: $432 + 1 = 433$.

questions.skill: Strategies and properties of addition and subtraction
questions.stem: Rita subtracted to find $812 - 475$. To check, she added her answer to 475 and got 812. What was Rita's answer?
questions.solution: Her answer plus 475 makes 812, so her answer is $812 - 475$. Count up from 475 to 500 is 25, to 800 is 300 more, to 812 is 12 more. $25 + 300 + 12 = 337$. Check: $337 + 475 = 812$.

questions.skill: Add with regrouping
questions.solution: Ones: $7 + 6 = 13$, write 3 and carry 1. Tens: $8 + 9 + 1 = 18$, write 8 and carry 1. Hundreds: $4 + 3 + 1 = 8$. The sum is 883.

questions.skill: Add with regrouping
Add with regrouping
questions.solution: Ones: $8 + 4 = 12$, write 2 and carry 1. Tens: $9 + 9 + 1 = 19$, write 9 and carry 1. Hundreds: $5 + 3 + 1 = 9$. The sum is 992.

questions.skill: Add with regrouping
questions.stem: Which sum equals 912?

questions.skill: Subtract with regrouping
questions.solution: Trade so that 9 hundreds, 0 tens, 0 ones becomes 8 hundreds, 9 tens, 10 ones. Ones: $10 - 7 = 3$. Tens: $9 - 5 = 4$. Hundreds: $8 - 4 = 4$. The answer is 443. Check: $443 + 457 = 900$.

questions.skill: Subtract with regrouping
Subtract with regrouping
questions.stem: Find the difference: $706 - 389$.
questions.solution: Trade so that 7 hundreds, 0 tens, 6 ones becomes 6 hundreds, 9 tens, 16 ones. Ones: $16 - 9 = 7$. Tens: $9 - 8 = 1$. Hundreds: $6 - 3 = 3$. The answer is 317. Check: $317 + 389 = 706$.

questions.skill: Subtract with regrouping
questions.stem: Which difference equals 268?
questions.solution: $514 - 246$: ones $14 - 6 = 8$, tens $0 - 4$ means trade, so $10 - 4 = 6$, hundreds $4 - 2 = 2$. That is 268. The other differences are 258, 278 and 258.

questions.skill: Equation with a missing number or digit
questions.stem: What digit goes in the place of the ? to make $3?4 + 157 = 501$ true?
questions.solution: $501 - 157 = 344$. So the three-digit number is 344, and the ? is 4. Check: $344 + 157 = 501$.

questions.skill: Equation with a missing number or digit
questions.stem: Which digit goes in the place of the ? to make $7?2 - 345 = 417$ true?
questions.solution: The first number is $417 + 345 = 762$. So the ? is 6. Check: $762 - 345 = 417$.

questions.skill: Equation with a missing number or digit
questions.stem: The difference between two numbers is 238. The smaller number is 457. What is the greater number?
questions.solution: The greater number is the smaller number plus the difference: $457 + 238 = 695$. Check: $695 - 457 = 238$.

questions.skill: Find a missing digit in a three-digit sum
questions.stem: A three-digit number is written 4?7, where ? is a digit that cannot be read. When 286 is added to this number, the sum is 733. What digit does the ? stand for?
questions.solution: Look at the ones: 7 + 6 = 13, so write 3 and regroup 1 ten. In the tens column, ? + 8 + 1 ten must end in 3, so ? + 9 = 13 and ? = 4. Check: 447 + 286 = 733.

solve.work: 4?7 + 286 = 733, so 4?7 = 733 - 286 = 447. Check: 447 + 286 = 733. The missing digit is 4. Only one digit works since the number is fixed by the subtraction.

questions.skill: Equal groups as a multiplication sentence
questions.stem: There are 4 bags with 6 apples in each bag. Which multiplication sentence shows the number of apples in all?
questions.solution: 4 bags with 6 apples in each bag is 4 equal groups of 6. That is $4 \times 6 = 24$ apples.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, and so on. What is the 7th number you say?
questions.solution: Count by 5s seven times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. The 7th number is 35, which is $7 \times 5$.

questions.skill: Multiply by 10
questions.stem: A pack has 10 pencils. How many pencils are in 6 packs?
questions.solution: 6 packs of 10 pencils is $6 \times 10 = 60$. (Six tens make sixty.)

questions.skill: Equal groups and multiplication sentences
questions.stem: Maya puts 3 marbles in each of 5 cups. Which number sentence shows how many marbles she has in all?
questions.solution: There are 5 cups with 3 marbles in each cup, which is 5 groups of 3. Equal groups are found by multiplying, so $5 \times 3 = 15$.

solve.work: 5 cups, 3 marbles each: 5 groups of 3 = 5 x 3 = 15. Other options give 8, 2, 9 and do not model equal groups of 5 cups.

questions.skill: Equal groups and multiplication sentences
questions.stem: $4 \times 3$ means 4 groups with 3 in each group. How many are there in all?
questions.solution: Add 3 four times: $3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12$. So $4 \times 3 = 12$.

questions.skill: Equal groups and multiplication sentences
questions.stem: Ben has 6 bags with 2 toy cars in each bag. He writes $6 \times 2 = 12$. What does the 2 tell us?
choices: the number of bags Ben has
the number of cars in each bag
the number of cars in all of the bags
how many more cars than bags
questions.answer: the number of cars in each bag
questions.solution: In $6 \times 2$ the 6 is the number of bags and the 2 is the number of cars in each bag. The total, 12, is the number of cars in all.

solve.answer: the number of cars in each bag
solve.work: 6 bags, 2 cars in each bag; 6 x 2 = 12. The 6 is the number of bags, the 2 is the number in each bag, 12 is the total.

questions.skill: Equal groups and multiplication sentences
questions.stem: 3 plates with 4 cookies on each plate can be written as $3 \times \square = 12$. What number goes in the box?
questions.solution: Each plate has 4 cookies, so the box holds 4. Check: $3 \times 4 = 12$.

solve.work: 3 plates with 4 cookies each: 3 x 4 = 12, so the box is 4.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: Count by 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12. What number comes next?
questions.solution: Each number is 3 more than the one before. $12 + 3 = 15$.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: Which list shows counting by 4s?
questions.solution: Counting by 4s adds 4 each time: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. The other lists add 2, add 3 or double.

solve.work: Counting by 4s adds 4 each time: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. Others double, add 2, or add 3.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: Nina counts by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. What is the 8th number she says?
questions.solution: The 8th number when counting by 10s is 8 tens, which is 80.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: Each child wears 2 shoes. Count by 2s to find how many shoes 6 children wear.
questions.solution: Count by 2s six times: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. So 6 children wear 12 shoes.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: Aiden counts by 3s: 12, 15, 18, ___, 24. Which number is missing?
questions.solution: Each number is 3 more than the one before, so the missing number is $18 + 3 = 21$. Check: $21 + 3 = 24$.

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Ravi finds $6 \times 4$ by breaking 6 into $5 + 1$. He knows $5 \times 4 = 20$ and $1 \times 4 = 4$. What is $6 \times 4$?

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: If 7 is broken into $5 + 2$, which expression is equal to $7 \times 3$?
questions.solution: 7 groups of 3 is 5 groups of 3 plus 2 groups of 3: $(5 \times 3) + (2 \times 3) = 15 + 6 = 21$.

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Lina knows $2 \times 9 = 18$ and $1 \times 9 = 9$. She adds them to find $3 \times 9$. What is $3 \times 9$?
questions.solution: $3 \times 9$ is 2 groups of 9 plus 1 group of 9: $18 + 9 = 27$.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: There are 5 tables in a room. Each table has 4 chairs. How many chairs are there in all?
questions.solution: 5 tables with 4 chairs each is 5 groups of 4: $5 \times 4 = 20$.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: A spider has 8 legs. How many legs do 3 spiders have?
questions.solution: 3 spiders with 8 legs each: $3 \times 8 = 24$ legs.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: Lena buys 6 packs of stickers. Each pack has 3 stickers. How many stickers does she buy?
questions.solution: 6 packs with 3 stickers in each pack: $6 \times 3 = 18$.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: A small carton holds 6 eggs. How many eggs are in 5 cartons?
questions.solution: 5 cartons with 6 eggs each: $5 \times 6 = 30$ eggs.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A muffin pan has 2 rows. Each row has 6 cups. How many cups are in the pan?
questions.solution: The array has 2 rows of 6 cups: $2 \times 6 = 12$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: Which array has 12 squares?
choices: 3 rows with 4 squares in each row
3 rows with 5 squares in each row
2 rows with 5 squares in each row
4 rows with 4 squares in each row
questions.answer: 3 rows with 4 squares in each row
questions.solution: $3 \times 4 = 12$. The other arrays have $3 \times 5 = 15$, $2 \times 5 = 10$ and $4 \times 4 = 16$ squares.

solve.answer: 3 rows with 4 squares in each row

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A sticker sheet has 5 rows and 2 columns of stickers. How many stickers are on the sheet?
questions.solution: There are 5 rows with 2 stickers in each: $5 \times 2 = 10$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: Chairs are set up in 4 rows with 4 chairs in each row. How many chairs are there?
questions.solution: 4 rows of 4 chairs: $4 \times 4 = 16$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: One array has 6 rows with 2 dots in each row. Another array has 2 rows with 6 dots in each row. Which statement is true?
choices: The first array has more dots
The second array has more dots
questions.solution: $6 \times 2 = 12$ and $2 \times 6 = 12$. Turning an array on its side does not change the number of dots.

questions.skill: Patterns in multiples
questions.stem: Which statement is true about the numbers you say when counting by 5s?
questions.solution: Counting by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, ... The ones digit switches between 5 and 0.

solve.work: 5, 10, 15, 20, ...: ones digits alternate 5 and 0. Not all 5, not all even.

questions.skill: Patterns in multiples
questions.stem: Which word describes every number you say when counting by 2s, starting at 2?
questions.solution: Counting by 2s gives 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, ... Every one of them is an even number.

solve.work: 2, 4, 6, 8, ...: all even. Not all multiples of 5, not all over 10, none odd.

questions.skill: Patterns in multiples
questions.stem: One tricycle has 3 wheels. Two tricycles have 6 wheels. Three tricycles have 9 wheels. Following the pattern, how many wheels do 5 tricycles have?
questions.solution: Each tricycle adds 3 wheels: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15. So 5 tricycles have 15 wheels.

questions.skill: Patterns in multiples
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 10 and adds 10 each time: 10, 20, 30, 40. What number comes right after 90 in this pattern?
questions.solution: Each number is 10 more than the one before, so after 90 comes $90 + 10 = 100$.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: What is $4 \times 20$? Think of 4 groups of 2 tens.
questions.solution: 4 groups of 2 tens is 8 tens, which is 80.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: Find $7 \times 10$.
questions.solution: 7 groups of 10 is 7 tens, which is 70.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: What is $2 \times 30$?
questions.solution: 2 groups of 3 tens is 6 tens, which is 60.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: Each bag holds 30 beads. How many beads are in 3 bags?
questions.solution: 3 bags with 3 tens in each is 9 tens, which is 90 beads.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: A dime is worth 10 cents. How many cents are 5 dimes worth?
questions.solution: 5 groups of 10 cents is 5 tens, which is 50 cents.

questions.skill: Match a story to a multiplication sentence
questions.stem: Which story matches $5 \times 4$?
choices: Maya has 5 pencils and then gets 4 more.
Maya has 5 pencils and then gives away 4.
Maya has 5 boxes. Each box has 4 pencils.
Maya shares 5 pencils equally among 4 friends.
questions.answer: Maya has 5 boxes. Each box has 4 pencils.
questions.solution: $5 \times 4$ means 5 equal groups of 4. 5 boxes with 4 pencils in each box matches. The other stories are adding, taking away and sharing.

solve.answer: Maya has 5 boxes. Each box has 4 pencils.
solve.work: 5 x 4 means 5 groups of 4: 5 boxes with 4 pencils each.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A theater has 6 rows of seats. Each row has 7 seats. How many seats are in the theater?
questions.solution: 6 rows of 7 seats is an array with $6 \times 7 = 42$ seats.

questions.skill: Break a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Kai finds $7 \times 8$ by breaking 7 into $5 + 2$ and writing $(5 \times 8) + (2 \times 8)$. What is $7 \times 8$?

questions.skill: Equal groups and multiplication sentences
questions.stem: Which repeated addition has the same total as $4 \times 6$?
questions.solution: $4 \times 6$ is 4 groups of 6, which is $6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24$. The other sums are 20, 18 and 10.

questions.skill: Equal groups and multiplication sentences
questions.stem: $7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7$ is the same as $6 \times \square$. What number goes in the box?
questions.solution: There are 6 sevens added together, so it is 6 groups of 7, or $6 \times 7$. The box holds 7.

solve.work: Six 7s added: 6 groups of 7 = 6 x 7, box = 7 (total 42).

questions.skill: Equal groups and multiplication sentences
questions.stem: Jon draws 3 groups with 8 dots in each group. Lia draws 8 groups with 3 dots in each group. How many dots does Lia draw in all?
questions.solution: Lia draws 8 groups of 3 dots, so $8 \times 3 = 24$. (Jon draws 24 too, because $3 \times 8 = 8 \times 3$.)

solve.work: Lia: 8 groups of 3 = 24 (same as Jon's 3 x 8 = 24).

questions.skill: Equal groups and multiplication sentences
questions.stem: Which one shows equal groups?
questions.solution: Equal groups all have the same number in them. Only the bags with 4, 4 and 4 apples are equal.

solve.work: Equal groups need the same number in every bag. Only 4, 4, 4 is equal.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: Count by 6s: 6, 12, 18, 24. What is the 7th number you say?
questions.solution: Keep counting by 6s: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42. The 7th number is 42.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: Which number do you say when you count by 8s, starting at 8?
questions.solution: Counting by 8s: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40. Only 40 is on the list.

solve.work: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48. 40 is said; 36, 44, 50 are not multiples of 8.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: A bus stops every 4 blocks along a street. The first stop is at block 4. At which block is the 6th stop?
questions.solution: The stops are at blocks 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. The 6th stop is at block 24.

solve.work: Stops at 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24: the 6th stop is block 24.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: Hana skip counts by 9s: 9, 18, 27, 36. What is the 6th number she says?
questions.solution: Keep counting by 9s: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54. The 6th number is 54.

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Ken knows that 4 groups of 6 make 24. He pictures 8 groups of 6 as two sets of 4 groups of 6. How many are in 8 groups of 6?
questions.solution: 8 groups of 6 is two sets of 4 groups of 6, so $24 + 24 = 48$.

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Which expression shows a way to find $9 \times 7$ by thinking of 9 as $10 - 1$?
questions.solution: 9 groups of 7 is 10 groups of 7 take away 1 group of 7: $70 - 7 = 63$.

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Ella knows $5 \times 9 = 45$. She adds one more group of 9 to find $6 \times 9$. What is $6 \times 9$?
questions.solution: 6 groups of 9 is 5 groups of 9 plus 1 more group of 9: $45 + 9 = 54$.

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Which pair of facts could help you find $7 \times 6$?
questions.solution: Break 7 into $5 + 2$. Then $7 \times 6 = (5 \times 6) + (2 \times 6) = 30 + 12 = 42$.

solve.issues: Minor: 'could help you find' is loose (e.g. 7 x 5 alone could help); the intended pair is the only one whose sum is 7 x 6, so it stands.

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Sal knows $4 \times 7 = 28$. He doubles 28 to find $8 \times 7$. What is $8 \times 7$?
questions.solution: 8 groups of 7 is two sets of 4 groups of 7, so $28 + 28 = 56$.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: The school library has 8 shelves. Each shelf holds 7 books. How many books fit on all of the shelves?
questions.solution: 8 shelves with 7 books on each: $8 \times 7 = 56$.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: Which problem can be solved with $6 \times 5$?
choices: Six friends each have 5 stickers. How many stickers do they have in all?
Six friends share 5 stickers. How many does each friend get?
Dan has 6 stickers and gets 5 more. How many does he have now?
Dan has 6 stickers and gives away 5. How many are left?
questions.answer: Six friends each have 5 stickers. How many stickers do they have in all?
questions.solution: $6 \times 5$ means 6 equal groups of 5. Only the first problem has 6 friends with 5 stickers each. The others add, subtract or share.

solve.answer: Six friends each have 5 stickers. How many stickers do they have in all?
solve.work: 6 x 5 = 6 groups of 5: six friends each with 5 stickers. The others are sharing (division), subtraction and addition.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: Dev reads 8 pages each night. How many pages does he read in 5 nights?
questions.solution: 5 nights with 8 pages each night: $5 \times 8 = 40$ pages.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: Each bus holds 9 students. How many students can ride in 6 buses?
questions.solution: 6 buses with 9 students in each bus: $6 \times 9 = 54$.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 8 slices. How many slices are there in 4 pizzas?
questions.solution: 4 pizzas with 8 slices each: $4 \times 8 = 32$ slices.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A bakery tray holds cookies in 5 rows and 6 columns. How many cookies fit on one tray?
questions.solution: The array has 5 rows with 6 cookies in each: $5 \times 6 = 30$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: An array has 24 squares in 4 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?
questions.solution: Think $4 \times \square = 24$. Since $4 \times 6 = 24$, each row has 6 squares.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: Mr. Lee sets up 35 desks in an array with 5 rows. How many desks are in each row?
questions.solution: Think $5 \times \square = 35$. Since $5 \times 7 = 35$, each row has 7 desks.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: Pia says an array with 6 rows and 4 columns has the same number of squares as an array with 4 rows and 6 columns. Is she right?
choices: No, the first has more squares
No, the second has more squares
questions.solution: $6 \times 4 = 24$ and $4 \times 6 = 24$. The two arrays have the same number of squares.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A game board has 8 rows and 8 columns of squares. How many squares are on the board?
questions.solution: $8 \times 8 = 64$ squares.

questions.skill: Patterns in multiples
questions.stem: Nina notices that when 9 is multiplied by a number from 1 to 10, the digits of the product add up to 9 (for example, $9 \times 3 = 27$ and $2 + 7 = 9$). Which number is $9 \times 7$?
questions.solution: Only 63 has digits that add up to 9, because $6 + 3 = 9$. Also, $9 \times 7 = 63$.

solve.work: 9 x 7 = 63; 6 + 3 = 9 fits the pattern. 65, 56, 61 have digit sums 11, 11, 7.

questions.skill: Patterns in multiples
questions.stem: Rin saves the same number of dollars each week. After 1 week she has 8 dollars, after 2 weeks she has 16 dollars, and after 3 weeks she has 24 dollars. How many dollars does she have after 7 weeks?
questions.solution: She adds 8 dollars each week, so after 7 weeks she has $7 \times 8 = 56$ dollars.

questions.skill: Patterns in multiples
questions.stem: Uma sees that multiplying by 4 gives double the answer for multiplying by 2. She knows $2 \times 7 = 14$. What is $4 \times 7$?
questions.solution: $4 \times 7$ is double $2 \times 7$: $14 + 14 = 28$.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: What is $6 \times 30$?
questions.solution: $6 \times 3 = 18$, so 6 groups of 3 tens is 18 tens, which is 180.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: Mia finds $4 \times 70$ by first finding $4 \times 7 = 28$. What is $4 \times 70$?
questions.solution: 28 groups of ten: 28 tens is 280.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: A farm stand packs 60 apples in each crate. How many apples are in 4 crates?
questions.solution: $4 \times 6 = 24$, so 4 groups of 6 tens is 24 tens, which is 240 apples.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: Pedro practices piano for 30 minutes every day. How many minutes does he practice in 5 days?
questions.solution: $5 \times 3 = 15$, so 5 groups of 3 tens is 15 tens, which is 150 minutes.

questions.skill: Multiply by a multiple of 10 in a story
questions.stem: A box holds 30 crayons. How many crayons are in 7 boxes?
questions.solution: $7 \times 30$ is 7 groups of 3 tens. $7 \times 3 = 21$, so 21 tens, which is 210.

questions.skill: Patterns made by repeated adding
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 0 and adds 4 each time: 0, 4, 8, 12, and so on. Which number will be in the pattern?
questions.solution: The numbers in the pattern are what you get by counting by 4s: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36. So 36 is in the pattern ($4 \times 9 = 36$). The numbers 30, 34 and 38 are skipped.

solve.work: Pattern is multiples of 4. 36 = 4 x 9 is in it; 38, 34, 30 are not multiples of 4.

questions.skill: Break a multiplication fact using 10
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $6 \times 9$?
questions.solution: 9 is one less than 10, so $6 \times 9$ is 6 less than $6 \times 10$. That is $60 - 6 = 54$, and $6 \times 9 = 54$.

questions.skill: Equal groups and multiplication sentences
questions.stem: Sam puts 36 stickers into groups of 4 with none left over. He writes $\square \times 4 = 36$ to show the number of groups. What number goes in the box?
questions.solution: Count how many 4s make 36: $9 \times 4 = 36$. So there are 9 groups.

questions.skill: Equal groups and multiplication sentences
questions.stem: Zoe wants to put 20 shells into equal groups with none left over. Which number of groups can she make?
questions.solution: 4 groups of 5 shells use $4 \times 5 = 20$ shells. With 3, 6 or 7 groups, some shells would be left over.

solve.work: 20 = 4 x 5, so 4 equal groups of 5 works. 20/7, 20/6, 20/3 leave remainders (20 = 7x2+6, 6x3+2, 3x6+2).

questions.skill: Equal groups and multiplication sentences
questions.stem: Which expression shows 5 groups of 3 together with 2 more groups of 3?
questions.solution: 5 groups of 3 plus 2 more groups of 3 make 7 groups of 3, which is $7 \times 3 = 21$.

solve.work: 5 groups of 3 plus 2 more groups of 3 = 7 groups of 3 = 7 x 3 = 21. (5 x 3) + 2 = 17, 5 x (3+2) = 25, 7 + 3 = 10 are wrong.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: Gabe counts by 8s: 8, 16, 24, and so on. How many numbers has he said when he says 56?
questions.solution: The numbers are 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56. That is 7 numbers, because $7 \times 8 = 56$.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: Which number would you NOT say when counting by 6s, starting at 6?
questions.solution: Counting by 6s: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48. The number 46 is skipped.

solve.work: Multiples of 6: 36, 42, 48 are all said (6x6, 6x7, 6x8). 46 is not a multiple of 6.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: A frog jumps 5 steps each time. It lands on 35, and then it jumps 3 more times. At what number does it land?
questions.solution: Counting by 5s from 35: 40, 45, 50. After 3 more jumps the frog lands on 50.

questions.skill: Skip-counting
questions.stem: Marcus counts by 9s: 9, 18, 27. He keeps going until he has said 8 numbers. What is the last number he says?
questions.solution: Counting by 9s: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72. The 8th number is 72.

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Mia finds $9 \times 6$ by writing $(5 \times 6) + (4 \times 6)$. What is $9 \times 6$?

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Which expression does NOT equal $8 \times 4$?
questions.solution: $8 \times 4 = 32$. The groups $4 + 4$, $5 + 3$ and $2 + 6$ all make 8, so they give 32. But $6 + 3 = 9$ groups of 4 is 36.

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Omar knows that 10 groups of 8 make 80. He takes away 1 group of 8 to find 9 groups of 8. How many are in 9 groups of 8?
questions.solution: Take one group of 8 away from 80: $80 - 8 = 72$. So $9 \times 8 = 72$.

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Dee knows $7 \times 7 = 49$. She takes away 3 groups of 7, which is $3 \times 7 = 21$, to find $4 \times 7$. What is $4 \times 7$?
questions.solution: $7 \times 7$ with 3 groups of 7 taken away leaves 4 groups of 7: $49 - 21 = 28$.

questions.skill: Breaking a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Ned breaks 9 into $4 + \square$ to find $9 \times 7$, writing $(4 \times 7) + (\square \times 7)$. What number goes in both boxes?
questions.solution: The two parts of 9 must add to 9, so $4 + \square = 9$ and the box holds 5. Check: $(4 \times 7) + (5 \times 7) = 28 + 35 = 63 = 9 \times 7$.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: Ari bought 4 boxes of markers with 6 markers in each box. Then he lost 5 markers. How many markers does he have now?
questions.solution: First find all the markers: $4 \times 6 = 24$. Then take away the 5 he lost: $24 - 5 = 19$.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: A farmer plants 7 rows of corn with 8 plants in each row, and 3 rows of beans with 8 plants in each row. How many plants are there in all?
questions.solution: There are $7 + 3 = 10$ rows with 8 plants each, so $10 \times 8 = 80$ plants.

solve.work: 7 x 8 = 56 corn, 3 x 8 = 24 beans, 56 + 24 = 80 (or 10 rows x 8).

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: Tess has 36 beads. She makes bracelets with 9 beads on each one. How many bracelets can she make?
questions.solution: Think of the missing factor: $4 \times 9 = 36$. So she can make 4 bracelets.

solve.issues: Leans toward division (measurement division) rather than the meaning of multiplication; acceptable as an unknown-factor equal-groups problem.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: Each ticket to the fair costs 3 dollars. Hana buys 5 tickets and pays with a 20-dollar bill. How many dollars does she get back?
questions.solution: The tickets cost $5 \times 3 = 15$ dollars. Her change is $20 - 15 = 5$ dollars.

questions.skill: Equal-groups word problems
questions.stem: A van has 3 rows of seats with 4 seats in each row. A school uses 4 of these vans. How many seats are there in all?
questions.solution: One van has $3 \times 4 = 12$ seats. Four vans have $4 \times 12 = 48$ seats.

solve.work: Each van: 3 x 4 = 12 seats. 4 vans: 4 x 12 = 48.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A box of chocolates has 5 rows with 6 chocolates in each row. Then 4 chocolates are eaten. How many chocolates are left?
questions.solution: The full box has $5 \times 6 = 30$ chocolates. After 4 are eaten, $30 - 4 = 26$ are left.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: The seats in a hall are in an array of 9 rows with 7 seats in each row. The last row is closed. How many seats are open?
questions.solution: Only 8 rows are open, with 7 seats each: $8 \times 7 = 56$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: One array of stamps has 4 rows and 9 columns. Another array has 6 rows and 5 columns. How many more stamps are in the first array than in the second?
questions.solution: The first array has $4 \times 9 = 36$ stamps. The second has $6 \times 5 = 30$ stamps. The difference is $36 - 30 = 6$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A farmer plants 48 apple trees in an array with equal rows. Which could be the array?
questions.solution: $6 \times 8 = 48$. The other arrays have $6 \times 9 = 54$, $5 \times 10 = 50$ and $7 \times 7 = 49$ trees.

questions.skill: Patterns in multiples
questions.stem: Which product is an even number?
questions.solution: $7 \times 4 = 28$ is even, because 4 is even. The others are $35$, $27$ and $45$, which are odd.

questions.skill: Patterns in multiples
questions.stem: The multiples of 5 are 5, 10, 15, 20, and so on. What is the ones digit of the 12th multiple of 5?
questions.solution: The 12th multiple of 5 is $12 \times 5 = 60$. The ones digit of 60 is 0.

questions.skill: Patterns in multiples
questions.stem: A rule machine multiplies every input by 6. When the input is 4, the output is 24. What is the output when the input is 9?
questions.solution: The rule is multiply by 6, so the output is $9 \times 6 = 54$.

questions.skill: Patterns in multiples
questions.stem: A baker packs 6 muffins in each box. After 1 box there are 6 muffins packed, after 2 boxes there are 12, and after 3 boxes there are 18. After how many boxes will 54 muffins be packed?
questions.solution: Each box adds 6 muffins. Since $9 \times 6 = 54$, it takes 9 boxes.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: What is $6 \times 90$?
questions.solution: $6 \times 9 = 54$, so 6 groups of 9 tens is 54 tens, which is 540.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: A theater has 9 sections. Each section has 80 seats. How many seats does the theater have?
questions.solution: $9 \times 8 = 72$, so 9 groups of 8 tens is 72 tens, which is 720 seats.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $7 \times 50$?
questions.solution: 50 is 5 tens, so $7 \times 50 = (7 \times 5) \times 10 = 35 \times 10 = 350$.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: $\square \times 40 = 320$. What number goes in the box?
questions.solution: 320 is 32 tens and 40 is 4 tens. Since $8 \times 4 = 32$, we have $8 \times 40 = 320$. The box holds 8.

questions.skill: Multiplying by multiples of 10
questions.stem: Rita has 3 boxes with 70 beads in each box. She uses 100 of the beads. How many beads does she have left?
questions.solution: All the beads: $3 \times 70 = 210$. After using 100, $210 - 100 = 110$ are left.

questions.skill: Share equally: size of each group
questions.stem: 12 cookies are shared equally among 4 children. How many cookies does each child get?
questions.solution: Share 12 into 4 equal groups: $12 \div 4 = 3$. Each child gets 3 cookies.

questions.skill: Make equal groups: number of groups
questions.stem: 20 stickers are put into groups of 5. How many groups are there?
questions.solution: Count how many groups of 5 fit in 20: $20 \div 5 = 4$. There are 4 groups.

questions.skill: Match a story to a division sentence
questions.stem: Which story matches $18 \div 3$?
choices: Maya has 18 pencils and gets 3 more.
18 pencils are shared equally among 3 students.
questions.answer: 18 pencils are shared equally among 3 students.
questions.solution: $18 \div 3$ means making equal shares of 18. Sharing 18 pencils equally among 3 students matches. The other stories are adding, multiplying and subtracting.

solve.answer: 18 pencils are shared equally among 3 students.
solve.work: 18 / 3 is sharing 18 equally into 3 groups. The other stories are multiplication, subtraction and addition.

questions.skill: Share equally: find the size of each group
questions.stem: Ben puts 15 marbles into 3 bags. Each bag has the same number of marbles. How many marbles are in each bag?
questions.solution: Sharing 15 marbles equally into 3 bags is $15 \div 3 = 5$. Check: $3 \times 5 = 15$.

questions.skill: Share equally: find the size of each group
questions.stem: 28 apples are shared equally among 4 baskets. How many apples go in each basket?
questions.solution: Each basket gets $28 \div 4 = 7$ apples. Check: $4 \times 7 = 28$. The other choices come from subtracting (24), adding (32), or giving the number of baskets (4).

questions.skill: Share equally: find the size of each group
questions.stem: A teacher hands out 24 pencils equally to 6 students. How many pencils does each student get?
questions.solution: $24 \div 6 = 4$, so each student gets 4 pencils. Check: $6 \times 4 = 24$.

questions.skill: Share equally: find the size of each group
questions.stem: Sixteen crayons are packed equally into 2 boxes. How many crayons are in each box?
questions.solution: Each box gets $16 \div 2 = 8$ crayons. Check: $2 \times 8 = 16$.

questions.skill: Share equally: find the size of each group
questions.stem: Four friends share 36 grapes. Each friend gets the same number of grapes. How many grapes does each friend get?
questions.solution: $36 \div 4 = 9$, so each friend gets 9 grapes. Check: $4 \times 9 = 36$.

questions.skill: Make equal groups: find the number of groups
questions.stem: 30 children go on a lake trip. They sit 5 to a canoe, and every canoe is full. How many canoes are there?
questions.solution: Each canoe holds 5 children, so the number of canoes is $30 \div 5 = 6$. Check: $6 \times 5 = 30$.

questions.skill: Make equal groups: find the number of groups
questions.stem: Leo has 21 books. He puts 3 books on each shelf. How many shelves does he use?
questions.solution: The number of shelves is $21 \div 3 = 7$. Check: $7 \times 3 = 21$. The other choices come from subtracting (18), adding (24), or multiplying (63).

questions.skill: Make equal groups: find the number of groups
questions.stem: A farmer puts 36 plums into boxes of 4 plums each. How many boxes does he fill?
questions.solution: The number of boxes is $36 \div 4 = 9$. Check: $9 \times 4 = 36$.

questions.skill: Make equal groups: find the number of groups
questions.stem: Kai makes piles of 9 cards from 45 cards. How many piles does Kai make?
questions.solution: The number of piles is $45 \div 9 = 5$. Check: $5 \times 9 = 45$.

questions.skill: Make equal groups: find the number of groups
