questions.stem: A warehouse has 450 boxes. A truck brings 275 more boxes. Then 380 boxes are shipped out. How many boxes are in the warehouse now?
questions.solution: After the truck comes there are $450 + 275 = 725$ boxes. After shipping, $725 - 380 = 345$ boxes.

questions.skill: Two-step: add and subtract in a story
questions.stem: A water tank has 600 liters of water. 245 liters are poured out. Then 130 liters are added. How many liters are in the tank now?
questions.solution: First $600 - 245 = 355$ liters. Then $355 + 130 = 485$ liters. The choice 355 forgets the water added, 225 takes away the 130, and 975 adds everything.

questions.skill: Two-step: add or subtract first, then multiply
questions.stem: A gardener plants 8 rows with 9 seeds in each row. In every row, 2 seeds do not sprout. How many seeds sprout in all?
questions.solution: In each row $9 - 2 = 7$ seeds sprout. Eight rows give $8 \times 7 = 56$ seeds.

questions.skill: Two-step: add or subtract first, then multiply
questions.stem: Mr. Ray has 6 boxes with 12 pencils in each box. He takes 4 pencils out of each box. How many pencils are left in the 6 boxes?
questions.solution: Each box now has $12 - 4 = 8$ pencils. Six boxes have $6 \times 8 = 48$ pencils. The choice 68 takes away only 4 pencils in all, 24 is the number taken out, and 8 is the count for one box.

questions.skill: Two-step: add or subtract first, then multiply
questions.stem: A school buys 4 boxes of red pens, 3 boxes of blue pens and 2 boxes of black pens. Each box has 10 pens. The school gives 30 of the pens to a class. How many pens are left?
questions.solution: The school buys $4 + 3 + 2 = 9$ boxes. That is $9 \times 10 = 90$ pens. After giving 30 away, $90 - 30 = 60$ pens are left.

questions.skill: Two-step: add two products
questions.stem: At a carnival, a ring toss costs 3 tickets for each turn and a dart game costs 4 tickets for each turn. Jo plays the ring toss 6 times and the dart game 5 times. How many tickets does Jo use?
questions.solution: The ring toss uses $6 \times 3 = 18$ tickets. The dart game uses $5 \times 4 = 20$ tickets. In all, $18 + 20 = 38$ tickets.

questions.skill: Two-step: add two products
questions.stem: Dad buys 7 packs of juice boxes with 6 boxes in each pack and 3 packs of water bottles with 8 bottles in each pack. How many drinks does he buy?
questions.solution: The juice is $7 \times 6 = 42$ and the water is $3 \times 8 = 24$, so $42 + 24 = 66$. The choice 42 counts only the juice, 24 counts only the water, and 140 multiplies (7 + 3) by (6 + 8).

questions.skill: Two-step: add two products
questions.stem: A florist makes 6 bouquets with 5 roses in each bouquet and 3 bouquets with 8 tulips in each bouquet. How many flowers does she use altogether?
questions.solution: The roses are $6 \times 5 = 30$ and the tulips are $3 \times 8 = 24$. Altogether $30 + 24 = 54$ flowers.

questions.skill: Two-step: compare two products
questions.stem: Sam saves 7 dollars every week for 9 weeks. Tara saves 6 dollars every week for 8 weeks. How many more dollars did Sam save than Tara?
questions.solution: Sam saved $7 \times 9 = 63$ dollars. Tara saved $6 \times 8 = 48$ dollars. Sam saved $63 - 48 = 15$ dollars more.

questions.skill: Two-step: compare two products
questions.stem: Which is more, 8 packs with 7 pencils in each pack or 6 packs with 9 pencils in each pack, and by how many pencils?
questions.solution: 8 packs of 7 is $8 \times 7 = 56$ pencils. 6 packs of 9 is $6 \times 9 = 54$ pencils. The first is more, by $56 - 54 = 2$ pencils.

questions.skill: Two-step: "more than" and "fewer than" stories
questions.stem: Pat collects 36 cans. Quinn collects 14 fewer cans than Pat. Rae collects 9 more cans than Quinn. How many cans do the three friends collect in all?
questions.solution: Quinn collects $36 - 14 = 22$ cans. Rae collects $22 + 9 = 31$ cans. In all, $36 + 22 + 31 = 89$ cans.

solve.issues: Needs three or four operations (two derived amounts, then a three-addend sum); more than the two steps the standard describes, though still solvable at grade 3.

questions.skill: Two-step: "more than" and "fewer than" stories
questions.stem: A zoo has 54 birds. It has 17 fewer reptiles than birds. How many birds and reptiles does the zoo have in all?
questions.solution: The zoo has $54 - 17 = 37$ reptiles. In all, $54 + 37 = 91$. The choice 37 is only the reptiles, 71 adds the 17 instead, and 108 counts the same number of reptiles as birds.

questions.skill: Two-step: three numbers to add or subtract
questions.stem: A shelf had 240 books. On Monday 85 books were checked out. On Tuesday 60 books were returned and 45 books were checked out. How many books are on the shelf now?
questions.solution: After Monday: $240 - 85 = 155$. Tuesday returns: $155 + 60 = 215$. Tuesday checkouts: $215 - 45 = 170$ books.

solve.issues: Three steps rather than two; fine for grade 3 but beyond the standard's two-step scope.

questions.skill: Two-step: three numbers to add or subtract
questions.stem: A jar has 500 beads in it. Lila uses 128 beads for a bracelet and 175 beads for a necklace. How many beads are left in the jar?
questions.solution: After the bracelet $500 - 128 = 372$. After the necklace $372 - 175 = 197$. The choice 372 forgets the necklace, 303 is the number of beads used, and 803 adds everything.

questions.skill: Estimate a sum or difference by rounding
questions.stem: Round each number to the nearest hundred, then add to estimate $148 + 291 + 304$.
questions.solution: 148 rounds to 100, 291 rounds to 300 and 304 rounds to 300. The estimate is $100 + 300 + 300 = 700$.

questions.skill: Estimate a sum or difference by rounding
questions.stem: Which number sentence shows an estimate of $346 + 528$ made by rounding each number to the nearest hundred?
questions.solution: 346 rounds to 300 (the tens digit 4 is less than 5) and 528 rounds to 500 (the tens digit 2 is less than 5). The estimate is $300 + 500 = 800$. The other choices round to the nearest ten or round 346 up.

questions.skill: Estimate the answer to a story
questions.stem: A truck carries 304 boxes. It drops off 98 boxes at the first stop and 107 boxes at the second stop. Round each number to the nearest hundred. About how many boxes are still on the truck?
questions.solution: 304 rounds to 300, 98 rounds to 100 and 107 rounds to 100. The estimate is $300 - 100 - 100 = 100$ boxes.

questions.skill: Estimate the answer to a story
questions.stem: A farm picked 386 apples on Monday and 214 apples on Tuesday. It packed 290 apples into boxes. Round each number to the nearest ten. About how many apples are not packed yet?
questions.solution: 386 rounds to 390, 214 rounds to 210 and 290 stays 290. The estimate is $390 + 210 - 290 = 310$. The choice 300 rounds to the nearest hundred instead, 600 forgets the packed apples, and 910 adds them.

solve.work: Nearest ten: 386 -> 390, 214 -> 210, 290 -> 290; 390 + 210 - 290 = 310. (Exact is also 310; nearest hundred would give 300.)

questions.skill: Estimate a product by rounding
questions.stem: A group has 100 dollars. Each ticket costs 19 dollars, and the group buys 4 tickets. Round 19 to the nearest ten. About how many dollars does the group have left?
questions.solution: 19 rounds to 20. Four tickets cost about $4 \times 20 = 80$ dollars. The group has about $100 - 80 = 20$ dollars left.

questions.skill: Check whether an answer is reasonable
questions.stem: Without finding exact answers, which expression has an answer closest to 400?
questions.solution: Round each number: $98 \times 4$ is about $100 \times 4 = 400$. The others are about $50 \times 4 = 200$, $20 \times 4 = 80$ and $25 \times 4 = 100$, which are much farther from 400.

solve.work: 25x4 = 100, 52x4 is about 200, 19x4 is about 80, 98x4 is about 100x4 = 400. Closest: 98 x 4.

questions.skill: Choose the equation or expression for a story
questions.stem: Jo has 3 bags with 8 marbles in each bag. He gives away $g$ marbles and has 17 marbles left. Which equation matches the story?
questions.solution: Jo starts with $3 \times 8$ marbles, gives away $g$, and has 17 left: $3 \times 8 - g = 17$.

solve.work: 3 x 8 = 24 marbles, gives away g, 17 left: 3 x 8 - g = 17 (g = 7).

questions.skill: Choose the equation or expression for a story
questions.stem: Which story matches the expression $4 \times 6 - 5$?
choices: Four bags hold 6 apples each, and 5 more apples are added.
Four bags hold 5 apples each, and then 6 apples are eaten.
Four bags hold 6 apples each, and 5 more bags are added.
Four bags hold 6 apples each, and then 5 apples are eaten.
questions.answer: Four bags hold 6 apples each, and then 5 apples are eaten.
questions.solution: $4 \times 6$ is 4 bags of 6 apples, and subtracting 5 means 5 apples are taken away or eaten.

solve.answer: Four bags hold 6 apples each, and then 5 apples are eaten.
solve.work: 4 x 6 = four bags of 6; - 5 = five apples taken away (eaten).

questions.skill: Find a missing amount in a two-step story
questions.stem: Lia has 4 bags with 7 beads in each bag. She gives some beads to a friend and has 19 beads left. How many beads did she give away?
questions.solution: Lia started with $4 \times 7 = 28$ beads. She gave away $28 - 19 = 9$ beads. The choice 47 adds 28 and 19, 23 adds 4 and 19, and 12 subtracts 7 from 19.

questions.skill: Find a missing amount in a two-step story
questions.stem: Sam had some stickers. He got 6 more stickers and then gave 4 stickers to his sister. Now he has 20 stickers. How many stickers did Sam have at the start?
questions.solution: Work backward. Before giving 4 away he had $20 + 4 = 24$. Before getting 6 more he had $24 - 6 = 18$ stickers.

questions.skill: Find a missing amount in a two-step story
questions.stem: Nate had 52 dollars. He bought a hat for 18 dollars and a book. Now he has 9 dollars left. How many dollars did the book cost?
questions.solution: After the hat Nate had $52 - 18 = 34$ dollars. He has 9 dollars left, so the book cost $34 - 9 = 25$ dollars. Check: $18 + 25 + 9 = 52$.

questions.skill: Decide what to find first, or decide with the total
questions.stem: Sue has 10 dollars. She wants to buy 3 pens that cost 2 dollars each and a notebook that costs 5 dollars. Does she have enough money?
choices: Yes, she will have 1 dollar left
questions.solution: The pens cost $3 \times 2 = 6$ dollars. With the notebook the total is $6 + 5 = 11$ dollars. Sue has 10 dollars, so she is $11 - 10 = 1$ dollar short.

solve.work: Pens 3 x 2 = 6; plus notebook 5 = 11 dollars; 11 - 10 = 1, so she needs 1 more dollar.

questions.skill: Unit fraction of a whole
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Mia eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza did she eat?
questions.solution: The pizza has 8 equal slices, so each slice is $\frac{1}{8}$ of the pizza. Mia ate 1 slice, so she ate $\frac{1}{8}$.

solve.work: 1 of 8 equal slices is 1/8 of the pizza.

questions.skill: Numerator counts shaded parts (area model in words)
questions.stem: A rectangle is cut into 6 equal parts. 5 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: The rectangle has 6 equal parts, so each part is $\frac{1}{6}$. 5 parts are shaded, so $\frac{5}{6}$ is shaded.

questions.skill: A whole as a fraction
questions.stem: A pie is cut into 4 equal pieces. Which fraction shows all of the pie?
questions.solution: Each piece is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the pie. All 4 pieces together are $\frac{4}{4}$, which is 1 whole pie.

solve.work: All 4 of 4 equal pieces: 4/4 = 1 whole. 4/1 would be 4 whole pies.

questions.skill: Unit fraction: one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: A ribbon is cut into 3 equal pieces. What fraction of the ribbon is one piece?
questions.solution: The ribbon has 3 equal pieces, so one piece is $\frac{1}{3}$ of it. The fraction $\frac{3}{3}$ is the whole ribbon.

questions.skill: Unit fraction: one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: A garden is split into 6 equal sections. One section has tomatoes. What fraction of the garden has tomatoes? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: The garden has 6 equal sections and 1 of them has tomatoes, so the fraction is $\frac{1}{6}$.

questions.skill: Unit fraction: one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: A square sheet of paper is folded into 4 equal parts. Which fraction names one of the parts?
questions.solution: The whole is split into 4 equal parts, so one part is $\frac{1}{4}$. The fraction $\frac{3}{4}$ names three of the parts.

questions.skill: Meaning of the numerator and the denominator
questions.stem: A whole is split into equal parts, and each part is $\frac{1}{6}$ of the whole. How many equal parts make the whole?
questions.solution: The 6 in $\frac{1}{6}$ tells how many equal parts make the whole, so the whole has 6 parts.

solve.work: Each part is 1/6, so 6 parts make the whole.

questions.skill: Meaning of the numerator and the denominator
questions.stem: A shape is cut into equal parts, and $\frac{3}{8}$ of it is shaded. What does the 8 tell you?
questions.solution: The denominator, 8, tells how many equal parts the whole is cut into. The numerator, 3, tells how many are shaded.

solve.work: The denominator 8 is the number of equal parts in the whole.

questions.skill: Fraction shown by the shaded parts of a shape
questions.stem: A rectangle is split into 4 equal parts and 3 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: 3 of the 4 equal parts are shaded, so $\frac{3}{4}$ of the rectangle is shaded.

questions.skill: Fraction shown by the shaded parts of a shape
questions.stem: A circle is split into 3 equal parts and 2 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the circle is shaded?
questions.solution: 2 of the 3 equal parts are shaded, so the fraction is $\frac{2}{3}$. The fraction $\frac{1}{3}$ names the part that is not shaded.

questions.skill: Fraction shown by the shaded parts of a shape
questions.stem: A strip is cut into 8 equal pieces. Four of the pieces are painted blue. What fraction of the strip is painted blue? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: 4 of the 8 equal pieces are blue, so the fraction is $\frac{4}{8}$ (which is the same as one half).

solve.issues: Answer 4/8 equals 1/2, the very example in "Write your answer like 1/2"; grading must accept 1/2 (compare by value).

questions.skill: Fraction at a point on a number line
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 4 equal parts. A point is at the 3rd mark after 0. What fraction names the point? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: Each part is $\frac{1}{4}$. The 3rd mark after 0 is 3 parts from 0, so it is at $\frac{3}{4}$.

questions.skill: Fraction at a point on a number line
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 2 equal parts. What fraction names the point exactly in the middle?
questions.solution: The middle point is 1 of the 2 equal parts from 0, so it is at $\frac{1}{2}$. The fraction $\frac{2}{2}$ is the end point, 1.

questions.skill: Fraction at a point on a number line
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 3 equal parts. Zoe puts a dot on the 1st mark after 0. What fraction names her dot? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: Each part of the line is $\frac{1}{3}$ long. The 1st mark after 0 is 1 part from 0, so it is at $\frac{1}{3}$.

questions.skill: Build a fraction from unit fractions
questions.stem: A fraction is made of 3 pieces that are each $\frac{1}{4}$ of a whole. What fraction is it? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: 3 pieces that are each $\frac{1}{4}$ make $\frac{3}{4}$.

questions.skill: Build a fraction from unit fractions
questions.stem: How many pieces that are each $\frac{1}{8}$ make $\frac{5}{8}$?
questions.solution: $\frac{5}{8}$ is made of 5 pieces that are each $\frac{1}{8}$. The choice 8 is the number of pieces in the whole.

questions.skill: A whole as a fraction, and fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: A candy bar is broken into 6 equal pieces. Tom eats all 6 pieces. What fraction of the bar did he eat?
questions.solution: He ate 6 of the 6 equal pieces, which is the whole bar. The fraction is $\frac{6}{6}$, which equals 1.

questions.skill: A whole as a fraction, and fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: What number goes in the box to make the equation true? $\frac{\square}{3} = 1$
questions.solution: A whole cut into 3 equal parts has 3 parts, so $\frac{3}{3} = 1$. The number is 3.

questions.skill: A whole as a fraction, and fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to 1 whole?
questions.solution: When the numerator and denominator are the same, all the parts are counted, so $\frac{4}{4} = 1$.

solve.work: Numerator equals denominator: 4/4 = 1. Others are less than 1.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions: find the missing number
questions.stem: What number goes in the box to make the fractions equal? $\frac{1}{4} = \frac{\square}{8}$
questions.solution: Cutting each fourth into 2 equal parts makes eighths. One fourth is 2 eighths, so $\frac{1}{4} = \frac{2}{8}$.

solve.work: Fourths to eighths: each fourth is 2 eighths, so 1/4 = 2/8.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions: find the missing number
questions.stem: Sam colors 1 of the 2 equal parts of a bar. Ana has a bar of the same size that is cut into 4 equal parts. How many of Ana's parts must she color to color the same amount as Sam?
questions.solution: One half equals two fourths, so $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{4}$. Ana must color 2 of her parts.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions: find the missing number
questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to $\frac{1}{2}$?
questions.solution: Half of 8 equal parts is 4 parts, so $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{4}{8}$.

questions.skill: Recognize equal fractions
questions.stem: Two bars are the same size. Bar A has 2 of its 4 equal parts colored. Bar B has 1 of its 2 equal parts colored. Which statement is true?
choices: The same amount of each bar is colored.
More of Bar A is colored.
More of Bar B is colored.
questions.answer: The same amount of each bar is colored.
questions.solution: Two fourths and one half name the same amount: $\frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.

solve.answer: The same amount of each bar is colored.
solve.work: Bar A 2/4 = 1/2; Bar B 1/2. Same amount.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: Which fraction is the greatest?
questions.solution: The denominators are all 8, so the one with the most parts is the greatest: $\frac{5}{8}$.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: Dad cuts a pie into 6 equal slices. Ana eats 4 slices and Raj eats 1 slice. Who eats more of the pie?
questions.solution: Ana eats $\frac{4}{6}$ of the pie and Raj eats $\frac{1}{6}$. The slices are the same size, so 4 slices is more than 1 slice.

solve.work: Ana 4/6, Raj 1/6 of the same pie; Ana eats more.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: Lee read $\frac{5}{6}$ of her book. Jo read $\frac{2}{6}$ of his book. The two books are the same length. Write the fraction for the person who read less. Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: Both fractions have sixths, so compare the numerators: 2 is less than 5. Jo read less, $\frac{2}{6}$ of his book.

solve.issues: Equivalent 1/3 must be accepted (compare by value).
solve.work: Same whole, same denominator: 2/6 < 5/6, so Jo read less: 2/6 (= 1/3).

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: Four pizzas of the same size are cut into 2, 4, 6 and 8 equal slices. Which fraction names the biggest single slice?
questions.solution: The fewer the equal slices, the bigger each slice is. A pizza cut into 2 slices has the biggest slices, each $\frac{1}{2}$.

solve.work: Fewer equal slices of the same whole means bigger slices; 2 slices -> 1/2 is biggest.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: Tom cuts a bar into 3 equal pieces. Ana cuts a bar of the same size into 6 equal pieces. Each of them takes 1 piece. Write the fraction that names the bigger piece. Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: Cutting into fewer pieces makes bigger pieces. Tom's piece is $\frac{1}{3}$ and Ana's piece is $\frac{1}{6}$, so $\frac{1}{3}$ is bigger.

solve.work: Same bar; 1/3 > 1/6 since fewer pieces are bigger. Bigger piece: 1/3.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: A cake is shared equally among 2 friends. Another cake of the same size is shared equally among 8 friends. Who gets the bigger share?
choices: A friend in the group of 2
A friend in the group of 8
The shares are the same size
questions.answer: A friend in the group of 2
questions.solution: Each friend in the group of 2 gets $\frac{1}{2}$ of a cake and each friend in the group of 8 gets $\frac{1}{8}$ of a cake. One half is bigger than one eighth.

solve.answer: A friend in the group of 2
solve.work: 1/2 of a cake > 1/8 of a same-size cake: a friend in the group of 2.

questions.skill: Compare a fraction with one half and one whole
questions.stem: Which fraction is less than $\frac{1}{2}$?
questions.solution: One fourth is less than half of the whole. The others, $\frac{3}{4}$, $\frac{2}{3}$ and $\frac{5}{6}$, are each more than half.

questions.skill: Compare a fraction with one half and one whole
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Leo eats 4 slices. How does the part Leo ate compare to $\frac{1}{2}$ of the pizza?
choices: It is less than $\frac{1}{2}$ of the pizza
It is equal to $\frac{1}{2}$ of the pizza
It is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$ of the pizza
It is equal to 1 whole pizza
questions.answer: It is equal to $\frac{1}{2}$ of the pizza
questions.solution: 4 of the 8 equal slices is half of the pizza, so $\frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}$.

solve.answer: It is equal to $\frac{1}{2}$ of the pizza

questions.skill: Put fractions in order
questions.stem: Which list puts $\frac{5}{8}$, $\frac{1}{8}$ and $\frac{3}{8}$ in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: All are eighths, so order the numerators 1, 3, 5 from least to greatest.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the symbols <, > and =
questions.stem: Choose the true statement about $\frac{2}{3}$ and $\frac{1}{3}$.
questions.solution: Both fractions are thirds, and 2 thirds is more than 1 third, so $\frac{2}{3} > \frac{1}{3}$.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions
questions.stem: What number makes $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\square}{6}$ true?
questions.solution: Cut each half into 3 equal parts. The whole has 2 halves, which is 6 sixths. So 1 half is 3 sixths, and $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{6}$.

questions.skill: Compare to one half
questions.stem: Which fraction is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$?
questions.solution: Half of 4 fourths is 2 fourths, so $\frac{3}{4}$ is more than $\frac{1}{2}$. Half of 8 eighths is 4 eighths, so $\frac{3}{8}$ is less than $\frac{1}{2}$. And $\frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{1}{4}$ are less than half.

questions.skill: Fraction at a point on a number line (in words)
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 8 equal parts. A point is on the 5th mark after 0. What fraction names the point? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: Each part of the number line is $\frac{1}{8}$ long. The 5th mark after 0 is 5 of those parts from 0, so the point is at $\frac{5}{8}$.

solve.work: Each part is 1/8; the 5th mark after 0 is 5/8.

questions.skill: Unit fraction: one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: Four friends share a sandwich so that each friend gets an equal part. What fraction of the sandwich does each friend get? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: The sandwich is shared in 4 equal parts, so each friend gets one part, which is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the sandwich.

questions.skill: Unit fraction: one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: Which of these fractions is a unit fraction?
questions.solution: A unit fraction has a numerator of 1. Only $\frac{1}{8}$ has a numerator of 1.

questions.skill: Meaning of the numerator and the denominator
questions.stem: A pie is cut into 8 equal slices. $\frac{3}{8}$ of the pie has been eaten. How many slices have not been eaten?
questions.solution: The pie has 8 slices and 3 have been eaten. The slices not eaten are $8 - 3 = 5$.

questions.skill: Meaning of the numerator and the denominator
questions.stem: A bar is cut into 6 equal parts. Kim colors 4 of them. Which fraction names the colored part?
questions.solution: 4 of the 6 equal parts are colored, so the fraction is $\frac{4}{6}$. The numerator counts the colored parts and the denominator counts all the parts.

questions.skill: Fraction shown by the shaded parts of a shape
questions.stem: A square is cut into 6 equal parts. 1 part is red, 2 parts are blue, and the rest are white. What fraction of the square is white?
questions.solution: The red and blue parts are $1 + 2 = 3$ parts, so $6 - 3 = 3$ parts are white. The fraction is $\frac{3}{6}$.

questions.skill: Fraction shown by the shaded parts of a shape
questions.stem: A garden bed is divided into 8 equal sections. Tomatoes grow in 3 sections, peppers grow in 2 sections, and the rest of the sections have beans. What fraction of the garden bed has beans? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: Tomatoes and peppers use $3 + 2 = 5$ sections, so $8 - 5 = 3$ sections have beans. The fraction is $\frac{3}{8}$.

questions.skill: Fraction shown by the shaded parts of a shape
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Max eats 2 slices and Nia eats 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza did the two children eat in all?
questions.solution: Together they ate $2 + 3 = 5$ of the 8 equal slices, which is $\frac{5}{8}$. The denominator stays 8 because the slices are still eighths.

questions.skill: Fraction at a point on a number line
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 6 equal parts. Which fraction names the point that is 4 parts from 0?
questions.solution: Each part is $\frac{1}{6}$. A point 4 parts from 0 is at $\frac{4}{6}$. The fraction $\frac{2}{6}$ would be 2 parts from 0.

questions.skill: Fraction at a point on a number line
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 8 equal parts. A frog starts at 0 and jumps 7 parts to the right. What fraction names where the frog lands? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: Each part is $\frac{1}{8}$. After jumping 7 parts the frog is at $\frac{7}{8}$.

questions.skill: Fraction at a point on a number line
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 6 equal parts. Which fraction names the point exactly halfway between 0 and 1?
questions.solution: Halfway is 3 of the 6 equal parts from 0, so the point is at $\frac{3}{6}$, which is the same as one half.

solve.work: Halfway between 0 and 1 in sixths is 3 parts: 3/6.

questions.skill: Build a fraction from unit fractions
questions.stem: Mia has 7 pieces of ribbon. Each piece is $\frac{1}{8}$ of a whole ribbon. She puts all the pieces together. What fraction of a whole ribbon is that? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: 7 pieces that are each $\frac{1}{8}$ make $\frac{7}{8}$ of a whole ribbon.

questions.skill: Build a fraction from unit fractions
questions.stem: Which tells how $\frac{5}{6}$ is made?
choices: 6 parts that are each $\frac{1}{5}$ of a whole
5 parts that are each $\frac{1}{6}$ of a whole
5 parts that are each $\frac{1}{5}$ of a whole
6 parts that are each $\frac{1}{6}$ of a whole
questions.answer: 5 parts that are each $\frac{1}{6}$ of a whole
questions.solution: $\frac{5}{6}$ is 5 copies of the unit fraction $\frac{1}{6}$. Six parts that are each $\frac{1}{6}$ would make a whole.

solve.answer: 5 parts that are each $\frac{1}{6}$ of a whole

questions.skill: A whole as a fraction, and fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: Each pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. The class eats 16 slices. How many whole pizzas did the class eat?
questions.solution: Each pizza has 8 slices. $16 \div 8 = 2$, so the class ate 2 pizzas. In fractions, $\frac{16}{8} = 2$.

solve.work: 8 slices per pizza; 16 = 8 + 8, so 2 whole pizzas (16/8 = 2).

questions.skill: A whole as a fraction, and fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: What whole number is equal to $\frac{8}{4}$?
questions.solution: $\frac{8}{4}$ means 8 fourths. Every 4 fourths make 1 whole, so 8 fourths make 2 wholes.

questions.skill: A whole as a fraction, and fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: Which list has only fractions that are equal to 1?
questions.solution: A fraction equals 1 when its numerator and denominator are the same. In the first list $\frac{3}{3}$, $\frac{2}{2}$ and $\frac{8}{8}$ all do. $\frac{3}{4}$ does not, and $\frac{2}{1}$, $\frac{3}{1}$ and $\frac{8}{1}$ are 2, 3 and 8.

solve.work: 2/2, 3/3, 8/8 each equal 1. First list equals 2, 3, 8; second are unit fractions; third has 3/4.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions: find the missing number
questions.stem: Find the missing number: $\frac{2}{3} = \frac{\square}{6}$
questions.solution: Each third is cut into 2 equal parts, so 3 parts become 6 parts and 2 parts become 4 parts. So $\frac{2}{3} = \frac{4}{6}$.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions: find the missing number
questions.stem: Fill in the box to complete the equal fractions: $\frac{3}{4} = \frac{6}{\square}$
questions.solution: The numerator went from 3 to 6, which is doubled, so double the denominator too: $4 \times 2 = 8$. So $\frac{3}{4} = \frac{6}{8}$.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions: find the missing number
questions.stem: Lia uses 2 of the 4 equal pieces of a ribbon. Sam has a ribbon of the same length cut into 8 equal pieces. How many of Sam's pieces equal the amount Lia used?
questions.solution: Each of Lia's pieces is 2 of Sam's pieces. So 2 pieces of Lia's equal $2 \times 2 = 4$ of Sam's pieces, and $\frac{2}{4} = \frac{4}{8}$.

questions.skill: Recognize equal fractions
questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to $\frac{2}{3}$?
questions.solution: Cutting each third into 2 parts makes sixths, and 2 thirds become 4 sixths: $\frac{2}{3} = \frac{4}{6}$.

questions.skill: Recognize equal fractions
questions.stem: Which fraction is not equal to $\frac{1}{2}$?
questions.solution: $\frac{2}{4}$, $\frac{3}{6}$ and $\frac{4}{8}$ are each half of their whole. Half of 8 is 4, so $\frac{3}{8}$ is less than one half.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: Which fraction is greater than $\frac{5}{8}$?
questions.solution: All the fractions are eighths, so compare the numerators. Only 7 is greater than 5.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: What whole number goes in the box to make this true? $\frac{4}{6} < \frac{\square}{6} < \frac{6}{6}$
questions.solution: The box must be a number greater than 4 and less than 6. The only whole number is 5.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: Mia ran $\frac{3}{6}$ of a track, Raj ran $\frac{5}{6}$ of it, and Ty ran $\frac{1}{6}$ of it. The track is the same for all three. Who ran the farthest?
choices: They all ran the same distance
questions.solution: All the distances are in sixths, so compare numerators: 5 is greater than 3 and 1. Raj ran the farthest.

solve.work: Same track, sixths: 5/6 is greatest, so Raj.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: Lena ate $\frac{3}{8}$ of a pizza. Max ate $\frac{3}{4}$ of a pizza of the same size. Who ate more?
questions.solution: Both ate 3 slices, but fourths are bigger than eighths. So 3 fourths is more than 3 eighths and Max ate more.

solve.work: Same numerator 3; fourths are bigger than eighths, so 3/4 > 3/8 (3/4 = 6/8). Max.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: Two bars are the same size. Bar X has 2 of its 3 equal parts colored. Bar Y has 2 of its 6 equal parts colored. Write the fraction that names the bar with less colored. Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: Both have 2 parts colored, but sixths are smaller than thirds. So $\frac{2}{6}$ is less than $\frac{2}{3}$.

solve.issues: Equivalent 1/3 must be accepted (compare by value).
solve.work: X = 2/3, Y = 2/6. Same numerator; sixths smaller, so Y has less: 2/6 (= 1/3).

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: These fractions all have a numerator of 3. Which fraction is the least?
questions.solution: With the same numerator, the larger the denominator, the smaller the parts. Eighths are the smallest parts, so $\frac{3}{8}$ is the least.

solve.work: Same numerator; largest denominator gives least: 3/8.

questions.skill: Compare a fraction with one half and one whole
questions.stem: How many of these fractions are greater than $\frac{1}{2}$? $\frac{1}{3}$, $\frac{3}{4}$, $\frac{3}{8}$, $\frac{5}{6}$, $\frac{4}{8}$, $\frac{2}{3}$
questions.solution: The fractions greater than one half are $\frac{3}{4}$, $\frac{5}{6}$ and $\frac{2}{3}$. The fractions $\frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{3}{8}$ are less than one half, and $\frac{4}{8}$ equals one half.

questions.skill: Compare a fraction with one half and one whole
questions.stem: Which fraction is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$ and less than 1?
questions.solution: $\frac{5}{6}$ is more than half (half is $\frac{3}{6}$) and less than the whole. $\frac{1}{3}$ is less than half, $\frac{4}{8}$ equals half, and $\frac{6}{6}$ equals 1.

questions.skill: Put fractions in order
questions.stem: Which list puts $\frac{3}{6}$, $\frac{3}{4}$ and $\frac{3}{8}$ in order from greatest to least?
questions.solution: The numerators are the same, so the fraction with the biggest parts is the greatest. Fourths are bigger than sixths, which are bigger than eighths.

solve.work: Same numerator; smaller denominator is greater: 3/4 > 3/6 > 3/8.

questions.skill: Put fractions in order
questions.stem: Ann ate $\frac{2}{6}$ of a pizza, Bo ate $\frac{5}{6}$ of a pizza and Cy ate $\frac{3}{6}$ of a pizza. The pizzas are the same size. What fraction did the child who ate the middle amount eat? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: In order from least to greatest the fractions are $\frac{2}{6}$, $\frac{3}{6}$, $\frac{5}{6}$. The middle one is $\frac{3}{6}$.

solve.issues: Equivalent 1/2 (also the hint's example) must be accepted (compare by value).

questions.skill: Equal pair of fractions
questions.stem: Which pair of fractions is equal?
questions.solution: Split each third into 2 equal parts: the whole has 6 equal parts, and 2 thirds becomes 4 sixths. So $\frac{2}{3} = \frac{4}{6}$. In the other pairs the denominators are different but the numerators are the same, so the fractions are not equal.

questions.skill: A fraction equal to a whole number
questions.stem: Each sandwich is cut into 4 equal pieces. Lee eats 8 pieces. How many sandwiches did Lee eat?
questions.solution: 4 pieces make 1 sandwich, so $\frac{4}{4} = 1$. 8 pieces make 2 sandwiches, so $\frac{8}{4} = 2$.

solve.work: 4 pieces make one sandwich; 8 pieces = 8/4 = 2 sandwiches.

questions.skill: Order unit fractions
questions.stem: Which list puts $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{1}{8}$ in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: When the top number is 1, the more parts the whole is cut into, the smaller each part is. Eighths are the smallest, then fourths, then halves. The order is $\frac{1}{8}, \frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{2}$.

solve.work: Same numerator: more parts means smaller parts. 1/8 < 1/4 < 1/2.

questions.skill: Unit fraction: one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: Which shows $\frac{1}{4}$ of a pizza eaten?
choices: A pizza cut into 4 slices of different sizes, with 1 slice eaten
A pizza cut into 3 equal slices, with 1 slice eaten
A pizza cut into 4 equal slices, with 1 slice eaten
A pizza cut into 4 equal slices, with 3 slices eaten
questions.answer: A pizza cut into 4 equal slices, with 1 slice eaten
questions.solution: The parts must be equal. $\frac{1}{4}$ means 1 of 4 equal parts. Unequal slices, 3 equal slices, or 3 slices eaten do not make $\frac{1}{4}$.

solve.answer: A pizza cut into 4 equal slices, with 1 slice eaten
solve.work: 1/4 needs 4 EQUAL parts with 1 taken. Unequal slices or 3 slices do not show 1/4; 3 of 4 eaten is 3/4.

questions.skill: Meaning of the numerator and the denominator
questions.stem: A rectangle is cut into equal parts. 5 parts are shaded and 3 parts are not shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: The rectangle has $5 + 3 = 8$ equal parts in all. 5 of them are shaded, so the fraction is $\frac{5}{8}$.

questions.skill: Meaning of the numerator and the denominator
questions.stem: Pam colored $\frac{2}{3}$ of a ribbon. Which statement describes the ribbon?
choices: It was cut into 2 equal parts and 3 parts were colored
It was cut into 5 equal parts and 2 parts were colored
It was cut into 3 equal parts and 3 parts were colored
It was cut into 3 equal parts and 2 parts were colored
questions.answer: It was cut into 3 equal parts and 2 parts were colored
questions.solution: In $\frac{2}{3}$ the denominator 3 is the number of equal parts and the numerator 2 is the number of colored parts.

solve.answer: It was cut into 3 equal parts and 2 parts were colored
solve.work: 2/3 means 3 equal parts with 2 of them colored.

questions.skill: Fraction shown by the shaded parts of a shape
questions.stem: A flag is cut into 6 equal stripes. 2 stripes are red, 2 stripes are white and the rest are blue. What fraction of the flag is not blue? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: The red and white stripes are $2 + 2 = 4$ stripes, and these are the stripes that are not blue. The fraction is $\frac{4}{6}$.

solve.issues: Equivalent 2/3 must be accepted (compare by value).

questions.skill: Fraction shown by the shaded parts of a shape
questions.stem: A chocolate bar has 8 equal squares. Pia eats 3 squares. Later she eats 2 more squares. What fraction of the bar is left?
questions.solution: Pia eats $3 + 2 = 5$ squares, so $8 - 5 = 3$ squares are left. The fraction left is $\frac{3}{8}$. The fraction $\frac{5}{8}$ is the part she ate.

questions.skill: Fraction at a point on a number line
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 8 equal parts. Point A is at $\frac{3}{8}$ and point B is at $\frac{7}{8}$. How many equal parts are between point A and point B?
questions.solution: Point A is 3 parts from 0 and point B is 7 parts from 0. They are $7 - 3 = 4$ parts apart.

solve.work: From 3/8 to 7/8 is 7 - 3 = 4 eighths, i.e. 4 equal parts.

questions.skill: Fraction at a point on a number line
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 6 equal parts. A point is exactly 1 part to the left of 1. Which fraction names the point?
questions.solution: The point 1 is 6 parts from 0. One part to the left is 5 parts from 0, so the point is at $\frac{5}{6}$.

solve.work: 1 = 6/6; one part to the left is 5/6.

questions.skill: Build a fraction from unit fractions
questions.stem: A whole is made of 6 pieces that are each $\frac{1}{6}$. Mia takes 4 pieces and her brother takes 1 piece. What fraction of the whole is left? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: The pieces taken are $4 + 1 = 5$, so $6 - 5 = 1$ piece is left. That piece is $\frac{1}{6}$ of the whole.

questions.skill: Build a fraction from unit fractions
questions.stem: Ken has 5 pieces that are each $\frac{1}{8}$ of a whole. How many more pieces that are each $\frac{1}{8}$ does he need to make exactly 1 whole?
questions.solution: A whole is 8 pieces that are each $\frac{1}{8}$. Ken has 5, so he needs $8 - 5 = 3$ more.

questions.skill: A whole as a fraction, and fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: A cook cuts each pizza into 6 equal slices. Each slice is $\frac{1}{6}$ of a pizza. How many slices make 3 whole pizzas?
questions.solution: Each whole pizza is 6 slices. Three pizzas are $3 \times 6 = 18$ slices. In fractions, $\frac{18}{6} = 3$.

questions.skill: A whole as a fraction, and fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to 3?
questions.solution: $\frac{12}{4}$ means 12 fourths, and every 4 fourths make 1 whole, so $12 \div 4 = 3$. The others equal 4, one half and 2.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions: find the missing number
questions.stem: Which number makes this equation true? $\frac{3}{6} = \frac{\square}{2}$
questions.solution: Six sixths make the whole, so half of the whole is 3 sixths. Half of the whole is also 1 of 2 equal parts, so $\frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$ and the box holds 1.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions: find the missing number
questions.stem: Use what you know about equal fractions to find the missing number: $\frac{6}{8} = \frac{\square}{4}$
questions.solution: Two eighths make one fourth. So 6 eighths make $6 \div 2 = 3$ fourths, and $\frac{6}{8} = \frac{3}{4}$.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions: find the missing number
questions.stem: Kai ate $\frac{2}{6}$ of a sandwich. Another sandwich of the same size is cut into 3 equal parts. How many of those parts would Kai need to eat to have the same amount?
questions.solution: Two sixths equal one third, so $\frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$. Kai would need 1 of the 3 equal parts.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions: find the missing number
questions.stem: Fill in the missing denominator: $\frac{4}{8} = \frac{2}{\square}$
questions.solution: The numerator went from 4 to 2, which is cut in half, so halve the denominator too: $8 \div 2 = 4$. So $\frac{4}{8} = \frac{2}{4}$.

questions.skill: Recognize equal fractions
questions.stem: Which statement is true?
questions.solution: Doubling the parts doubles both numbers of $\frac{2}{3}$ to give $\frac{4}{6}$. Fractions with the same numerator but different denominators, such as $\frac{3}{4}$ and $\frac{3}{8}$, are not equal.

questions.skill: Recognize equal fractions
questions.stem: Dev cuts a sandwich into 6 equal pieces and eats 4 of them. Ana has a sandwich of the same size cut into 3 equal pieces. How many of Ana's pieces must she eat to eat the same amount as Dev?
questions.solution: Dev ate $\frac{4}{6}$ of a sandwich. Two sixths make one third, so $\frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$. Ana must eat 2 of her 3 pieces.

solve.work: Dev ate 4/6 = 2/3, so Ana eats 2 of her 3 pieces.

questions.skill: Recognize equal fractions
questions.stem: Which set shows three names for the same amount?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{2}{4}$ and $\frac{4}{8}$ are all one half. In each other set one fraction does not match: $\frac{4}{6}$ is two thirds, not one half; $\frac{3}{8}$ is not equal to $\frac{1}{3}$; and $\frac{4}{8}$ is one half, not three fourths.

solve.work: 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8 all same. Others: 3/8 is not 1/3; 4/8 is not 3/4; 4/6 is not 1/2.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: How many of these fractions are greater than $\frac{3}{8}$? $\frac{1}{8}$, $\frac{4}{8}$, $\frac{7}{8}$, $\frac{3}{8}$, $\frac{5}{8}$, $\frac{2}{8}$
questions.solution: The numerators greater than 3 are 4, 7 and 5. So 3 of the fractions are greater than $\frac{3}{8}$. The fraction $\frac{3}{8}$ itself is not greater than $\frac{3}{8}$.

solve.work: Greater than 3/8: 4/8, 7/8, 5/8 (3/8 itself is not greater). Count 3.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: A fraction has a denominator of 8. It is greater than $\frac{3}{8}$ and less than $\frac{5}{8}$. What is the fraction? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: The numerator must be greater than 3 and less than 5, so it is 4. The fraction is $\frac{4}{8}$.

solve.issues: 4/8 equals 1/2, the example in the answer hint; a child typing 1/2 has the right value, so grading should compare by value.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: Bar A is cut into 3 equal parts. Bar B is the same size as Bar A and is cut into 6 equal parts. Which statement is true?
choices: Each part of Bar B is smaller than each part of Bar A.
Each part of Bar B is larger than each part of Bar A.
Each part of Bar B is the same size as each part of Bar A.
Bar B is longer than Bar A.
questions.answer: Each part of Bar B is smaller than each part of Bar A.
questions.solution: Cutting the same whole into more parts makes smaller parts. Sixths are smaller than thirds.

solve.answer: Each part of Bar B is smaller than each part of Bar A.
solve.work: Same size bars; more parts means smaller parts. 1/6 < 1/3.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: How many of the fractions $\frac{2}{2}$, $\frac{2}{3}$, $\frac{2}{4}$ and $\frac{2}{8}$ are less than $\frac{2}{3}$?
questions.solution: All have a numerator of 2, so compare the sizes of the parts. Fourths and eighths are smaller than thirds, so $\frac{2}{4}$ and $\frac{2}{8}$ are less than $\frac{2}{3}$. The fraction $\frac{2}{2}$ is greater, and $\frac{2}{3}$ is not less than itself.

solve.work: Same numerator 2: 2/2 = 1 is greater; 2/3 is equal, not less; 2/4 and 2/8 are less. Count 2.

questions.skill: Compare a fraction with one half and one whole
questions.stem: Sam says that $\frac{3}{8}$ is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$ because 3 is greater than 1. Which statement is correct?
choices: $\frac{3}{8}$ is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$, because 8 is greater than 2
$\frac{3}{8}$ is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$, because it has more parts
$\frac{3}{8}$ is less than $\frac{1}{2}$, because $\frac{1}{2}$ is equal to $\frac{4}{8}$
$\frac{3}{8}$ is equal to $\frac{1}{2}$, because both are less than 1
questions.answer: $\frac{3}{8}$ is less than $\frac{1}{2}$, because $\frac{1}{2}$ is equal to $\frac{4}{8}$
questions.solution: The numerator and denominator must be compared together. One half equals four eighths, and 3 eighths is less than 4 eighths. So $\frac{3}{8}$ is less than $\frac{1}{2}$.

solve.answer: $\frac{3}{8}$ is less than $\frac{1}{2}$, because $\frac{1}{2}$ is equal to $\frac{4}{8}$

questions.skill: Compare a fraction with one half and one whole
questions.stem: A fraction has a denominator of 8. It is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$ and less than $\frac{6}{8}$. What is its numerator?
questions.solution: One half equals $\frac{4}{8}$. The numerator must be greater than 4 and less than 6, so it is 5.

questions.skill: Put fractions in order
questions.stem: Which list shows $\frac{1}{6}$, $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{1}{3}$ in order from greatest to least?
questions.solution: For unit fractions, the smaller the denominator, the bigger the fraction. So the order from greatest to least is $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{3}$, $\frac{1}{4}$, $\frac{1}{6}$.

solve.work: Unit fractions: smaller denominator is greater. 1/2 > 1/3 > 1/4 > 1/6.

questions.skill: Put fractions in order
questions.stem: Write the second greatest of these fractions: $\frac{3}{8}$, $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{7}{8}$ and $\frac{5}{8}$. Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: One half equals $\frac{4}{8}$. In order from least to greatest: $\frac{3}{8}$, $\frac{4}{8}$ (one half), $\frac{5}{8}$, $\frac{7}{8}$. The second greatest is $\frac{5}{8}$.

questions.skill: Put fractions in order
questions.stem: Three runners ran parts of a track of the same length. Dee ran $\frac{5}{6}$ of it, Eli ran $\frac{1}{3}$ of it and Flo ran $\frac{1}{2}$ of it. Which list shows the runners from the shortest distance to the longest?
questions.solution: One third is less than one half, and five sixths is more than one half (one half is $\frac{3}{6}$). So the order is $\frac{1}{3}$ (Eli), $\frac{1}{2}$ (Flo), $\frac{5}{6}$ (Dee).

solve.work: In sixths: Eli 1/3 = 2/6, Flo 1/2 = 3/6, Dee 5/6. Shortest to longest: Eli, Flo, Dee.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the symbols <, > and =
questions.stem: Which comparison is true?
questions.solution: Three sixths is half of the whole, so $\frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$. The others are false: $\frac{3}{4} = \frac{6}{8}$ is greater than $\frac{5}{8}$, thirds are bigger than fourths, and eighths are smaller than sixths.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the symbols <, > and =
questions.stem: One of these four comparisons is false. Which one?
questions.solution: With the same numerator, sixths are bigger than eighths, so $\frac{4}{6} > \frac{4}{8}$ and the statement $\frac{4}{6} < \frac{4}{8}$ is false. The other three are true.

solve.work: 4/6 > 4/8 (same numerator, sixths bigger), so '4/6 < 4/8' is false. 3/8 < 4/8 = 1/2 true; 2/4 = 4/8 true; 5/6 > 5/8 true.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the symbols <, > and =
questions.stem: How many of these four statements are true? $\frac{1}{4} < \frac{1}{3}$, $\frac{6}{8} > \frac{3}{4}$, $\frac{4}{4} = \frac{8}{8}$, $\frac{1}{2} > \frac{5}{8}$
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{4} < \frac{1}{3}$ is true. $\frac{6}{8} > \frac{3}{4}$ is false because $\frac{6}{8} = \frac{3}{4}$. $\frac{4}{4} = \frac{8}{8}$ is true because both equal 1. $\frac{1}{2} > \frac{5}{8}$ is false because $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{4}{8}$. So 2 are true.

questions.skill: Name parallel lines
questions.stem: Two lines on a page never cross, no matter how far they go. What are these lines called?
questions.solution: Lines that stay the same distance apart and never cross are parallel lines. Perpendicular lines cross at a square corner, and intersecting lines cross.

solve.work: Lines in one plane that never meet are parallel lines.

questions.skill: Right angles in a rectangle
questions.stem: How many right angles does a rectangle have?
questions.solution: Every corner of a rectangle is a square corner (a right angle). A rectangle has 4 corners, so it has 4 right angles.

solve.work: A rectangle has 4 right angles, one at each corner.

questions.skill: Name a right angle
questions.stem: An angle makes a square corner, like the corner of a book. What kind of angle is it?
questions.solution: An angle that makes a square corner is a right angle.

solve.work: A square corner is a right angle.

questions.skill: Points, lines and line segments
questions.stem: Which word names an exact spot that has no length and no width?
questions.solution: A point shows an exact place. A line and a line segment both have length, and an angle is made by two lines meeting.

solve.work: An exact location with no length or width is a point. A line and segment have length; an angle is two rays.

questions.skill: Points, lines and line segments
questions.stem: How many endpoints does a line segment have?
questions.solution: A line segment is a straight piece with a beginning and an end, so it has 2 endpoints.

solve.work: A line segment has two endpoints, one at each end.

questions.skill: Points, lines and line segments
questions.stem: Mia draws a straight path from point A to point B and stops at each of those points. What did she draw?
questions.solution: A straight path that starts at one point and stops at another is a line segment. A line would keep going forever.

solve.work: A straight path that starts at A and stops at B has two endpoints: a line segment.

questions.skill: Points, lines and line segments
questions.stem: Which of these goes on and on forever in both directions?
questions.solution: A line has no endpoints and never stops. A line segment has two endpoints, and a point and a quadrilateral do not go on forever.

solve.work: A line goes on forever in both directions; a segment stops at endpoints.

questions.skill: Points, lines and line segments
questions.stem: Maria draws 3 separate line segments on a page. How many endpoints do the 3 segments have in all?
questions.solution: Each line segment has 2 endpoints. $3 \times 2 = 6$ endpoints.

questions.skill: Points, lines and line segments
questions.stem: Which sentence is true about a line segment?
choices: It goes on forever in both directions.
It always makes a square corner.
questions.solution: A line segment is a straight piece with a start and an end. Because it stops at both ends, it has two endpoints and it can be measured.

solve.work: A segment has two endpoints; it has length, does not go on forever, and makes no corner.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: Which pair is the best example of parallel lines?
choices: the two rails of a straight train track
the two hands of a clock at 3:00
two roads that cross each other
the two edges that meet at a corner of a page
questions.answer: the two rails of a straight train track
questions.solution: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet. The two rails of a straight track do that. The other pairs meet each other.

solve.answer: the two rails of a straight train track
solve.work: Straight train rails never meet and stay the same distance apart: parallel. Page corner edges and clock hands at 3:00 are perpendicular; crossing roads intersect.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: Two parallel lines are drawn on a page and made longer and longer in both directions. What happens to them?
choices: They cross and make a square corner.
questions.solution: Parallel lines always stay the same distance apart, so they never meet, however long they are drawn.

solve.work: Parallel lines never meet, however far they are extended.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: How many pairs of parallel sides does a square have?
questions.solution: The top and bottom sides are parallel, and the left and right sides are parallel. That is 2 pairs.

solve.work: Top/bottom and left/right: 2 pairs of parallel sides.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: Which sentence is true about parallel lines?
choices: They are always the same distance apart.
questions.answer: They are always the same distance apart.
questions.solution: Parallel lines never cross, so the space between them stays the same all the way along.

solve.answer: They are always the same distance apart.
solve.work: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart; they never cross or make corners.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: Which pair is the best example of perpendicular lines?
choices: the two edges that meet at the corner of a sheet of paper
the two long edges of a sheet of paper
the two rails of a straight train track
the top and bottom edges of a door
questions.answer: the two edges that meet at the corner of a sheet of paper
questions.solution: Perpendicular lines meet at a square corner (a right angle). The two edges that meet at a corner of a sheet of paper do that. The other pairs are parallel.

solve.answer: the two edges that meet at the corner of a sheet of paper
solve.work: Edges meeting at a paper's corner form a right angle: perpendicular. The others are parallel pairs.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: Perpendicular lines meet at what kind of angle?
choices: no angle, because they never meet
questions.solution: Perpendicular lines cross or meet at a square corner. A square corner is a right angle.

solve.work: Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: The two bars of a plus sign (+) cross each other at square corners. How many square corners (right angles) are made where the bars cross?
questions.solution: Two perpendicular lines that cross make 4 square corners around the crossing point, one in each direction.

solve.work: Two crossing perpendicular bars make 4 angles around the crossing, each a right angle: 4.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: The top edge and the side edge of a door frame meet at a square corner. How are the two edges related?
questions.solution: Two lines that meet at a square corner are perpendicular. Parallel lines never meet at all, and the top of a door is shorter than its side.

solve.work: Edges meeting at a square corner are perpendicular.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: Which kind of angle is smaller than a right angle?
questions.solution: An acute angle is smaller than a square corner. An obtuse angle is wider than a square corner, and a straight angle is a flat line.

solve.work: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: How many right angles does the capital letter L have?
questions.solution: The two lines of the letter L meet at one square corner, so L has 1 right angle.

solve.work: The letter L is a vertical stroke and a horizontal stroke meeting at one square corner: 1 right angle.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: Which of these is a good model of a right angle?
choices: the corner of a notebook page
the sharp tip of a pencil
a book opened until it lies flat
the narrow tip of a slice of pie
questions.answer: the corner of a notebook page
questions.solution: The corner of a notebook page is a square corner, which is a right angle. The pencil tip and the pie tip are narrow, so they are acute. A book lying flat is a straight line.

solve.answer: the corner of a notebook page
solve.work: A notebook page corner is a square corner (right angle). Pie tip and pencil tip are acute; a flat-open book is a straight angle.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: What kind of angle do the hands of a clock make at exactly 3:00?
questions.solution: At 3:00 one hand points straight up and the other points straight to the right. That makes a square corner, a right angle.

solve.work: At 3:00 the hands point to 12 and 3, a quarter turn apart: a right angle.

questions.skill: Right angles in shapes
questions.stem: Maya draws 2 squares. How many right angles do the 2 squares have in all?
questions.solution: Each square has 4 right angles. $2 \times 4 = 8$.

solve.work: Each square has 4 right angles; 2 x 4 = 8.

questions.skill: Right angles in shapes
questions.stem: Which of these shapes has 4 right angles?
questions.solution: A rectangle has 4 square corners. A circle and an oval have no corners, and a triangle has only 3 corners.

solve.work: A rectangle has 4 right angles; a triangle has 3 angles; circle and oval have none.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: How many sides does a quadrilateral have?
questions.solution: A quadrilateral is a shape with 4 straight sides.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: How many corners (vertices) does a rectangle have?
questions.solution: A rectangle has 4 sides, so it has 4 corners.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: A rhombus has 4 sides that are all the same length. One side is 6 centimeters long. How long is each of the other 3 sides, in centimeters?
questions.solution: All 4 sides of a rhombus are the same length, so each of the other sides is also 6 centimeters long.

solve.work: All sides of a rhombus are equal, so each other side is 6 cm.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: Dan draws 3 quadrilaterals. How many sides do the 3 shapes have in all?
questions.solution: Each quadrilateral has 4 sides. $3 \times 4 = 12$ sides.

questions.skill: Identify a quadrilateral from its features
questions.stem: A shape has 4 equal sides and 4 square corners. What is the shape?
questions.solution: A shape with 4 equal sides and 4 right angles is a square. A triangle has 3 sides, a pentagon 5 and a hexagon 6.

solve.work: 4 equal sides and 4 right angles: a square.

questions.skill: Identify a quadrilateral from its features
questions.stem: A shape has 4 square corners. Its two long sides are equal, and its two short sides are equal. What is the shape?
questions.solution: Four square corners with two long and two short sides make a rectangle. A square has all sides equal, so it has no long and short sides.

solve.work: 4 right angles, two long equal sides and two short equal sides: a rectangle (not a square, since long and short differ).

questions.skill: Identify a quadrilateral from its features
questions.stem: A shape has 4 sides that are all the same length. Which name fits the shape?
questions.solution: A quadrilateral with 4 equal sides is a rhombus. A triangle, a pentagon and a hexagon do not have 4 sides.

solve.work: A 4-sided shape with all sides equal is a rhombus. Hexagon, triangle, pentagon have the wrong number of sides.

questions.skill: Quadrilateral or not
questions.stem: Which of these shapes is a quadrilateral?
questions.solution: A quadrilateral has exactly 4 sides. A rhombus has 4 sides. A triangle has 3, a pentagon 5 and a hexagon 6.

solve.work: A rhombus has 4 sides; the others have 3, 6 and 5.

questions.skill: Quadrilateral or not
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a quadrilateral?
questions.solution: A square, a rectangle and a rhombus each have 4 sides. A triangle has only 3 sides, so it is not a quadrilateral.

solve.work: A triangle has 3 sides, so it is not a quadrilateral; square, rectangle and rhombus are.

questions.skill: Quadrilateral or not
questions.stem: Jack says a shape with 5 straight sides is a quadrilateral. Is he right?
choices: Yes, any shape with straight sides is a quadrilateral.
No, a quadrilateral has exactly 4 sides.
questions.answer: No, a quadrilateral has exactly 4 sides.
questions.solution: "Quad" means four. A quadrilateral has exactly 4 sides, so a shape with 5 sides is not one.

solve.answer: No, a quadrilateral has exactly 4 sides.
solve.work: A quadrilateral has exactly 4 sides; a 5-sided shape is a pentagon. Jack is wrong.

questions.skill: Name an obtuse angle
questions.stem: An angle opens wider than a square corner, but not as wide as a straight line. What kind of angle is it?
questions.solution: An angle smaller than a square corner is acute. A square corner is a right angle. An angle wider than a square corner but not yet a straight line is obtuse.

solve.work: Wider than a right angle but less than a straight angle: obtuse.

questions.skill: Identify a kind of quadrilateral
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides and no right angles. Which shape could it be?
questions.solution: A square and a rectangle both have 4 right angles, so they are out. A pentagon has 5 sides, so it is not a quadrilateral. A rhombus has 4 equal sides and does not need right angles.

solve.work: 4 equal sides: rhombus or square. Square has right angles, rectangle has right angles, pentagon has 5 sides. So rhombus.

questions.skill: Parallel sides of a rectangle
questions.stem: How many pairs of parallel sides does a rectangle have?
questions.solution: The two long sides are parallel to each other. The two short sides are parallel to each other. That makes 2 pairs.

solve.work: Opposite sides of a rectangle are parallel: 2 pairs.

questions.skill: Points, lines and line segments
questions.stem: How many endpoints does a line have?
questions.solution: A line goes on forever in both directions, so it never stops. It has no endpoints.

solve.work: A line goes on forever in both directions, so it has no endpoints: 0.

questions.skill: Points, lines and line segments
questions.stem: Which sentence tells how a line and a line segment are different?
choices: A line goes on forever in both directions, but a line segment has two endpoints.
A line has two endpoints, but a line segment goes on forever.
A line is curved, but a line segment is straight.
A line makes a square corner, but a line segment does not.
questions.answer: A line goes on forever in both directions, but a line segment has two endpoints.
questions.solution: A line has no ends. A line segment is a piece of a line with an endpoint at each end. Both are straight.

solve.answer: A line goes on forever in both directions, but a line segment has two endpoints.
solve.work: A line is endless both ways; a segment has two endpoints. The other options are false or reversed.

questions.skill: Points, lines and line segments
questions.stem: Points A, B and C are in order on one straight line. How many different line segments can be named using two of these points as endpoints?
questions.solution: The segments are AB, BC and AC. That is 3 line segments.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: A rectangle has 4 sides. How many other sides of the rectangle are parallel to its top side?
questions.solution: The bottom side is parallel to the top side. The left and right sides meet the top side at square corners, so they are not parallel to it. The answer is 1.

solve.work: Only the bottom side is parallel to the top side; the left and right sides are perpendicular to it. Answer 1.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: Which of these shapes has NO parallel sides?
questions.solution: A rectangle, a square and a rhombus each have two pairs of parallel sides. In a triangle every pair of sides meets at a corner, so none are parallel.

solve.work: Square, rhombus and rectangle each have 2 pairs of parallel sides; a triangle has none.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: A rhombus has 4 equal sides. Its opposite sides are parallel. How many pairs of parallel sides does a rhombus have?
questions.solution: Opposite sides are parallel. A rhombus has 2 pairs of opposite sides, so it has 2 pairs of parallel sides.

solve.work: Two pairs of opposite sides, both parallel: 2.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: Main Street runs east and west. Which street is parallel to Main Street?
choices: Pine Street, which runs north and south
Elm Street, which crosses Main Street at a square corner
Oak Street, which also runs east and west
Bay Street, which crosses Main Street and slants
questions.answer: Oak Street, which also runs east and west
questions.solution: A street parallel to Main Street runs the same way and never meets it. Oak Street does that. The other streets all cross Main Street.

solve.answer: Oak Street, which also runs east and west
solve.work: A street running the same direction (east-west) is parallel: Oak Street. Elm and Pine are perpendicular; Bay crosses.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: Line m runs straight up and down. Which line is perpendicular to line m?
choices: a line that runs straight across, side to side
another line that runs straight up and down
a line that leans a little to one side
questions.answer: a line that runs straight across, side to side
questions.solution: A line is perpendicular to another when they meet at a square corner. A line that runs straight across meets an up-and-down line at a square corner.

solve.answer: a line that runs straight across, side to side
solve.work: A vertical line is perpendicular to a horizontal (side to side) line.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: At which time do the hands of a clock make a square corner?
questions.solution: At 9:00 one hand points up and the other points left, which makes a square corner. At 6:00 the hands form a straight line, at 12:00 they lie together, and at 1:00 the angle is narrow.

solve.work: 9:00: hands at 12 and 9, a quarter turn apart = right angle. 1:00 acute; 12:00 hands together; 6:00 straight line.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: One street runs north and south. Another street runs east and west. How are the two streets related?
questions.solution: North-south and east-west directions meet at a square corner, so the two streets are perpendicular.

solve.work: North-south and east-west directions meet at square corners: perpendicular.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: Which of these shapes has sides that are perpendicular to each other?
choices: a rhombus with no right angles
questions.solution: Perpendicular sides meet at square corners. A rectangle has 4 square corners. The triangle and the rhombus have no square corners, and a circle has no sides.

solve.work: A rectangle's adjacent sides meet at right angles, so they are perpendicular. Equilateral triangle (60 degree angles), circle, non-square rhombus have none.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: Angle P is smaller than a square corner. Angle Q is a square corner. Angle R is wider than a square corner but is not a straight line. Which list names the angles P, Q and R in order?
questions.solution: An angle smaller than a square corner is acute. A square corner is a right angle. An angle wider than a square corner, but not a straight line, is obtuse.

solve.work: P smaller than right = acute; Q = right; R wider than right but not straight = obtuse.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: Which statement about angles is true?
choices: An obtuse angle is wider than a right angle.
An acute angle is wider than a right angle.
A right angle is smaller than an acute angle.
An obtuse angle is smaller than an acute angle.
questions.answer: An obtuse angle is wider than a right angle.
questions.solution: From narrowest to widest the kinds are acute, then right, then obtuse. So an obtuse angle is wider than a right angle.

solve.answer: An obtuse angle is wider than a right angle.
solve.work: Obtuse > right > acute. Only 'An obtuse angle is wider than a right angle' is true.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: At 3:00 the hands of a clock make a square corner. What kind of angle do the hands make at 2:00?
questions.solution: At 2:00 the hands are closer together than at 3:00, so the angle is smaller than a square corner. That is an acute angle.

solve.work: At 2:00 the hands are 2 hour-marks apart, less than the 3 marks of a right angle (3:00): acute.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: Four angles are described. Angle A is a square corner. Angles B and C are each smaller than a square corner. Angle D is wider than a square corner but is not a straight line. How many of the four angles are acute?
questions.solution: An acute angle is smaller than a square corner. Angles B and C are acute. Angle A is a right angle and angle D is obtuse. So 2 angles are acute.

solve.work: A right, B and C acute, D obtuse: 2 acute.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: Which capital letter has an acute angle in it?
questions.solution: The two lines of the letter V meet in a narrow point, smaller than a square corner, so V has an acute angle. L has a right angle, and O and I have no corners.

solve.work: V has two strokes meeting at a narrow point: acute. L is a right angle; I and O have no angle.

questions.skill: Right angles in shapes
questions.stem: Ben draws 3 rectangles. How many right angles do the 3 rectangles have in all?
questions.solution: Each rectangle has 4 right angles. $3 \times 4 = 12$.

questions.skill: Right angles in shapes
questions.stem: How many acute angles does a rectangle have?
questions.solution: All 4 angles of a rectangle are right angles, so none of them are acute.

solve.work: All 4 angles of a rectangle are right angles, so 0 acute.

questions.skill: Right angles in shapes
questions.stem: A page shows a square and a rhombus that is not a square. The rhombus has no right angles. How many right angles are there in the two shapes together?
questions.solution: The square has 4 right angles and the rhombus has none. $4 + 0 = 4$.

questions.skill: Right angles in shapes
questions.stem: Sam has 1 square tile and 3 rectangle tiles. How many right angles do the 4 tiles have in all?
questions.solution: Each tile is a square or a rectangle, so each has 4 right angles. $4 \times 4 = 16$.

solve.work: 4 tiles, each with 4 right angles: 4 x 4 = 16.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: A rectangle has one side that is 9 inches long and another side that is 4 inches long. How many of its 4 sides are 4 inches long?
questions.solution: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal. The side across from the 4-inch side is also 4 inches. So 2 sides are 4 inches long and 2 sides are 9 inches long.

solve.work: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal: two 9-inch sides and two 4-inch sides. Answer 2.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: Which quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
questions.solution: A rectangle, a square and a rhombus each have two pairs of parallel sides. A trapezoid has only one pair.

solve.issues: Relies on the exclusive trapezoid definition (exactly one pair); under the inclusive one a trapezoid need not have exactly one. Still the only defensible option here.
solve.work: Square, rectangle and rhombus each have 2 pairs of parallel sides; a trapezoid is the one with exactly one pair.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: Mia's shape has 4 sides. Two of the sides are parallel. The other two sides are not parallel to each other. How many pairs of parallel sides does her shape have?
questions.solution: Only one pair of sides is parallel, so there is 1 pair.

solve.work: One pair of parallel sides; the other two are not parallel: 1 pair.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: Jin draws a quadrilateral with 4 sides that are all 7 inches long. How many inches long is its shortest side?
questions.solution: All 4 sides are the same length, so the shortest side is 7 inches long too.

solve.work: All 4 sides are 7 inches, so the shortest is 7.

questions.skill: Identify a quadrilateral from its features
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has 4 right angles. Two of its sides are 10 centimeters long and the other two are 6 centimeters long. Which shape is it?
questions.solution: Four right angles with sides of two different lengths make a rectangle. A square and a rhombus have 4 equal sides, and a triangle has only 3 sides.

solve.work: 4 right angles with two different side lengths (10 and 6): rectangle, not a square.

questions.skill: Identify a quadrilateral from its features
questions.stem: Which description fits a rhombus?
choices: exactly one pair of parallel sides
4 sides that are all the same length
4 right angles and two different side lengths
questions.answer: 4 sides that are all the same length
questions.solution: A rhombus is a quadrilateral with 4 equal sides. A triangle has 3 sides, a trapezoid has one pair of parallel sides, and a shape with 4 right angles and two side lengths is a rectangle.

solve.answer: 4 sides that are all the same length
solve.work: A rhombus has 4 equal sides. Option 2 describes a non-square rectangle, 3 a trapezoid, 4 a triangle.

questions.skill: Identify a quadrilateral from its features
questions.stem: A shape has 4 sides. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, but none of its angles are right angles. Which shape could it be?
choices: a parallelogram that is not a rectangle
questions.answer: a parallelogram that is not a rectangle
questions.solution: A shape with two pairs of parallel sides is a parallelogram. A rectangle and a square have right angles, and a triangle has no parallel sides. So it is a parallelogram that is not a rectangle.

solve.answer: a parallelogram that is not a rectangle
solve.work: Two pairs of parallel sides but no right angles: a parallelogram that is not a rectangle. Rectangle and square have right angles; triangle has 3 sides.

questions.skill: Quadrilateral or not
questions.stem: Ella says that a trapezoid, a rhombus, a square and a pentagon are all quadrilaterals. Which shape did she get wrong?
questions.solution: A quadrilateral has 4 sides. A trapezoid, a rhombus and a square each have 4 sides. A pentagon has 5 sides, so it is not a quadrilateral.

solve.work: A pentagon has 5 sides, so it is not a quadrilateral; the others have 4 sides.

questions.skill: Relate kinds of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: A square always has 4 right angles. Which other shape always has 4 right angles?
questions.solution: Every rectangle has 4 right angles. A rhombus, a trapezoid and a parallelogram can have angles that are not right angles.

solve.work: A rectangle always has 4 right angles; trapezoid, parallelogram and rhombus need not.

questions.skill: Relate kinds of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: Dana says every shape with 4 sides is a square. Which shape shows that Dana is wrong?
choices: a rectangle with two long sides and two short sides
questions.answer: a rectangle with two long sides and two short sides
questions.solution: The shape must have 4 sides and not be a square. A rectangle with long and short sides does that. A square would fit what Dana said, and a triangle and a circle do not have 4 sides.

solve.answer: a rectangle with two long sides and two short sides
solve.work: A counterexample must have 4 sides and not be a square: a rectangle with long and short sides. Circle and triangle do not have 4 sides.

questions.skill: Relate kinds of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: Which statement is true?
choices: Every rectangle is also a square.
Every rhombus has four right angles.
Every square is also a rectangle.
Every quadrilateral has four equal sides.
questions.answer: Every square is also a rectangle.
questions.solution: A square has 4 sides and 4 right angles, so it is a special kind of rectangle. But a rectangle can have long and short sides, so not every rectangle is a square. A rhombus can lean, and any quadrilateral can have sides of different lengths.

solve.answer: Every square is also a rectangle.
solve.work: A square has 4 right angles and opposite sides parallel/equal, so it is a rectangle. The other statements are false (a non-square rhombus has no right angles, a 2-by-3 rectangle is not a square, a trapezoid need not have equal sides).

questions.skill: Perpendicular to a parallel pair
questions.stem: Lines A, B and C are all on one flat page. Line A is parallel to line B. Line C crosses line A and makes a right angle with it. What is true about line C and line B?
choices: Line C is perpendicular to line B.
Line C is parallel to line B.
Line C is the same line as line B.
Line C makes an acute angle with line B.
questions.answer: Line C is perpendicular to line B.
questions.solution: Parallel lines A and B lean the same way. If line C makes a square corner with line A, it makes a square corner with line B too. So line C is perpendicular to line B.

solve.answer: Line C is perpendicular to line B.
solve.work: C is perpendicular to A, and B is parallel to A, so C crosses B at a right angle too: C is perpendicular to B.

questions.skill: Count right angles in three shapes
questions.stem: A page has a rectangle, a square and a rhombus that is not a square. How many right angles do the three shapes have in all?
questions.solution: The rectangle has 4 right angles and the square has 4. A rhombus that is not a square has no right angles. In all: 4 + 4 + 0 = 8.

solve.work: Rectangle 4 right angles, square 4, a rhombus that is not a square has none (one right angle would force all four). 4 + 4 + 0 = 8.

questions.skill: Points, lines and line segments
questions.stem: Points A, B, C and D lie in order on one straight line. How many different line segments can be named using two of these points as endpoints?
questions.solution: The segments are AB, AC, AD, BC, BD and CD. That is 6. A quick count is $3 + 2 + 1 = 6$: three start at A, two more start at B, and one more starts at C.

solve.work: Pairs: AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD = 6.

questions.skill: Points, lines and line segments
questions.stem: Which statement about lines and line segments is true?
choices: You can measure the length of a whole line, but not a line segment.
You can measure both a line and a line segment.
You can measure the length of a line segment, but not of a whole line, because a line never ends.
A line segment never ends, but a line has two endpoints.
