questions.answer: You can measure the length of a line segment, but not of a whole line, because a line never ends.
questions.solution: A line segment stops at both ends, so it has a length that can be measured. A line goes on forever, so it cannot be measured.

solve.answer: You can measure the length of a line segment, but not of a whole line, because a line never ends.
solve.work: A segment has a measurable length; a line never ends, so it cannot be measured.

questions.skill: Points, lines and line segments
questions.stem: Segment XY has endpoints X and Y. Point Z is on segment XY, between X and Y. Which statement is true?
choices: Segment XZ is longer than segment XY.
Segment XZ is shorter than segment XY.
Segment XZ is the same length as segment XY.
Point Z is not on segment XY.
questions.answer: Segment XZ is shorter than segment XY.
questions.solution: Segment XZ is only a part of segment XY, so it is shorter. Z is on the segment, so "Point Z is not on segment XY" is false.

solve.answer: Segment XZ is shorter than segment XY.
solve.work: Z is strictly between X and Y, so XZ is part of XY and shorter.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: Lines p, q and r are three different lines on one flat page. Line p is parallel to line q, and line r is parallel to line q. What is true about lines p and r?
questions.solution: Lines that are each parallel to the same line all run in the same direction. So p and r never meet: they are parallel to each other.

solve.work: Two different lines both parallel to q on one plane are parallel to each other.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: A page shows a square, a rectangle and a trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides. How many pairs of parallel sides are there in all three shapes together?
questions.solution: The square has 2 pairs, the rectangle has 2 pairs and the trapezoid has 1 pair. $2 + 2 + 1 = 5$.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: Which statement about a rectangle is true?
choices: Opposite sides are perpendicular, and sides that meet at a corner are parallel.
All 4 sides are parallel to each other.
Opposite sides are parallel, and sides that meet at a corner are perpendicular.
questions.answer: Opposite sides are parallel, and sides that meet at a corner are perpendicular.
questions.solution: Sides across from each other never meet, so they are parallel. Sides that meet at a corner make a right angle, so they are perpendicular.

solve.answer: Opposite sides are parallel, and sides that meet at a corner are perpendicular.
solve.work: In a rectangle opposite sides are parallel and adjacent sides meet at right angles (perpendicular).

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: Two parallel lines that run left to right are crossed by two parallel lines that run up and down, like the # sign. All the lines cross at square corners. The lines cross at 4 points. How many right angles are made altogether?
questions.solution: Each crossing point has 4 right angles around it. With 4 crossing points, $4 \times 4 = 16$ right angles.

solve.work: Each of the 4 crossing points has 4 right angles around it: 4 x 4 = 16.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: Line a is perpendicular to line b. Line b is perpendicular to line c. The three lines are different and are on one flat page. What is true about lines a and c?
choices: They cross at an acute angle.
They cross at an obtuse angle.
questions.solution: Line a meets line b at a square corner, and so does line c. So a and c both run across b in the same direction, and they never meet. They are parallel.

solve.work: a and c are both perpendicular to b on one plane, so they run in the same direction and are parallel.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: A rectangle has 4 corners. At each corner two sides meet at a right angle. How many pairs of sides in a rectangle are perpendicular to each other?
questions.solution: Each of the 4 corners is made by one pair of perpendicular sides. So there are 4 pairs.

solve.work: Sides T, B, L, R. Perpendicular pairs meet at corners: T-L, T-R, B-L, B-R = 4 (T-B and L-R are parallel).

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: A rhombus that is not a square has no right angles. How many pairs of its sides are perpendicular to each other?
questions.solution: Sides are perpendicular only when they meet at a right angle. This rhombus has no right angles, so none of its sides are perpendicular.

solve.work: Adjacent sides meet at non-right angles; opposite sides are parallel. So 0 perpendicular pairs.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: Two streets cross, and one of the 4 corners they make is a right angle. What is true about the other 3 corners?
choices: Two are obtuse angles and one is acute.
questions.solution: If two straight lines cross at a square corner, they are perpendicular, and all 4 corners around the crossing are right angles.

solve.work: If one angle where two lines cross is right, the lines are perpendicular and all 4 angles are right angles.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: The hands of a clock make a square corner at 3:00 and a straight line at 6:00. What kind of angle do the hands make at 4:00?
questions.solution: At 4:00 the hands are farther apart than at 3:00 but not as far as at 6:00. So the angle is wider than a square corner but not a straight line: it is obtuse.

solve.work: 4:00 is between 3:00 (right) and 6:00 (straight): wider than a right angle, less than straight: obtuse.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: At which time do the hands of a clock make an obtuse angle?
questions.solution: At 3:00 the hands make a square corner and at 6:00 they make a straight line, so the angle at 5:00 is wider than a square corner but not straight. That is obtuse. At 1:00 and 2:00 the angle is acute.

solve.work: 5:00 is 5 hour-marks apart, between 3 (right) and 6 (straight): obtuse. 1:00 and 2:00 are acute; 3:00 is right.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: Look at the hands of a clock at 12:00, at 3:00, at 6:00 and at 9:00. At how many of these four times do the hands make a right angle?
questions.solution: The hands make a right angle at 3:00 and at 9:00. At 6:00 they make a straight line and at 12:00 they lie on top of each other. So 2 of the times.

solve.work: 12:00 hands overlap; 3:00 right; 6:00 straight; 9:00 right. Answer 2.

questions.skill: Right angles in shapes
questions.stem: A page shows 1 square, 2 rectangles and 1 triangle that has one right angle. How many right angles are there in all four shapes?
questions.solution: The square has 4 right angles. The 2 rectangles have $2 \times 4 = 8$. The triangle has 1. $4 + 8 + 1 = 13$.

questions.skill: Right angles in shapes
questions.stem: Rina draws a rectangle. She cuts it into 2 smaller rectangles with one straight cut from the middle of the top side to the middle of the bottom side. How many right angles do the 2 smaller rectangles have in all?
questions.solution: The cut makes 2 rectangles. Each has 4 right angles. $2 \times 4 = 8$.

solve.work: A vertical cut from midpoint of top to midpoint of bottom is perpendicular to both, giving 2 rectangles with 4 right angles each: 8.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: How are a rectangle and a rhombus alike?
choices: Both have two pairs of parallel sides.
Both have four sides of equal length.
Both have exactly one pair of parallel sides.
questions.answer: Both have two pairs of parallel sides.
questions.solution: A rectangle and a rhombus each have opposite sides that are parallel, so each has 2 pairs. A rectangle does not need equal sides, and a rhombus does not need right angles.

solve.answer: Both have two pairs of parallel sides.
solve.work: Both rectangle and rhombus are parallelograms: two pairs of parallel sides. Not both have equal sides or right angles.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: Maya has a square, a rectangle, a rhombus and a trapezoid that has exactly one pair of parallel sides. How many of the 4 shapes have two pairs of parallel sides?
questions.solution: The square, the rectangle and the rhombus each have 2 pairs of parallel sides. The trapezoid has only 1 pair. So 3 shapes.

solve.work: Square, rectangle, rhombus have 2 pairs each; the trapezoid has 1. Answer 3.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: Maya has a square, a rectangle, a rhombus and a trapezoid. How many of these 4 shapes ALWAYS have four right angles?
questions.solution: Every square and every rectangle has 4 right angles. A rhombus and a trapezoid can have angles that are not right angles. So 2 shapes always do.

solve.work: Square and rectangle always have 4 right angles; rhombus and trapezoid not always. Answer 2.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: A rhombus has one side that is 9 centimeters long. A rectangle has two sides of 9 centimeters and two sides of 4 centimeters. How many of the 8 sides of these two shapes are 9 centimeters long?
questions.solution: All 4 sides of a rhombus are equal, so all 4 are 9 centimeters long. The rectangle has 2 sides of 9 centimeters. $4 + 2 = 6$.

solve.work: Rhombus: all 4 sides 9 cm. Rectangle: 2 sides 9 cm. 4 + 2 = 6.

questions.skill: Sides, corners and parallel sides of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: How is a square different from a rectangle that is not a square?
choices: A square has 4 right angles, but the other rectangle does not.
The other rectangle has parallel sides, but a square does not.
A square has 3 sides, but the other rectangle has 4.
A square has 4 equal sides, but the sides of the other rectangle are not all equal.
questions.answer: A square has 4 equal sides, but the sides of the other rectangle are not all equal.
questions.solution: Both shapes have 4 right angles, 4 sides and two pairs of parallel sides. The difference is that every side of a square is the same length.

solve.answer: A square has 4 equal sides, but the sides of the other rectangle are not all equal.
solve.work: Both have 4 right angles and parallel sides; the difference is a square's 4 equal sides.

questions.skill: Identify a quadrilateral from its features
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has 4 sides of equal length. Which of these must also be true?
choices: It has exactly one pair of parallel sides.
questions.solution: A quadrilateral with 4 equal sides is a rhombus (a square is one kind), and the opposite sides of a rhombus are parallel. It may or may not have right angles, and it never has just one pair of parallel sides.

solve.work: 4 equal sides = rhombus, whose opposite sides are always parallel. Right angles only if square; acute angles fail for a square; it has 2 pairs, not one.

questions.skill: Identify a quadrilateral from its features
questions.stem: Which quadrilateral could have 2 acute angles and 2 obtuse angles, but no right angles?
choices: a rhombus that is not a square
questions.answer: a rhombus that is not a square
questions.solution: A rectangle and a square have only right angles. A triangle has only 3 angles. A rhombus that is not a square has two narrow angles and two wide angles.

solve.answer: a rhombus that is not a square
solve.work: A non-square rhombus has 2 acute and 2 obtuse angles. Square and rectangle have right angles; a triangle is not a quadrilateral.

questions.skill: Identify a quadrilateral from its features
questions.stem: Ivy describes a quadrilateral: "Opposite sides are parallel, I have 4 right angles, and my sides are not all equal." Which quadrilateral is it?
choices: a rectangle that is not a square
a rhombus that is not a square
a trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides
questions.answer: a rectangle that is not a square
questions.solution: Four right angles and two pairs of parallel sides make a rectangle. The sides are not all equal, so it is not a square. A rhombus has no right angles here, and a trapezoid has one pair of parallel sides.

solve.answer: a rectangle that is not a square
solve.work: Opposite sides parallel, 4 right angles, sides not all equal: a rectangle that is not a square.

questions.skill: Relate kinds of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: Which statement is FALSE?
questions.solution: A square has 4 right angles and 4 equal sides, so it is a rectangle, a rhombus and a quadrilateral. But a rectangle with long and short sides is not a square.

solve.work: A rectangle with unequal sides is not a square, so 'Every rectangle is a square' is false. The others are true.

questions.skill: Relate kinds of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: Which shape belongs in both groups: "shapes with 4 right angles" and "shapes with 4 equal sides"?
choices: a rectangle that is not a square
a rhombus that is not a square
a trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides
questions.solution: Only a square has both 4 right angles and 4 equal sides. The other rectangle has unequal sides, and the other rhombus has no right angles.

solve.work: A square has both 4 right angles and 4 equal sides.

questions.skill: Relate kinds of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: Dev says a square is also a rhombus. Tara says a square is also a rectangle. Who is correct?
choices: Both Dev and Tara are correct.
questions.answer: Both Dev and Tara are correct.
questions.solution: A square has 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. It also has 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. Both are correct.

solve.answer: Both Dev and Tara are correct.
solve.work: A square has 4 equal sides (rhombus) and 4 right angles (rectangle): both correct.

questions.skill: Quadrilateral or not
questions.stem: A pentagon has 5 sides and a hexagon has 6 sides. Tia draws 2 quadrilaterals, 1 pentagon and 1 hexagon. How many sides do her 4 shapes have in all?
questions.solution: The 2 quadrilaterals have $2 \times 4 = 8$ sides. Add the pentagon and the hexagon: $8 + 5 + 6 = 19$.

questions.skill: Quadrilateral or not
questions.stem: How many of these six shapes are quadrilaterals: a square, a triangle, a trapezoid, a pentagon, a rhombus, a hexagon?
questions.solution: A quadrilateral has 4 sides. The square, the trapezoid and the rhombus have 4 sides. The triangle has 3, the pentagon has 5 and the hexagon has 6. So 3 shapes.

solve.work: Quadrilaterals: square, trapezoid, rhombus = 3. Triangle, pentagon, hexagon are not.

questions.skill: Right, acute and obtuse angles
questions.stem: Mina marks 10 angles in a drawing. 2 of them are right angles. There are 3 times as many acute angles as right angles. All the other angles are obtuse. How many angles are obtuse?
questions.solution: There are $3 \times 2 = 6$ acute angles. The right and acute angles together make $2 + 6 = 8$ angles. The other $10 - 8 = 2$ angles are obtuse.

questions.skill: Elapsed time within an hour
questions.stem: Soccer practice starts at 4:10 and ends at 4:45. How many minutes long is practice?
questions.solution: From 4:10 to 4:45 is the same hour. Subtract the minutes: 45 − 10 = 35 minutes.

questions.skill: Choose a unit of weight
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the weight of a watermelon?
questions.solution: Weight is measured in ounces or pounds. A watermelon is heavy, so pounds is the best unit. Inches measure length, and cups and gallons measure how much a container holds.

solve.work: Weight in customary units: pounds. Inches is length; cups and gallons are capacity.

questions.skill: One-step length problem
questions.stem: A string is 12 inches long. Dina cuts off 4 inches. How many inches of string are left?
questions.solution: 12 − 4 = 8 inches are left.

questions.skill: Elapsed time: find how long
questions.stem: Story hour at the library starts at 2:15 and ends at 2:45. How many minutes long is story hour?
questions.solution: From 2:15 to 2:45 is 30 minutes. Check: $45 - 15 = 30$.

questions.skill: Elapsed time: find how long
questions.stem: Lena starts her homework at 4:10 and finishes at 4:50. How many minutes did she work?
questions.solution: From 4:10 to 4:50 is $50 - 10 = 40$ minutes. The other choices come from using only one of the times (10 or 50) or from the minutes in a whole hour (60).

questions.skill: Elapsed time: find how long
questions.stem: It is 6:10 now. Dinner is at 6:45. How many minutes is it until dinner?
questions.solution: From 6:10 to 6:45 is $45 - 10 = 35$ minutes.

questions.skill: Elapsed time: find how long
questions.stem: The school bus left at 8:05 and arrived at 8:30. How many minutes did the bus ride take?
questions.solution: From 8:05 to 8:30 is $30 - 5 = 25$ minutes. Adding the minutes gives 35, and using only one time gives 30 or 5.

questions.skill: Elapsed time: find the end time
questions.stem: A show starts at 4:00 and lasts 30 minutes. What time does it end?
questions.solution: 30 minutes after 4:00 is 4:30.

questions.skill: Elapsed time: find the end time
questions.stem: Football practice begins at 3:20 and lasts 15 minutes. Practice ends at 3:__. What number goes in the blank?
questions.solution: 15 minutes after 3:20 is 3:35, since $20 + 15 = 35$. The blank is 35.

questions.skill: Elapsed time: find the end time
questions.stem: A bus ride starts at 7:15 and takes 20 minutes. What time does the bus ride end?
questions.solution: 20 minutes after 7:15 is 7:35, since $15 + 20 = 35$.

questions.skill: Elapsed time: find the start time
questions.stem: A cartoon ends at 6:30. It lasted 30 minutes. What time did it start?
questions.solution: 30 minutes before 6:30 is 6:00.

questions.skill: Elapsed time: find the start time
questions.stem: A show ended at 2:45 and lasted 15 minutes. It started at 2:__. What number goes in the blank?
questions.solution: 15 minutes before 2:45 is 2:30, since $45 - 15 = 30$. The blank is 30.

questions.skill: Time before and after a given time
questions.stem: What time is 10 minutes after 4:20?
questions.solution: 10 minutes after 4:20 is 4:30.

questions.skill: Time before and after a given time
questions.stem: What time is 5 minutes before 9:00?
questions.solution: 5 minutes before 9:00 is 8:55, because the minute hand goes back past the 12 to the 11.

questions.skill: Read a clock to the minute
questions.stem: On a clock, the hour hand points exactly at the 5 and the minute hand points exactly at the 12. What time is it?
questions.solution: The minute hand on the 12 means 0 minutes past the hour. The hour hand on the 5 means it is 5 o'clock: 5:00.

solve.work: Minute hand on 12 means o'clock; hour hand exactly at 5: 5:00.

questions.skill: Read a clock to the minute
questions.stem: The hour hand of a clock is between the 2 and the 3. The minute hand points at the 6. What time is it?
questions.solution: The hour hand has not reached the 3, so the hour is 2. The minute hand on the 6 means $6 \times 5 = 30$ minutes. The time is 2:30.

solve.work: Minute hand on 6 = 30 minutes; hour hand between 2 and 3 means after 2: 2:30.

questions.skill: Choose the best unit of measure
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a pencil?
questions.solution: A pencil is a short length, so inches fit best. Miles are for long distances, gallons for liquids and ounces for weight.

solve.work: A pencil's length is a few inches; gallons and ounces are not length units, miles too large.

questions.skill: Choose the best unit of measure
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the amount of milk in a small glass?
questions.solution: Milk is a liquid, so we measure how much it holds in units of capacity. A small glass holds about 1 cup.

solve.work: Liquid volume in a small glass: cups. Miles and inches are length, pounds weight.

questions.skill: Choose the best unit of measure
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the weight of a bag of apples?
questions.solution: Weight is measured in ounces or pounds. A bag of apples is heavy enough for pounds.

solve.work: Weight of a bag of apples: pounds. The others are length or capacity units.

questions.skill: Choose the best unit of measure
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the distance between two towns?
questions.solution: A long distance is measured in miles. Inches are far too small, and cups and ounces do not measure distance.

solve.work: Distance between towns is large: miles.

questions.skill: Choose the right measuring tool
questions.stem: Which tool is best for measuring how long a pencil is?
questions.solution: A ruler measures length. A measuring cup measures liquid, a scale measures weight and a clock tells time.

solve.work: Length of a pencil: a ruler.

questions.skill: Choose the right measuring tool
questions.stem: Which tool is best for finding how heavy a bag of rice is?
questions.solution: A scale measures weight. A ruler measures length, a measuring cup measures how much a container holds and a clock tells time.

questions.skill: Estimate length, capacity and weight
questions.stem: About how tall is a classroom door?
questions.solution: A classroom door is a little taller than most adults, about 7 feet. 7 inches is as long as a pencil, and 7 yards or 7 miles is much too tall.

solve.work: A door is a bit taller than an adult, about 7 feet. 7 yards = 21 ft too tall; 7 inches too short; 7 miles absurd.

questions.skill: Estimate length, capacity and weight
questions.stem: About how much water does a small drinking glass hold?
questions.solution: A glass holds about 1 cup. A gallon is a big jug that holds 16 cups, so a glass holds much less.

solve.work: A small glass holds about 1 cup; gallons are far too much.

questions.skill: Estimate length, capacity and weight
questions.stem: Each of Tom's big steps is about 1 yard long. He takes 15 big steps across a room. About how many yards wide is the room?
questions.solution: 15 steps of about 1 yard each is about $15 \times 1 = 15$ yards.

solve.work: 15 steps of about 1 yard each: about 15 yards.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: A rectangular card is cut into two pieces. One piece is 5 units by 3 units and the other is 5 units by 1 unit. What was the area of the whole card in square units?
questions.solution: The first piece has area $5 \times 3 = 15$ and the second has area $5 \times 1 = 5$. The whole card has area $15 + 5 = 20$ square units.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: A sheet of paper is 6 inches long and 4 inches wide. It is cut into two rectangles. One of them is 6 inches by 1 inch. What is the area of the other rectangle in square inches?
questions.solution: The whole sheet has area $6 \times 4 = 24$ square inches. The small piece has area $6 \times 1 = 6$ square inches. The other piece has area $24 - 6 = 18$ square inches.

solve.work: Whole = 6 x 4 = 24. Piece 6 x 1 = 6. Other = 24 - 6 = 18 (6 by 3).

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: A triangle has sides that are 3 inches, 4 inches and 5 inches long. What is its perimeter in inches?
questions.solution: Perimeter is the distance around, so add all the sides: $3 + 4 + 5 = 12$ inches.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: A rectangular door mat is 4 feet long and 2 feet wide. What is its perimeter in feet?
questions.solution: A rectangle has two long sides and two short sides: $4 + 2 + 4 + 2 = 12$ feet.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: Which word names the distance around the outside of a shape?
questions.solution: The distance around the outside of a shape is its perimeter. Area is the space inside it.

solve.work: The distance around a shape is its perimeter.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: Each side of a square sign is 7 inches long. How many inches is it around the whole sign?
questions.solution: A square has 4 equal sides: $4 \times 7 = 28$ inches.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: A pentagon has 5 sides that are each 3 centimeters long. What is its perimeter in centimeters?
questions.solution: All 5 sides are the same length: $5 \times 3 = 15$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: Sam walks once around the edge of a rectangular yard that is 5 meters long and 3 meters wide. Which expression shows how many meters he walks?
questions.solution: He walks along all four sides: $5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16$ meters. Multiplying $5 \times 3$ gives the area, not the distance around.

solve.work: Once around = sum of the four sides = 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16. (5x3x2 = 30, wrong.)

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: Jin glues ribbon around the edge of a rectangular card that is 6 centimeters long and 4 centimeters wide. How many centimeters of ribbon does he need to go all the way around?
questions.solution: Add all four sides: $6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: Mia walks once around a triangular park. The whole walk is 30 meters. The first two sides are 12 meters and 10 meters long. How many meters long is the third side?
questions.solution: The three sides add to 30. The first two sides total $12 + 10 = 22$, so the third side is $30 - 22 = 8$ meters.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: A square has a perimeter of 20 centimeters. How many centimeters long is each side?
questions.solution: A square has 4 equal sides, so each side is $20 \div 4 = 5$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: A four-sided shape has a perimeter of 20 units. Three of its sides are 3 units, 4 units and 6 units. Let $n$ be the length of the fourth side. Which equation can be used to find $n$?
questions.solution: All four sides add up to the perimeter: $3 + 4 + 6 + n = 20$. Then $13 + n = 20$, so $n = 7$.

solve.work: Sum of all four sides = perimeter: 3 + 4 + 6 + n = 20 (n = 7).

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: A hexagon has six sides of equal length. Its perimeter is 30 centimeters. How many centimeters long is each side?
questions.solution: Six equal sides add to 30, so each side is $30 \div 6 = 5$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Area or perimeter: which to find, and which units
questions.stem: Ben puts a fence around the edge of his rectangular garden. What should he find to know how much fence he needs?
questions.solution: A fence goes around the edge, so Ben needs the distance around the garden, which is the perimeter.

solve.work: Fence goes around the edge: perimeter.

questions.skill: Area or perimeter: which to find, and which units
questions.stem: Which unit would you use to measure the perimeter of a rectangular rug?
questions.solution: Perimeter is a length, so it is measured in units of length such as feet. Square units measure area.

solve.work: Perimeter is a length, measured in linear units: feet.

questions.skill: Area or perimeter: which to find, and which units
questions.stem: Which job needs the area of a rectangle?
choices: putting a ribbon around the edge of a card
putting a fence around a yard
walking once around the edge of a field
questions.solution: Paint covers the flat surface of the wall, so the job needs area. The other three jobs go around the edge, so they need perimeter.

solve.work: Fence, walking around, ribbon around edge are perimeter; painting a wall covers its surface: area.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter together
questions.stem: Maya draws a rectangle that is 2 units wide and 3 units long. She counts 6 unit squares inside it, and the distance around it is 10 units. What is the area of the rectangle in square units?
questions.solution: Area is the number of unit squares inside the rectangle, which is 6. The 10 is the perimeter, the distance around.

solve.work: Area = unit squares inside = 2 x 3 = 6. (10 is the perimeter.)

questions.skill: Area by multiplying side lengths
questions.stem: A rectangular garden is 9 feet long and 6 feet wide. What is the area of the garden in square feet?
questions.solution: Area of a rectangle = length × width. $9 \times 6 = 54$ square feet.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangle is 8 centimeters long and 3 centimeters wide. What is its perimeter in centimeters?
questions.solution: A rectangle has 2 long sides and 2 short sides: 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22 centimeters.

questions.skill: Missing side of a triangle from its perimeter
questions.stem: A triangle has a perimeter of 24 inches. Two of its sides are 7 inches and 9 inches long. How many inches long is the third side?
questions.solution: The two known sides add to 7 + 9 = 16 inches. The third side is the rest of the perimeter: 24 − 16 = 8 inches.

questions.skill: Area by tiling with unit squares
questions.stem: A rectangle is covered by 24 unit squares arranged in 4 equal rows, with no gaps or overlaps. How many unit squares are in each row?
questions.solution: Share 24 squares equally among 4 rows: $24 \div 4 = 6$ squares in each row. Check: $4 \times 6 = 24$.

questions.skill: Area by tiling with unit squares
questions.stem: Which rectangle can be covered exactly by 18 unit squares, with no gaps and no overlaps?
choices: a rectangle that is 3 units by 5 units
a rectangle that is 4 units by 5 units
a rectangle that is 2 units by 8 units
a rectangle that is 3 units by 6 units
questions.answer: a rectangle that is 3 units by 6 units
questions.solution: The number of squares is length times width. $3 \times 6 = 18$, so the 3 by 6 rectangle works. The others need 15, 20 and 16 squares.

solve.answer: a rectangle that is 3 units by 6 units

questions.skill: Area by tiling with unit squares
questions.stem: A patio is covered by square paving stones that are each 1 meter on each side. There are 7 rows with 8 stones in each row. What is the area of the patio in square meters?
questions.solution: Each stone covers 1 square meter. There are 7 rows of 8 stones, so $7 \times 8 = 56$ square meters. The choice 15 adds, 30 is the distance around, and 49 multiplies 7 by 7.

solve.work: 7 rows of 8 one-meter stones: 7 x 8 = 56 square meters.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square by multiplying side lengths
questions.stem: The floor of a classroom is a rectangle that measures 8 feet by 9 feet. How many square feet is the floor?
questions.solution: Area is $8 \times 9 = 72$ square feet. The choice 17 adds the sides, 34 is the distance around, and 81 is $9 \times 9$.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square by multiplying side lengths
questions.stem: A rectangular playground is 10 meters long and 7 meters wide. What is its area in square meters?
questions.solution: Area is $10 \times 7 = 70$ square meters. The choice 34 is the distance around, 17 adds the sides, and 60 multiplies 10 by 6.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square by multiplying side lengths
questions.stem: A square garden bed is 9 feet on each side. What is its area in square feet?
questions.solution: All four sides are 9 feet, so the area is $9 \times 9 = 81$ square feet.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square by multiplying side lengths
questions.stem: A rectangle is 4 inches long and 6 inches wide. Which statement is true?
questions.solution: Area is length times width: $4 \times 6 = 24$ square inches. The value 10 is $4 + 6$, 20 is the distance around, and 48 is double the area.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the area
questions.stem: A rectangular garden has an area of 56 square meters and is 8 meters long. How many meters wide is the garden?
questions.solution: Width $= 56 \div 8 = 7$ meters. Check: $8 \times 7 = 56$. The choice 48 subtracts, 64 adds, and 8 repeats the length.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the area
questions.stem: A rectangular classroom rug has an area of 54 square feet. It is 9 feet wide. How many feet long is the rug?
questions.solution: Length $= 54 \div 9 = 6$ feet. Check: $9 \times 6 = 54$.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the area
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 36 square inches. Which could be its length and width?
questions.solution: The length times the width must be 36. $9 \times 4 = 36$. The other pairs give $6 \times 8 = 48$, $5 \times 7 = 35$ and $10 \times 3 = 30$.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the area
questions.stem: A farmer's rectangular pen has an area of 72 square feet. Its width is 8 feet. How many feet long is the pen?
questions.solution: Length $= 72 \div 8 = 9$ feet. Check: $8 \times 9 = 72$.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: To find $7 \times 6$, Zoe thinks of a rectangle 7 units long and 6 units wide. She splits it into a 7 by 5 rectangle and a 7 by 1 rectangle. What is the total area in square units?
questions.solution: $7 \times 5 = 35$ and $7 \times 1 = 7$. Add the two areas: $35 + 7 = 42$ square units.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: A rectangle 8 units long and 7 units wide is split into a part that is 8 by 4 and a part that is 8 by 3. Which expression gives the area of the whole rectangle?
questions.solution: The area of the whole is the sum of the areas of the two parts: $8 \times 4 + 8 \times 3 = 32 + 24 = 56$, which is also $8 \times 7$.

solve.work: Area = sum of parts = 8 x 4 + 8 x 3 = 32 + 24 = 56 = 8 x 7.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: A garden has a vegetable part that is 6 yards by 5 yards and a flower part that is 6 yards by 3 yards. The parts are side by side and do not overlap. What is the total area of the garden in square yards?
questions.solution: The vegetable part is $6 \times 5 = 30$ square yards and the flower part is $6 \times 3 = 18$ square yards. Together: $30 + 18 = 48$ square yards.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: Kai finds the area of a rectangle 12 units long and 4 units wide by splitting the 12 into 10 and 2. The two smaller rectangles are 10 by 4 and 2 by 4. What is the area of the whole rectangle in square units?
questions.solution: $10 \times 4 = 40$ and $2 \times 4 = 8$. Add them: $40 + 8 = 48$ square units.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: A hexagon has six sides that are 4 cm, 6 cm, 5 cm, 3 cm, 7 cm and 2 cm long. What is its perimeter in centimeters?
questions.solution: Add all six sides: $4 + 6 + 5 + 3 + 7 + 2 = 27$ centimeters. Each other choice leaves out one side.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: A rectangular dog pen is 12 feet long and 8 feet wide. How many feet of fence go all the way around the pen?
questions.solution: There are two sides of 12 feet and two sides of 8 feet: $12 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 40$ feet.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: A triangular garden has sides that are 8 meters, 10 meters and 13 meters long. What is its perimeter in meters?
questions.solution: Add all three sides: $8 + 10 + 13 = 31$ meters. The other choices each leave out one side.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: Which shape has a perimeter of 20 units?
choices: a rectangle that is 6 units by 5 units
a triangle with three sides of 7 units
a square with sides of 5 units
a rectangle that is 8 units by 4 units
questions.answer: a square with sides of 5 units
questions.solution: The square has $4 \times 5 = 20$ units around. The 6 by 5 rectangle has 22 units, the triangle has 21 units and the 8 by 4 rectangle has 24 units.

solve.answer: a square with sides of 5 units
solve.work: Square 4 x 5 = 20; triangle 3 x 7 = 21; 6 by 5: 22; 8 by 4: 24. Only the square.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: The perimeter of a square flag is 36 inches. How many inches long is each side of the flag?
questions.solution: Each side is $36 \div 4 = 9$ inches. Check: $4 \times 9 = 36$.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: A four-sided field has a perimeter of 50 meters. Three of its sides are 12 meters, 15 meters and 9 meters long. How many meters long is the fourth side?
questions.solution: The three known sides total $12 + 15 + 9 = 36$ meters. The fourth side is $50 - 36 = 14$ meters.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: A pentagon has a perimeter of 40 centimeters. Four of its sides are 6, 9, 7 and 8 centimeters long. How many centimeters long is the fifth side?
questions.solution: The four known sides total $6 + 9 + 7 + 8 = 30$ centimeters. The fifth side is $40 - 30 = 10$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: A triangle has a perimeter of 34 inches. Two of its sides are 11 inches and 13 inches long. How many inches long is the third side?
questions.solution: The two known sides total $11 + 13 = 24$ inches. The third side is $34 - 24 = 10$ inches.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is 32 inches. What is the sum of its length and its width in inches?
questions.solution: The perimeter is two lengths plus two widths, which is twice the sum of one length and one width. So length plus width is $32 \div 2 = 16$ inches.

solve.work: Perimeter = 2 x (length + width), so length + width = 32 / 2 = 16.

questions.skill: Area or perimeter: which to find, and which units
questions.stem: A rectangular poster is 4 feet by 3 feet. Rosa puts a wooden frame around its edges. Which tells how much wood the frame needs?
questions.solution: The frame goes around the edge, so we need the perimeter: $4 + 3 + 4 + 3 = 14$ feet. The choice 12 square feet is the area of the poster.

solve.work: Frame goes around: perimeter = 4 + 3 + 4 + 3 = 14 feet. 12 square feet is the area.

questions.skill: Area or perimeter: which to find, and which units
questions.stem: Which measurement needs square units?
questions.solution: Area counts the unit squares that cover a surface, so it is written in square units. Perimeter, the length of a fence and a height are all lengths.

solve.work: Area is measured in square units; the others are lengths.

questions.skill: Area or perimeter: which to find, and which units
questions.stem: A cloth cover for a rectangular table is 5 feet by 3 feet, and ribbon is sewn along its whole edge. Which question is answered by finding the AREA of the cover?
choices: How much ribbon goes along the edge?
How long is the longest side?
How much cloth is the cover made from?
How far is it around the cover?
questions.answer: How much cloth is the cover made from?
questions.solution: The amount of cloth is the flat space the cover takes up, which is its area: $5 \times 3 = 15$ square feet. The other questions are about lengths or the distance around.

solve.answer: How much cloth is the cover made from?
solve.work: Area tells how much surface the cloth covers: how much cloth. Ribbon/around are perimeter; longest side is a length.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter together
questions.stem: Rectangle A is 8 units by 3 units. Rectangle B is 6 units by 4 units. Which statement is true?
choices: They have the same area, but A has the longer perimeter
They have the same area and the same perimeter
A has the greater area and the longer perimeter
B has the greater area and the longer perimeter
questions.answer: They have the same area, but A has the longer perimeter
questions.solution: Both have an area of 24 square units ($8 \times 3$ and $6 \times 4$). Rectangle A has a perimeter of 22 units and Rectangle B has 20 units.

solve.answer: They have the same area, but A has the longer perimeter
solve.work: A: area 24, perimeter 22. B: area 24, perimeter 20. Same area, A longer perimeter.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter together
questions.stem: Rectangle X is 5 units by 3 units. Rectangle Y is 6 units by 2 units. They have the same perimeter. How many more square units is the area of X than the area of Y?
questions.solution: X has area $5 \times 3 = 15$ square units. Y has area $6 \times 2 = 12$ square units. X has $15 - 12 = 3$ more square units.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter together
questions.stem: Which pair of rectangles has the same area?
choices: a 3 by 8 rectangle and a 5 by 5 rectangle
a 2 by 12 rectangle and a 6 by 4 rectangle
a 9 by 4 rectangle and a 7 by 5 rectangle
a 10 by 3 rectangle and a 6 by 6 rectangle
questions.answer: a 2 by 12 rectangle and a 6 by 4 rectangle
questions.solution: $2 \times 12 = 24$ and $6 \times 4 = 24$. The other pairs have areas 24 and 25, 36 and 35, and 30 and 36.

solve.answer: a 2 by 12 rectangle and a 6 by 4 rectangle

questions.skill: Missing side of a rectangle from its perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 centimeters. It is 9 centimeters long. How many centimeters wide is it?
questions.solution: The length and width together are half the perimeter: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 centimeters. The width is 15 − 9 = 6 centimeters. Check: 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: A floor is made of two rectangles joined together with no overlap. One rectangle is 6 feet by 4 feet. The other is 3 feet by 2 feet. What is the total area of the floor in square feet?
questions.solution: First rectangle: $6 \times 4 = 24$ square feet. Second rectangle: $3 \times 2 = 6$ square feet. Total: 24 + 6 = 30 square feet.

questions.skill: Same area, different perimeter
questions.stem: Rectangle A is 6 units by 2 units. Rectangle B is 4 units by 3 units. Both have an area of 12 square units. Which statement is true?
choices: Rectangle B has the greater perimeter.
Rectangle A has the greater perimeter.
The perimeters are equal because the areas are equal.
The perimeters are equal because both have four sides.
questions.answer: Rectangle A has the greater perimeter.
questions.solution: Perimeter of A: 6 + 2 + 6 + 2 = 16 units. Perimeter of B: 4 + 3 + 4 + 3 = 14 units. So A has the greater perimeter, even though the areas are equal.

solve.answer: Rectangle A has the greater perimeter.
solve.work: A: 6+2+6+2 = 16. B: 4+3+4+3 = 14. A has the greater perimeter.

questions.skill: Area by tiling with unit squares
questions.stem: Dev covers a rectangle with 3 rows of 8 unit squares. Then he adds 2 more rows of 8 unit squares below, with no gaps. How many unit squares cover the rectangle now?
questions.solution: There are now $3 + 2 = 5$ rows with 8 squares in each row, so $5 \times 8 = 40$ unit squares. (Or $24 + 16 = 40$.)

questions.skill: Area by tiling with unit squares
questions.stem: Rectangle A is covered by 5 rows with 4 unit squares in each row. Rectangle B is covered by 3 rows with 7 unit squares in each row. How many more unit squares cover Rectangle B than Rectangle A?
questions.solution: Rectangle A uses $5 \times 4 = 20$ squares. Rectangle B uses $3 \times 7 = 21$ squares. Rectangle B uses $21 - 20 = 1$ more square.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square by multiplying side lengths
questions.stem: A kitchen floor is 9 feet by 7 feet. A bathroom floor is 5 feet by 6 feet. How many more square feet is the area of the kitchen floor than the area of the bathroom floor?
questions.solution: The kitchen floor is $9 \times 7 = 63$ square feet. The bathroom floor is $5 \times 6 = 30$ square feet. The difference is $63 - 30 = 33$ square feet.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square by multiplying side lengths
questions.stem: Which expression does NOT give the area of a rectangle that is 6 units by 4 units?
questions.solution: The area is 24 square units. $6 \times 4$ and $4 \times 6$ both equal 24, and $6 + 6 + 6 + 6$ is 4 groups of 6, which is also 24. But $6 + 4 = 10$ does not give the area.

solve.work: Area = 24. 4x6=24, 6x4=24, 6+6+6+6=24 (4 rows of 6), but 6+4=10. So 6+4 does not give the area.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square by multiplying side lengths
questions.stem: Ana covers a board with 4 square stickers that do not overlap. Each side of a sticker is 5 centimeters long. What is the total area of the stickers in square centimeters?
questions.solution: One sticker has area $5 \times 5 = 25$ square centimeters. Four stickers have area $4 \times 25 = 100$ square centimeters.

solve.work: Each sticker 5 x 5 = 25 sq cm; 4 stickers: 4 x 25 = 100 sq cm.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square by multiplying side lengths
questions.stem: A rectangular banner is 9 feet long. Its width is 4 feet shorter than its length. What is the area of the banner in square feet?
questions.solution: The width is $9 - 4 = 5$ feet. The area is $9 \times 5 = 45$ square feet. The choice 36 uses 4 as the width, 28 is the distance around, and 14 adds the sides.

solve.work: Width = 9 - 4 = 5 ft. Area = 9 x 5 = 45 square feet.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the area
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 63 square centimeters and a width of 7 centimeters. What is its perimeter in centimeters?
questions.solution: First find the length: $63 \div 7 = 9$ centimeters. The perimeter is $9 + 7 + 9 + 7 = 32$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the area
questions.stem: A rug has an area of 45 square feet and is 9 feet long. A second rug has the same width but is 4 feet longer. What is the area of the second rug in square feet?
questions.solution: The width of the first rug is $45 \div 9 = 5$ feet. The second rug is $9 + 4 = 13$ feet long and 5 feet wide, so its area is $13 \times 5 = 65$ square feet.

solve.work: First rug width = 45 / 9 = 5 ft. Second rug: width 5, length 9 + 4 = 13. Area = 13 x 5 = 65 (= 45 + 4 x 5).

questions.skill: Missing side length from the area
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 30 square units. Which pair of side lengths can NOT be its length and width?
questions.solution: The two sides must multiply to 30. $5 \times 6$, $3 \times 10$ and $2 \times 15$ all equal 30, but $4 \times 8 = 32$.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the area
questions.stem: A square mirror has an area of 81 square inches. How many inches long is each side of the mirror?
questions.solution: All sides of a square are equal, so we need a number that times itself is 81. $9 \times 9 = 81$, so each side is 9 inches.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: A flag is 6 inches tall and 10 inches wide. A blue stripe along the left side is 6 inches tall and 4 inches wide. The rest of the flag is red. What is the area of the red part in square inches?
questions.solution: The red part is a rectangle 6 inches tall and $10 - 4 = 6$ inches wide, so its area is $6 \times 6 = 36$ square inches. The choice 60 is the whole flag and 24 is the blue stripe.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: A hallway is shaped like an L. One part is 10 feet long and 3 feet wide. The other part is 6 feet long and 3 feet wide. The two parts meet at a corner and do not overlap. What is the total area of the hallway in square feet?
questions.solution: The first part is $10 \times 3 = 30$ square feet. The second part is $6 \times 3 = 18$ square feet. Together: $30 + 18 = 48$ square feet.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: A playground has three rectangular parts that do not overlap. The sand area is 5 meters by 4 meters, the grass area is 6 meters by 3 meters, and the court is 4 meters by 2 meters. What is the total area of the playground in square meters?
questions.solution: Sand: $5 \times 4 = 20$. Grass: $6 \times 3 = 18$. Court: $4 \times 2 = 8$. Total: $20 + 18 + 8 = 46$ square meters.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: An L-shaped patio is made of a rectangle that is 9 feet by 2 feet and a rectangle that is 4 feet by 3 feet. The two rectangles touch along one side and do not overlap. What is the area of the patio in square feet?
questions.solution: The first rectangle has area $9 \times 2 = 18$ square feet. The second has area $4 \times 3 = 12$ square feet. Together: $18 + 12 = 30$ square feet.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: A board is 9 inches long and 7 inches wide. Mia saws it across into three pieces that are each 9 inches long. Two of the pieces are 2 inches wide and 3 inches wide. What is the area of the third piece in square inches?
questions.solution: The third piece is $7 - 2 - 3 = 2$ inches wide, so its area is $9 \times 2 = 18$ square inches. (Check: $63 - 18 - 27 = 18$.)

solve.work: Widths add to 7: third = 7 - 2 - 3 = 2 in. Area = 9 x 2 = 18 (check 63 - 18 - 27 = 18).

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: A field has five sides that are 14 meters, 9 meters, 12 meters, 8 meters and 17 meters long. What is the perimeter of the field in meters?
questions.solution: Add all five sides: $14 + 9 + 12 + 8 + 17 = 60$ meters. Each other choice leaves out one side.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: A rectangle is 3 times as long as it is wide. Its width is 4 centimeters. What is its perimeter in centimeters?
questions.solution: The length is $3 \times 4 = 12$ centimeters. The perimeter is $12 + 4 + 12 + 4 = 32$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: Gia walks 3 times around a square block. Each side of the block is 40 meters long. How many meters does she walk in all?
questions.solution: One trip around is $4 \times 40 = 160$ meters. Three trips are $3 \times 160 = 480$ meters.

solve.work: Once around = 4 x 40 = 160 m. Three times = 3 x 160 = 480 m.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon (adding all the sides)
questions.stem: Two squares, each with sides of 4 centimeters, are joined along one whole side to make one rectangle. What is the perimeter of the new rectangle in centimeters?
questions.solution: The new rectangle is $4 + 4 = 8$ centimeters long and 4 centimeters wide. Its perimeter is $8 + 4 + 8 + 4 = 24$ centimeters.

solve.work: Joined squares make an 8 cm by 4 cm rectangle. Perimeter = 8 + 4 + 8 + 4 = 24 cm.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangular field has a perimeter of 38 yards. Its width is 7 yards. How many yards long is the field?
questions.solution: The two widths total $2 \times 7 = 14$ yards, which leaves $38 - 14 = 24$ yards for the two lengths. One length is $24 \div 2 = 12$ yards.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: A triangle has two sides of equal length. Its third side is 6 centimeters long and its perimeter is 26 centimeters. How many centimeters long is each of the two equal sides?
questions.solution: The two equal sides share $26 - 6 = 20$ centimeters, so each is $20 \div 2 = 10$ centimeters.

solve.work: 26 - 6 = 20 for the two equal sides; 20 / 2 = 10 cm.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: A square has sides of 7 centimeters. A rectangle has the same perimeter as the square and is 9 centimeters long. How many centimeters wide is the rectangle?
questions.solution: The square's perimeter is $4 \times 7 = 28$ centimeters. The rectangle's two lengths take $2 \times 9 = 18$, leaving $28 - 18 = 10$ for the two widths. Each width is $10 \div 2 = 5$ centimeters.

solve.work: Square perimeter 4 x 7 = 28. Rectangle: length + width = 14; width = 14 - 9 = 5 cm.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: A four-sided shape has a perimeter of 46 units. Two of its sides are each 11 units long. The other two sides are equal in length. How many units long is each of the other two sides?
questions.solution: The two sides of 11 take $2 \times 11 = 22$ units, leaving $46 - 22 = 24$ units for the other two sides. Each is $24 \div 2 = 12$ units.

questions.skill: Missing side length from the perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 22 units. Which could be its length and width?
questions.solution: The perimeter is $2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$, so the length and width must add to 11. $8 + 3 = 11$. The other pairs add to 12, 10 and 13.

questions.skill: Area or perimeter: which to find, and which units
questions.stem: Dara is building a rectangular play yard. She needs to buy fence for the edge and grass seed to cover the ground. Which pair is correct?
questions.solution: The fence goes around the edge, so it needs the perimeter. The seed covers the ground, so it needs the area.

solve.work: Fence around the edge: perimeter. Seed covering the ground: area.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter together
questions.stem: A rectangle covered by exactly 16 unit squares can be 16 by 1, 8 by 2 or 4 by 4 units. Which one has the smallest perimeter?
choices: They all have the same perimeter
questions.solution: The perimeters are 16 units for 4 by 4, 20 units for 8 by 2, and 34 units for 16 by 1. The same area can have different perimeters.

solve.work: Perimeters: 16 by 1 = 34, 8 by 2 = 20, 4 by 4 = 16. Smallest: 4 by 4.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter together
questions.stem: A square has a perimeter of 24 centimeters. What is its area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each side is $24 \div 4 = 6$ centimeters, so the area is $6 \times 6 = 36$ square centimeters.

solve.work: Side = 24 / 4 = 6 cm. Area = 6 x 6 = 36 sq cm.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter together
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 21 square units and a length of 7 units. A square has the same perimeter as this rectangle. What is the area of the square in square units?
questions.solution: The rectangle's width is $21 \div 7 = 3$ units, so its perimeter is $7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20$ units. The square's sides are $20 \div 4 = 5$ units, so its area is $5 \times 5 = 25$ square units.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter together
questions.stem: Ming says, "A rectangle with a greater area always has a greater perimeter." Which pair of rectangles shows that Ming is wrong?
choices: a 5 by 5 rectangle and a 3 by 4 rectangle
a 6 by 6 rectangle and a 2 by 5 rectangle
a 3 by 7 rectangle and a 2 by 3 rectangle
a 4 by 4 rectangle and a 1 by 9 rectangle
questions.answer: a 4 by 4 rectangle and a 1 by 9 rectangle
questions.solution: The 4 by 4 rectangle has the greater area (16 against 9) but the shorter perimeter (16 against 20). In each other pair, the rectangle with the greater area also has the longer perimeter.

solve.answer: a 4 by 4 rectangle and a 1 by 9 rectangle
solve.work: Need greater area with NOT greater perimeter. 5x5 (25, P20) vs 3x4 (12, P14): no. 6x6 (36, P24) vs 2x5 (10, P14): no. 4x4 (16, P16) vs 1x9 (9, P20): greater area, smaller perimeter, yes. 3x7 (21, P20) vs 2x3 (6, P10): no.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter together
questions.stem: Rectangle A is 6 units by 5 units. Rectangle B has the same area as Rectangle A and is 10 units long. What is the perimeter of Rectangle B in units?
questions.solution: The area of A is $6 \times 5 = 30$ square units. Rectangle B is 10 units long, so its width is $30 \div 10 = 3$ units. Its perimeter is $10 + 3 + 10 + 3 = 26$ units.

solve.work: Area of A = 6 x 5 = 30. B: 10 long, width = 30 / 10 = 3. Perimeter = 10 + 3 + 10 + 3 = 26.

questions.skill: Total from a frequency list
questions.stem: Ms. Lee's class voted for a favorite fruit. Apple got 8 votes, banana got 5 votes and grape got 7 votes. How many students voted in all?
questions.solution: Add all the votes: 8 + 5 + 7 = 20 students.

questions.skill: Read a picture graph with a key
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each star stands for 2 books. The row for Monday has 5 stars. How many books does the Monday row stand for?
questions.solution: Each of the 5 stars stands for 2 books. $5 \times 2 = 10$ books.

questions.skill: Find the most popular category
questions.stem: Students voted for a favorite pet. Dog got 9 votes, cat got 12 votes, fish got 4 votes and bird got 7 votes. Which pet got the most votes?
questions.solution: Compare the votes: 9, 12, 4 and 7. The greatest is 12, which is for cat.

questions.skill: Read and use a frequency table
questions.stem: Students voted for a favorite color. A frequency table shows blue 8, red 5 and green 6. What does the 8 next to blue tell you?
choices: Blue is the eighth color on the list
8 more students voted for blue than for red
8 students voted for colors other than blue
questions.solution: A frequency table tells how many times each choice was picked. The 8 next to blue means 8 students voted for blue. Blue got 3 more votes than red (not 8 more), and the other colors got $5 + 6 = 11$ votes.

solve.work: In a frequency table the number beside a category is how many chose it: 8 students voted for blue.

questions.skill: Read and use a frequency table
questions.stem: A frequency table shows the weather on each day of one month: sunny 15 days, cloudy 9 days and rainy 6 days. How many days are in that month?
questions.solution: Every day is in exactly one row, so add the rows: $15 + 9 + 6 = 30$ days.

questions.skill: Read and use a frequency table
questions.stem: A frequency table shows how many students joined each club: art 9, chess 4, choir 12 and robotics 7. Which club has the fewest students?
questions.solution: The smallest number in the table is 4, which is chess.

solve.work: art 9, chess 4, choir 12, robotics 7. Fewest = chess (4).

questions.skill: Tally marks and organizing a list of answers
questions.stem: In a tally chart, a full group of five votes is drawn as four lines with one line across them. Sam's chart shows 2 full groups of five and 3 single marks for cat. How many votes did cat get?
questions.solution: Each full group counts 5, so 2 groups make $2 \times 5 = 10$. Add the 3 single marks: $10 + 3 = 13$ votes.

questions.skill: Tally marks and organizing a list of answers
questions.stem: In a tally chart, one full group counts 5 marks. Which entry shows 7 marks?
questions.solution: One full group is 5, and 2 more single marks make $5 + 2 = 7$. The other entries show 12, 10 and 8 marks.

solve.work: 5 + 3 = 8; 5 + 7 = 12; 5 + 2 = 7; 2 groups = 10. So 1 full group and 2 single marks.

questions.skill: Tally marks and organizing a list of answers
questions.stem: Students were asked their favorite season. Their answers were: summer, fall, summer, winter, spring, summer, fall, summer, winter, fall. How many students chose summer?
questions.solution: Count the word summer in the list: it is the 1st, 3rd, 6th and 8th answer, so 4 students chose summer.

questions.skill: Read a scaled bar graph
questions.stem: On a bar graph, each grid line stands for 5 students, and the first line above 0 is 5. The bar for hockey reaches the 4th grid line above 0. How many students chose hockey?
questions.solution: Each line adds 5, so the 4th line is at $4 \times 5 = 20$. Twenty students chose hockey.

questions.skill: Read a scaled bar graph
questions.stem: What number comes next on a bar graph scale that goes 0, 3, 6, 9, 12?
questions.solution: The scale counts by 3s, so the next number is $12 + 3 = 15$.

questions.skill: Read a scaled bar graph
questions.stem: The scale of a bar graph counts by 5s. The bar labeled Soccer ends exactly at the line marked 15. What does this tell you?
choices: Soccer is the 15th sport on the graph
questions.solution: The top of a bar shows how many chose that category. The bar for Soccer ends at 15, so 15 students chose soccer.

solve.issues: Minor: the stem never says the graph counts students; the options assume it. Still only one defensible choice.
solve.work: Bar ending at 15 means a count of 15 for soccer: 15 students chose soccer.

questions.skill: Read a scaled bar graph
questions.stem: On a bar graph, which bar shows the category chosen by the most students?
questions.solution: The taller the bar, the greater the number it shows, so the tallest bar is the category with the most.

solve.work: The longest/tallest bar shows the greatest count.

questions.skill: Read a scaled bar graph
questions.stem: A bar graph has bars for four sports. Its scale counts by 2s. The bars end at 10 for soccer, 6 for tennis, 14 for swimming and 8 for golf. How many students chose swimming?
questions.solution: Read the number where the swimming bar ends: 14 students chose swimming.

questions.skill: Read a picture graph with a key
questions.stem: In a picture graph about pets, the key says one paw print stands for 2 pets. The row for dogs shows 7 paw prints. How many dogs does the row stand for?
questions.solution: Each paw print stands for 2 dogs, so 7 paw prints stand for $7 \times 2 = 14$ dogs.

questions.skill: Read a picture graph with a key
questions.stem: Why does a picture graph need a key?
choices: It tells who made the graph
It tells which row is the longest
It tells how many each picture stands for
It tells the date of the survey
questions.answer: It tells how many each picture stands for
questions.solution: One picture may stand for more than one thing, such as 2 or 5. The key tells how many each picture stands for, so you can read the graph correctly.

solve.answer: It tells how many each picture stands for
solve.work: The key gives the value of each picture.

questions.skill: Read a picture graph with a key
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each cup picture stands for 3 glasses of juice. The juice row stands for 12 glasses. How many cup pictures are in the juice row?
questions.solution: Each cup is 3 glasses, so the number of cups is $12 \div 3 = 4$. Check: $4 \times 3 = 12$.

questions.skill: Compare categories: how many more or fewer
questions.stem: A graph shows that 12 students chose cats and 7 students chose dogs. How many more students chose cats than dogs?
questions.solution: Subtract to compare: $12 - 7 = 5$ more students chose cats.

questions.skill: Compare categories: how many more or fewer
questions.stem: A frequency table shows that 15 children chose the swing and 11 children chose the slide. How many fewer children chose the slide than the swing?
questions.solution: Subtract: $15 - 11 = 4$ fewer children chose the slide. The choice 26 adds the two numbers instead.

questions.skill: Compare categories: how many more or fewer
questions.stem: A bar graph's scale counts by 5s. The bar for bananas ends at 25 and the bar for grapes ends at 10. How many more students chose bananas than grapes?
questions.solution: Read the two bars and subtract: $25 - 10 = 15$ more students chose bananas.

questions.skill: Two-step problems from a graph or table
questions.stem: A frequency table shows 9 votes for soccer, 5 votes for tennis and 6 votes for golf. Then 3 more students vote for tennis. How many votes does tennis have now?
questions.solution: Tennis had 5 votes and gets 3 more: $5 + 3 = 8$ votes.

questions.skill: Make a graph: choose a scale or the number of symbols
questions.stem: Ana's data are 10, 30, 20 and 40 votes. She wants a bar graph scale that lands exactly on every one of these numbers. Which scale should she use?
questions.solution: Each number is a multiple of 10, so a scale that counts by 10s (0, 10, 20, 30, 40) lands exactly on all of them. Counting by 4s, 7s or 100s skips some of the numbers.

solve.work: 10, 20, 30, 40 are all multiples of 10; not of 4 (10), 7, or 100.

questions.skill: Make a graph: choose a scale or the number of symbols
questions.stem: Which of these does a bar graph need so that people can read it?
choices: a title, labels on the bars and a scale of numbers
a key that says what each picture stands for
questions.answer: a title, labels on the bars and a scale of numbers
questions.solution: Readers need a title to know the topic, labels to know what each bar shows, and a scale to read the numbers. A key belongs on a picture graph.

solve.answer: a title, labels on the bars and a scale of numbers
solve.work: A readable bar graph needs a title, category labels and a numbered scale. A picture key is for picture graphs.

questions.skill: Make a graph: choose a scale or the number of symbols
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each picture stands for 5 students. How many pictures should Rita draw for 30 students?
questions.solution: Each picture is 5 students, so Rita draws $30 \div 5 = 6$ pictures.

questions.skill: Pose a question that data can answer
questions.stem: Sam wants to find out which fruit his classmates like best. Which question should he ask each classmate?
choices: Which fruit do you like best: apple, banana or grape?
questions.answer: Which fruit do you like best: apple, banana or grape?
questions.solution: Sam's question must be about his classmates' favorite fruit and give choices he can count. The other questions do not tell him anything about favorite fruit.

solve.answer: Which fruit do you like best: apple, banana or grape?
solve.work: Only one option asks about favorite fruit, with categories.

questions.skill: Pose a question that data can answer
questions.stem: Which question can a class answer by making a bar graph of its own answers?
choices: How old is the school building?
How many sides does a square have?
What is your favorite kind of music?
questions.answer: What is your favorite kind of music?
questions.solution: Each student can give a different answer about music, and the answers can be counted in groups. The other questions have one correct answer for everyone.

solve.answer: What is your favorite kind of music?
solve.work: Favorite music varies by student and gives categories to graph; the others have one fixed answer.

questions.skill: Pose a question that data can answer
questions.stem: Which question has answers that can be sorted into groups like red, blue and green?
choices: How many pencils do you have?
questions.solution: Colors are categories. The other questions have number answers, not color groups.

solve.work: Favorite color gives categories like red, blue, green; the others give numbers.

questions.skill: Plan and carry out data collection
questions.stem: Rosa will ask her classmates to choose a favorite pet. What can she use to keep count while she asks?
questions.solution: A tally chart lets Rosa make one mark for each answer as she goes, then count the marks.

solve.work: A tally chart keeps count of choices as they are made.

questions.skill: Plan and carry out data collection
questions.stem: Which is the first step of the data cycle?
choices: Ask a question that data can answer
questions.answer: Ask a question that data can answer
questions.solution: The data cycle starts with a question. Then you collect the data, show it in a table or graph, and draw conclusions.

solve.answer: Ask a question that data can answer
solve.work: The data cycle starts by posing a question that data can answer.

questions.skill: Plan and carry out data collection
questions.stem: Mia wants to know the favorite subject of the students in her class. Which group should she ask?
questions.solution: To learn about the students in her class, Mia should ask the students in her class.

solve.work: To learn about her class, ask the students in her class.

questions.skill: Draw conclusions and make predictions from data
questions.stem: A bar graph shows that 20 students chose pizza, 15 chose tacos and 5 chose salad. Which conclusion is true?
choices: More students chose pizza than salad
Pizza and tacos got the same number of votes
questions.answer: More students chose pizza than salad
questions.solution: Pizza has 20 and salad has 5, so more chose pizza. Five students did choose salad, pizza got more votes than tacos, and 20 is not the same as 15.

solve.answer: More students chose pizza than salad

questions.skill: Draw conclusions and make predictions from data
questions.stem: Rosa's table shows that 12 students picked soccer and 6 students picked golf. Which sentence is supported by the data?
choices: Soccer was picked by twice as many students as golf
Golf was picked by more students than soccer
questions.answer: Soccer was picked by twice as many students as golf
questions.solution: 12 is twice 6, so twice as many students picked soccer as picked golf. The other sentences do not match the table.

solve.answer: Soccer was picked by twice as many students as golf

questions.skill: Draw conclusions and make predictions from data
questions.stem: In a class vote, 15 of the 20 students chose dogs as their favorite pet. The class votes again next week. Which prediction makes the most sense?
choices: Dogs will probably get the most votes again
Cats will get the most votes
questions.answer: Dogs will probably get the most votes again
questions.solution: Dogs got most of the votes this time, so it is reasonable to predict dogs will do well again.

solve.answer: Dogs will probably get the most votes again
solve.work: Dogs won strongly (15 of 20), so likely again; the others are unsupported or certain-sounding.

questions.skill: Read a bar between two scale marks
questions.stem: A bar graph has a scale that counts by 10s: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40. The bar for soccer ends halfway between 20 and 30. How many students chose soccer?
questions.solution: Halfway between 20 and 30 is 25, because 10 split in half is 5 and $20 + 5 = 25$.

questions.skill: Difference using a picture graph scale
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each picture stands for 4 pets. The dog row has 6 pictures and the fish row has 3 pictures. How many more dogs than fish are shown?
questions.solution: The dog row has 3 more pictures than the fish row. Each picture is 4 pets, so $3 \times 4 = 12$ more dogs.

solve.work: Dogs 6 x 4 = 24, fish 3 x 4 = 12; 24 - 12 = 12 more dogs.

questions.skill: Pose a question that collects data
questions.stem: Mr. Cruz's class wants to collect data from their classmates. Which question should they ask?
choices: Which fruit do you like best: apple, banana or grape?
How many days are in one week?
What color is Mr. Cruz's car?
questions.answer: Which fruit do you like best: apple, banana or grape?
questions.solution: A question for collecting data should have answers that can be different for different classmates. Everyone gives the same answer to the days in a week and to 7 + 5, and the car has just one color. Favorite fruit gives different answers that the class can count.

solve.answer: Which fruit do you like best: apple, banana or grape?
solve.work: A data question has answers that vary among classmates and fall into categories: favourite fruit. The others have one fixed answer.

questions.skill: Read and use a frequency table
questions.stem: A frequency table shows the pets students have: dog 11, cat 8, fish 5, bird 3 and rabbit 2. Each student named one pet. How many students have either a dog or a cat?
questions.solution: Add the dog row and the cat row: $11 + 8 = 19$ students.

solve.work: Each student named one pet: dog 11 + cat 8 = 19.

questions.skill: Read and use a frequency table
questions.stem: 36 students voted for a field trip. A frequency table shows that the zoo got 14 votes, the museum got 9 votes, and the park got all the rest of the votes. How many votes did the park get?
questions.solution: The zoo and the museum got $14 + 9 = 23$ votes. The park got the rest: $36 - 23 = 13$ votes.

questions.skill: Read and use a frequency table
questions.stem: A frequency table shows how many times each fruit was chosen: apples 7, pears 12, plums 5 and cherries 12. Which statement is true?
choices: Pears and cherries were chosen the same number of times
Plums were chosen more often than apples
questions.answer: Pears and cherries were chosen the same number of times
questions.solution: Pears and cherries both have 12, so they were chosen the same number of times. Apples (7) were not the most, plums (5) were chosen less often than apples (7), and cherries (12) were not the fewest.

solve.answer: Pears and cherries were chosen the same number of times
solve.work: Pears 12 and cherries 12 are equal. Apples (7) not most; plums 5 < apples 7; cherries not fewest.

questions.skill: Tally marks and organizing a list of answers
questions.stem: Lila makes a tally chart of birds. Sparrows have 3 full groups of five and 2 single marks. Robins have 2 full groups of five and 4 single marks. How many more sparrows than robins did she count?
questions.solution: Sparrows: $3 \times 5 + 2 = 17$. Robins: $2 \times 5 + 4 = 14$. Lila counted $17 - 14 = 3$ more sparrows.

questions.skill: Tally marks and organizing a list of answers
questions.stem: Twelve students named the pet they own. The answers were: dog, cat, dog, fish, cat, dog, bird, cat, dog, fish, dog, cat. How many students own a cat or a fish?
questions.solution: Count the cats: 4 (the 2nd, 5th, 8th and 12th answers). Count the fish: 2 (the 4th and 10th). Together: $4 + 2 = 6$ students.

solve.work: dog 5, cat 4 (positions 2,5,8,12), fish 2 (4,10), bird 1; total 12. Cat or fish = 4 + 2 = 6.

questions.skill: Tally marks and organizing a list of answers
questions.stem: Kai wrote down the colors of 10 cars: red, blue, red, white, red, blue, white, red, blue, red. Which frequency table is correct?
questions.solution: Count each color: red appears 5 times, blue 3 times and white 2 times. The three counts add up to 10, the number of cars.

solve.work: red at 1,3,5,8,10 = 5; blue at 2,6,9 = 3; white at 4,7 = 2. Total 10.

questions.skill: Read a scaled bar graph
questions.stem: A bar graph's scale counts by 4s: 0, 4, 8, 12, 16. The bar for pizza ends halfway between 8 and 12. How many students chose pizza?
questions.solution: The number halfway between 8 and 12 is $(8 + 12) \div 2 = 10$, so 10 students chose pizza.

questions.skill: Read a scaled bar graph
questions.stem: A bar graph's scale counts by 10s. The bars end at 40 for bike, 30 for walk, 50 for bus and 20 for car. Each student comes to school one way. How many students walk or ride a bike?
questions.solution: Add the walk bar and the bike bar: $30 + 40 = 70$ students.

questions.skill: Read a scaled bar graph
questions.stem: A bar graph shows how many books four classes read. Ms. A's bar ends at 25, Mr. B's at 40, Ms. C's at 35 and Mr. D's at 30. Which classes read more than 30 books?
questions.solution: More than 30 means a number greater than 30. Mr. B read 40 and Ms. C read 35. Mr. D read exactly 30, which is not more than 30.

solve.work: More than 30: Mr. B (40), Ms. C (35). Mr. D is exactly 30, not more.

questions.skill: Read a scaled bar graph
questions.stem: A bar graph's scale counts by 2s. The bar for green ends at 14. The bar for blue is 6 shorter than the bar for green. How many students chose blue?
questions.solution: The blue bar ends 6 below the green bar: $14 - 6 = 8$ students.

questions.skill: Read a picture graph with a key
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each book picture stands for 10 books. Row A has 6 pictures and Row B has 4 pictures. How many books do the two rows stand for together?
questions.solution: There are $6 + 4 = 10$ pictures, and each stands for 10 books: $10 \times 10 = 100$ books.

questions.skill: Read a picture graph with a key
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each picture stands for 2 books. Ann's row has 6 pictures, Bo's row has 4 pictures and Cy's row has 5 pictures. Who read 8 books?
questions.solution: Bo's 4 pictures stand for $4 \times 2 = 8$ books. Ann read $6 \times 2 = 12$ books and Cy read $5 \times 2 = 10$ books.

solve.work: Ann 12, Bo 4 x 2 = 8, Cy 10. Bo read 8.

questions.skill: Read a picture graph with a key
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each cookie picture stands for 2 cookies, and half a picture stands for 1 cookie. Jo's row has 6 whole pictures and 1 half picture. How many cookies does Jo's row stand for?
questions.solution: The 6 whole pictures stand for $6 \times 2 = 12$ cookies. The half picture stands for 1 more. Total: $12 + 1 = 13$ cookies.

questions.skill: Compare categories: how many more or fewer
questions.stem: A frequency table shows how many books were borrowed: Monday 24, Tuesday 18 and Wednesday 31. How many more books were borrowed on Wednesday than on Tuesday?
questions.solution: Subtract: $31 - 18 = 13$ more books on Wednesday.

questions.skill: Compare categories: how many more or fewer
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each picture stands for 2 students. The pizza row has 7 pictures and the taco row has 4 pictures. How many more students chose pizza than tacos?
questions.solution: Pizza has $7 - 4 = 3$ more pictures, and each picture stands for 2 students: $3 \times 2 = 6$ more students.

questions.skill: Compare categories: how many more or fewer
questions.stem: A bar graph's scale counts by 10s. The bars end at 50 for hockey, 80 for soccer, 30 for tennis and 20 for golf. Which sport got 30 fewer votes than soccer?
questions.solution: $80 - 30 = 50$, and the hockey bar ends at 50. Tennis is 50 below soccer and golf is 60 below soccer.

questions.skill: Two-step problems from a graph or table
questions.stem: A bar graph's scale counts by 5s. The bars end at 40 for apples, 15 for pears and 20 for plums. How many more students chose apples than chose pears and plums together?
questions.solution: Pears and plums together: $15 + 20 = 35$. Apples: 40. The difference is $40 - 35 = 5$.

questions.skill: Two-step problems from a graph or table
questions.stem: A frequency table shows the trees planted: oak 12, maple 9, pine 15 and birch 6. How many more pine and oak trees together were planted than maple and birch trees together?
questions.solution: Pine and oak: $15 + 12 = 27$. Maple and birch: $9 + 6 = 15$. The difference is $27 - 15 = 12$ trees.

questions.skill: Two-step problems from a graph or table
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each picture stands for 5 students. The soccer row has 6 pictures, the tennis row has 4 pictures and the golf row has 3 pictures. How many students are shown in all?
questions.solution: There are $6 + 4 + 3 = 13$ pictures, and each stands for 5 students: $13 \times 5 = 65$. The choice 13 forgets the key; 50 and 35 each leave out a row.

questions.skill: Two-step problems from a graph or table
questions.stem: A bar graph shows the minutes Tara read: Monday 20, Tuesday 35 and Wednesday 15. Tara wants to read 100 minutes this week. How many more minutes does she still need to read?
questions.solution: So far she has read $20 + 35 + 15 = 70$ minutes. She needs $100 - 70 = 30$ more minutes.

questions.skill: Make a graph: choose a scale or the number of symbols
questions.stem: A bar graph's scale counts by 10s. Tomas wants to show 45 students. Where should the top of the bar be?
questions.solution: 45 is halfway between 40 and 50, so the top of the bar goes halfway between the lines labeled 40 and 50.

questions.skill: Make a graph: choose a scale or the number of symbols
questions.stem: The largest number in Kai's data is 45. Which bar graph scale can show every bar?
questions.solution: The scale has to reach at least 45. Only the scale from 0 to 50 does. The others stop at 30, 40 and 20.

solve.work: Scale must reach at least 45: only 0 to 50 by 5s (45 lands on a line).

questions.skill: Make a graph: choose a scale or the number of symbols
questions.stem: Rae makes a bar graph whose scale counts by 6s: 0, 6, 12, 18, 24. The top of the bar for games should be at 18. How many lines above 0 is that?
questions.solution: Each line adds 6, so 18 is the $18 \div 6 = 3$rd line above 0.

questions.skill: Pose a question that data can answer
questions.stem: Mr. Cho wants to learn which game third graders would like to play at recess. Which is the best question to ask?
choices: Which game would you like to play at recess: soccer, kickball, tag or jump rope?
What did you eat for lunch?
